posts.content:

The 2027 governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, in Akwa Ibom State, Senator John James Akpanudoedehe in a video circulating online has accused the governor, Umo Eno of reporting his predecessor to the anti-graft agency, hence the seizure of the property.



However, the Commissioner for Information, Aniekan Umanah in a statement on Sunday described Akpanudoedehe’s comment as baseless, inciting and threat to peace.

posts.excerpt: Elliot is seen in a video circulating on social media, on his knees pleading with Gbajabiamila for forgiveness and seeking reintegration into the ruling party in Lagos.The post Desmond Elliot begs G
posts.content:
Lagos State House of Assembly member, Desmond Elliot, has apologised to Femi Gbajabiamila, Chief of Staff to President Bola Tinubu, over his actions during the last All Progressives Congress (APC) primary election in Lagos.



Elliot is seen in a video circulating on social media, on his knees pleading with Gbajabiamila for forgiveness and seeking reintegration into the ruling party in Lagos.



“I’m sorry, I have no excuse, I have nothing other than to say I’m deeply sorry and I am hoping to be cultured in the future,” Elliot said.







The development followed a disagreement between Elliot and the party leadership after the APC primary for the Surulere Constituency I seat in May.

posts.title: Jhené Aiko Achieves First No. 1 Album on Billboard 200 With ‘Westside Whimsy’
posts.excerpt: It’s the first R&B album by a woman to top the chart this year.
posts.content:
Jhené Aiko achieves her first No. 1 on the Billboard 200 albums chart as Westside Whimsy debuts atop the tally dated Sept. 26.

	The set earned 74,000 equivalent album units in the United States in the week ending Sept. 17, according to Luminate. It’s the first R&B album by a woman to lead the chart in 2026, and the first to rank at No. 1 since SZA’s SOS was tops for a 13th and final week in May of 2025. The only other R&B set to hit No. 1 in 2026 was Bruno Mars’ The Romantic (March 14 chart). (R&B albums are defined as those that are eligible for, or have charted on, Billboard’s Top R&B Albums chart.)

	Westside Whimsy was released on Sept. 11, after it was announced on Sept. 8.

Attorney Edward Paltzik said Michael P. Desronvil, whose refusal to join the other 11 jurors led to a mistrial, will issue a personal statement in the "near future."

"Michael will be making a personal statement in the near future, in his own words," Paltzik wrote in a Facebook post.

Paltzik thanked those who sent emails, texts and voice messages in support of Desronvil, while acknowledging that others may disagree with the position he took inside the jury room.

posts.title: TARABA TERTIARY SCHOOLS UNDER SECURITY THREAT AS STUDENTS CALL FOR URGENT INTERVENTION
posts.excerpt: Security
posts.content:
The Danji SS Campaign Council expresses deep concern over the rising wave of insecurity in our institutions, especially around Taraba State College of Nursing and Midwifery where reportedly students were raped, beaten and have their phones stolen.

We have received disturbing reports of persistent burglary, theft, phone snatching, invasion of students' off-campus apartments, and attacks with knives and cutlasses around the university and college communities.

The situation reached a breaking point this week. Just last week, armed men wielding machetes and cutlasses invaded the Taraba State College of Nursing Sciences hostel, injured students and carted away many mobile phones. Now, another tragic incident has been reported at the Sambisa Forest Hostel, where a female student was allegedly raped, beaten and robbed of her phone after attackers forced her to reveal her password. As a result, students have taken to the streets today to protest.

Why should a government who pride security as it scorecard allow more attacks before taking decisive action? Students have complained that whenever they raise security concerns, their cries are treated as if they do not matter.

We call on the Taraba State Government, Security Agencies, the Ministry of Health, the Ministry of Tertiary Education and the management of the affected institutions to intervene immediately, secure both on-campus hostels and off-campus student residential areas, investigate these allegations thoroughly and ensure justice for every victim.

Furthermore, we strongly urge the authorities and security agencies to handle the ongoing student protest with utmost care, restraint and professionalism. These students are not criminals, they are victims crying out for safety after enduring trauma. Their constitutional right to peaceful protest must be fully respected, and any form of harassment, intimidation or use of force against them must be avoided while their legitimate grievances are being addressed.

Students went to school to become nurses, teachers and graduates, not to become victims of rape, robbery and assault. Security of our students is not negotiable.

Signed: Emmanuel Umaru 
Director, Media ans Strategy Danji SS Campaign Organization

New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill called on handpicked Lt. Gov. Dale Caldwell to resign by Friday after an independent investigation substantiated sexual harassment and two ethics violations.

The investigation found Caldwell told a female staffer that "you young women are looking for young sperm" after she told him her younger friend was not interested in a romantic relationship with him.

Investigators concluded the sexually charged remark constituted sexual harassment and said Caldwell's denial that he made the comment was not credible.

The staffer said she subsequently attempted to distance herself from Caldwell at work and avoid traveling with him when possible.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/politics/new-jersey-gov-mikie-sherrill-calls-lieutenant-governor-resign-sexual-harassment-investigation

posts.excerpt: The Southend spoke to NME about going back to basics on their "smaller and noisy" latest album, looked back at their debut LP, and teased what to expect from their biggest headline tour to date The po
posts.content:
Nothing But Thieves have spoken to NME about their new album ‘Stray Dogs’ and latest single ‘#5’, as well as reflecting on how they’re “still making it up” 10 years on, ahead of their huge headline tour.

Out today (Friday September 25), the LP marks the fifth full-length project from the Southend five-piece – following on from 2023’s ‘Dead Club City’, and sees them lean into themes of introspection, reflection and gratitude.

Written over five months as they were out on the road, Conor Mason and co. retraced their roots for the recording process, heading back to the same studio where they made their 2015 self-titled debut.

posts.title: Fulton Sheen became a TV sensation preaching faith, morality and warnings Michael Knowles says still resonate
posts.excerpt: Conservative commentator says famous Catholic archbishop would be branded a "far-right extremist" today without changing his message on faith and communism.
posts.content:
Archbishop Fulton Sheen drew tens of millions of Americans to their TV sets with little more than a chalkboard, a cape and a message about Christianity, morality and the threat of communism.

More than seven decades later, conservative commentator Michael Knowles said that he believes the legendary Catholic broadcaster could deliver essentially the same message and immediately find himself branded a "far-right extremist."

"I think he would be taking his first breath to utter the first syllable of the very first sentence just when someone called him a far-right extremist," Knowles told Fox News Digital. "He wouldn't need to change his message."…

posts.content:
Akoo River in Nkalunta Ibere village, Otu Uzo-Ibere, in Ikwuano Local Government Area of Abia State has overflowed its banks and flooded homes and farms in the community, destroying houses, livestock, poultry and churches.

The incident, which occurred after a week-long heavy rainfall, rendered more than 300 people homeless.

According to members of the community, Akoo River rose above its normal water level following persistent rainfall that pounded the community for one week.

The impact of the overflowing river, according to residents of Nkalunta Ibere village, also swept reptiles, fish and other aquatic animals from the river onto the surrounding land.

posts.content:
CNN reporters have been barred from traveling with US President Donald Trump as planned on Saturday, in a new move by the White House to limit the news network’s access.

The president last week sought to ban three US outlets – CNN, MS NOW and Politico – from the White House, accusing them of providing only negative coverage on him.

After journalists with the three outlets were blocked from entering the White House complex, a judge ordered their access to be temporarily restored, saying Trump’s move was likely unconstitutional.

For Trump’s trip on Saturday to Tennessee, CNN had been scheduled to be the TV network in the press “pool” traveling with him.

The waterway key to the world’s oil supply is central to the conflict between the United States and Iran, which is at a stalemate after nearly seven months.

Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met for talks on Tuesday with Trump’s envoy Steve Witkoff, and previously set out conditions for ending the war and reopening the vital shipping channel.

posts.excerpt: Pope Leo XIV drew an estimated 800,000 to Place de la Concorde for a historic open-air Mass, urging French Catholics to share their faith openly.
posts.content:
Pope Leo XIV drew an estimated 800,000 people into the heart of Paris on Saturday for a massive open-air Mass, filling one of the French republic’s most storied public squares as he urged Catholics to openly share their faith in an "increasingly secularized society."

Flag-waving crowds packed the Champs-Élysées and Place de la Concorde as the American pope traveled roughly 1.2 miles through central Paris in the popemobile before celebrating Mass.

The Vatican estimated attendance at 800,000, roughly 200,000 more people than had registered in advance.

posts.title: 'Knots Landing' star Ted Shackelford spotted with walker during rare Los Angeles outing at 80
posts.excerpt: Ted Shackelford, who starred on "Knots Landing" and "The Young and the Restless," was photographed on a rare outing in Los Angeles with a walker.
posts.content:
"Knots Landing" star Ted Shackelford was spotted out in Los Angeles on a rare outing.

posts.content:
A 76-year-old Florida man with a suspended license allegedly admitted during a traffic stop that he had been drinking rum — later telling deputies he had also recently used cocaine — just four months after a separate DUI arrest, authorities said.

Charles Ducking, 76, of Lake Wales, was pulled over after a sheriff's deputy allegedly observed him swerving while driving along U.S. Highway 27 in Waverly, according to the Polk County Sheriff's Office.

The deputy detected the odor of alcohol and noticed that Ducking allegedly had slurred speech and watery eyes.

When asked for his driver's license, Ducking allegedly told the deputy it had been suspended.

posts.title: Hank Brown's last-second touchdown pass lifts Iowa to 20-19 win over Michigan in Big Ten
posts.excerpt: Hank Brown's 16-yard scoring strike to Reece Vander Zee with 2 seconds left gave the Iowa Hawkeyes a dramatic 20-19 Big Ten win over Michigan.
posts.content:
At the same stadium where Michigan benefited from an extra second in a controversial win over Western Michigan, the Iowa Hawkeyes made the most of their final opportunity Saturday.

Iowa quarterback Hank Brown connected with Reece Vander Zee for a game-winning 16-yard touchdown as time expired, lifting No. 17 Iowa to a 20-19 upset of No. 18 Michigan.

"To be able to silence a stadium like that, there’s no greater feeling," Brown said.

The Hawkeyes covered 91 yards on the game-winning drive, aided by an unnecessary roughness penalty against Michigan on third down near midfield. Brown’s 29-yard completion to Addison Ostrenga set up the winning touchdown with two seconds remaining.

posts.title: Woman caught smuggling alcohol disguised as bottled water to inmate in Ogun
posts.excerpt: Operatives of the Ibara Custodial Centre in Abeokuta on Saturday intercepted a woman, Shobowale Balikis, while attempting to smuggle alcohol disguised in a bottled-water pack to an inmate. The suspect
posts.content:
Operatives of the Ibara Custodial Centre in Abeokuta on Saturday intercepted a woman, Shobowale Balikis, while attempting to smuggle alcohol disguised in a bottled-water pack to an inmate.

The suspect was arrested at about 3:50 pm after officers detected ethanol concealed as drinking water during a routine search.

Confirming the incident to DAILY POST, the Public Relations Officer, PRO, of the Command, Odukoya Olayinka, said the swift action of correctional officers ensured that the illicit substance was detected before it could reach the inmate population.

Olayinka disclosed that the suspect had since been handed over to the Nigerian Police for further investigation and prosecution.

posts.title: I lost a state championship to a boy. I refuse to lose my voice
posts.excerpt: A Minnesota softball player describes losing her state championship semifinal to a team with a transgender pitcher and her fight for female athletes.
posts.content:
I have never been much of a crier.

So when my softball team lost in the semifinals of the Minnesota state tournament, I surprised even myself. I sobbed to my parents and family. I was devastated, confused, and hurt. But underneath it all was a sense of helplessness.

I was a senior, and my biggest goal was to make the state tournament and play alongside my younger sister. We made it. We battled through the tournament as underdogs. And then our season ended because the opposing team was allowed to put a boy in as the pitcher on a girls' team. His team went on to win the girls' high school state championship.

WE WERE FORCED TO COMPETE AGAINST A MALE. THE SUPREME COURT HAD OUR BACKS…

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/opinion/lost-state-championship-boy-refuse-lose-voice

posts.content:

posts.excerpt: A top US official on Sunday dismissed a proposal for reopening the Strait of Hormuz presented by Iran as "cynical" and indicated it was a non-starter for Washington. The post US dismisses Iran’s offer
posts.content:
A top US official on Sunday dismissed a proposal for reopening the Strait of Hormuz presented by Iran as “cynical” and indicated it was a non-starter for Washington.

Iran’s truce plan, announced by Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi at the United Nations earlier this week, calls for the release of frozen Iranian assets, the lifting of sanctions on Iranian oil and an end to the US naval blockade in order for the key waterway central to the world’s energy supplies to be opened.

“This was, I think, a pretty cynical attempt to put something on the table that they knew was unacceptable,” US Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz said on Sunday in an interview with NBC.

posts.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

ABUJA — BARRING any last-minute change, President Bola Tinubu is expected to return to Nigeria on Tuesday, September 29, ending a four-week working vacation in Europe.

Upon his return, the President is scheduled to mark Nigeria’s 66th Independence Anniversary in Lagos before returning to Abuja next weekend.
He was earlier expected to return to Abuja at the weekend before the change of schedule.

Presidency sources revealed on Sunday that Tinubu would arrive through Lagos, where he is expected to be received at the presidential wing of the Murtala Muhammed International Airport by Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu.

posts.title: Pope says assisted dying not ‘normal’
posts.excerpt: Pope Leo XIV on Sunday said assisted dying was not "normal", as he continued a landmark visit to France, where parliament has legalised the practice for certain patients. The post Pope says assisted d
posts.content:
Pope Leo XIV on Sunday said assisted dying was not “normal”, as he continued a landmark visit to France, where parliament has legalised the practice for certain patients.

“No human law should ever make you lose the certainty of your dignity,” he told believers who were sick or suffered from disabilities, at the French pilgrimage site of Lourdes.

“We must reject the temptation to cause death under the guise of false compassion. It is impossible to regard causing death as something normal,” he added.

“What is legal is not necessarily moral.”

France’s parliament passed legislation in June establishing a right to assisted dying for some adults suffering from an incurable condition.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/09/pope-says-assisted-dying-not-normal/

posts.title: Serbia’s President Vucic resigns as ruling party faces youth-backed opposition
posts.excerpt: Serbia’s President Aleksandar Vucic announced his resignation on ​Sunday, seven months before his tenure was originally scheduled to expire. 56-year-old Vucic ended his second and final five-year term
posts.content:
Serbia’s President Aleksandar Vucic announced his resignation on ​Sunday, seven months before his tenure was originally scheduled to expire.

56-year-old Vucic ended his second and final five-year term amid campaigning for the October ​25 snap parliamentary vote to elect 250 members of​ the National Assembly.

His departure sets the stage for early presidential elections and allows him to ​be appointed Prime Minister if the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) retains majority control of government.

“I have faithfully served you ​and my fatherland, Serbia. I am proud of what we ​have done together,” he told supporters at the Presidency building in Belgrade.

Source: https://dailypost.ng/2026/09/27/serbias-president-vucic-resigns-as-ruling-party-faces-youth-backed-opposition/

posts.title: NSCDC custody deaths and Nigeria’s detention crisis
posts.excerpt: Recently, thirty-seven illegal miners were arrested and detained in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) in Minna but never came out alive. That grim fact alone demands
posts.content:
Recently, thirty-seven illegal miners were arrested and detained in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) in Minna but never came out alive. That grim fact alone demands a thorough reckoning with Nigeria’s detention system and the accountability of agencies entrusted with the custody of lawfully detained citizens.

Whatever offences they were accused of committing, none had been convicted. Their detention could not extinguish their constitutional rights to life and dignity. The circumstances surrounding their deaths must therefore be established independently, transparently and without institutional defensiveness in the ongoing investigations.

posts.content:
I just turned 25.

People with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) aren't expected to see another birthday after this one. DMD is a progressive disease; my muscles weaken over time and things that used to be automatic now take planning, assistance, or simply aren't possible anymore. Even sleeping can be hard. Bed sores are now an issue. Basic physical function takes work most people never have to think about.

I know what the statistics say. I am not ready to let them write the ending of my story.

TRUMP FDA PICK REPEATEDLY SIDESTEPS SANDERS' UNIVERSAL HEALTHCARE DEMANDS IN HEATED CLASH

I want to grow my career, I want to get married and start a family.

posts.title: Malicious browser extensions can hijack AI assistants
posts.excerpt: BragJack research reveals how a single malicious browser extension could hijack Gemini, Perplexity Comet and Edge AI agents with zero clicks.
posts.content:
AI assistants are moving deeper into the browsers we use every day. They can summarize a webpage, explain what you are looking at and, in some cases, take action on websites for you. That convenience also gives these tools access that a normal webpage would never have. Now, security researcher Gal Weizman of Forever Security has shown how a malicious browser extension could potentially turn those powerful AI capabilities against you. His research, called BragJack, targeted Gemini Live in Chrome, Perplexity Comet, Microsoft Edge Actions, Opera Neon and Anthropic's Claude in Chrome. The findings resulted in more than $20,000 in bug bounties and two CVEs.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/tech/malicious-browser-extensions-hijack-ai-assistants

Before Game 162 against the Los Angeles Angels, Wilson held a closed-door meeting to inform players and staff.

posts.excerpt: An appeals court in Iran has confirmed a sentence of 74 lashes handed to prominent singer Parastoo Ahmadi after she performed without the mandatory hijab, according to her lawyers. The post Iran court
posts.content:
An appeals court in Iran has confirmed a sentence of 74 lashes handed to prominent singer Parastoo Ahmadi after she performed without the mandatory hijab, according to her lawyers.

Ahmadi, 29, performed in a sleeveless dress during a concert livestreamed on her YouTube channel in December 2024. The performance went viral and attracted millions of views.

Iranian law requires women to cover their hair and wear modest clothing in public. Public performances by women are also prohibited.

Iran’s judiciary opened proceedings against Ahmadi after the performance, describing it as being “in violation of the country’s legal and cultural regulations”.

For those who missed it, Stephens hit a sliding Moore in the helmet during the second quarter, knocking Moore out of the game and sending the star quarterback to the hospital down the street on a stretcher. The hit was brutal. Stephens' reaction to the play, while Moore was lying lifeless on the turf, was even more brutal.

posts.title: Republicans have a midterm problem. Reagan’s American vision is the answer
posts.excerpt: Trump lost 41 House seats in his first term's midterms, but Ronald Reagan's playbook of heralding American heroes offers Republicans a path forward.
posts.content:
Now in the autumn of this critical political season, a midterm loss of Congress for Republicans feels inevitable, as the last five midterm elections saw the party in power lose seats in Congress.

This trend goes back even longer than the 2000s. Since 1946, the president’s party has lost seats in the U.S. House of Representatives in 18 of 20 midterm elections (90% of the time).

President Donald Trump ran into this trend in his first term when, in 2018, Republicans lost 41 seats in the House — though they did gain two seats in the U.S. Senate.

MIDTERM HISTORY MASSIVELY FAVORS DEMOCRATS. BUT THEY ARE MAKING A BIG MISTAKE

Despite the pattern, a loss is not inevitable.

posts.title: The Big Reset: Will Nigerians Feel It?
posts.excerpt: The Monetary Policy Committee reset Nigeria's benchmark interest rate from 26.5 per cent to 23 per cent; a dramatic 350-basis-point adjustment, while recalibrating the corridor around the Monetary Pol
posts.content:
THE BIG RESET: WILL NIGERIANS FEEL IT?

Something important happened in Abuja last week.

It did not involve a defection, a campaign rally or another declaration about 2027. It happened at the Central Bank.

The Monetary Policy Committee reset Nigeria’s benchmark interest rate from 26.5 per cent to 23 per cent; a dramatic 350-basis-point adjustment, while recalibrating the corridor around the Monetary Policy Rate. The CBN insists that this is not simply a return to easy money. It describes it as an operational reset intended to reconnect the official policy rate with the rates actually operating in the financial system.

Technically, that distinction matters.

posts.title: NIGERIA @ 66: Focus On Judiciary – Disgraceful conflicting judgements that taint courts reputation
posts.excerpt: When two courts issue different orders over the same dispute, the law can suddenly acquire two voices. For litigants, lawyers, security agencies and ordinary citizens, the consequence is more than leg
posts.content:
By Henry Ojelu, Assistant Judicial Editor

When two courts issue different orders over the same dispute, the law can suddenly acquire two voices. For litigants, lawyers, security agencies and ordinary citizens, the consequence is more than legal confusion.

It can mean uncertainty over which order to obey, prolonged litigation and, in politically sensitive cases, the risk of turning a courtroom dispute into a wider public crisis.

That concern has become one of the most persistent issues confronting Nigeria’s judiciary, with the Kano Emirate crisis, the Rivers State political dispute and recent Supreme Court decisions providing striking examples of the problem.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/nigeria-66-focus-on-judiciary-disgraceful-conflicting-judgements-that-taint-courts-reputation/

posts.title: NIGERIA @ 66: Scandalised? – How NJC’s hammer fell on judges, justices
posts.excerpt: Perhaps the most dramatic recent disciplinary action came in Imo State in 2025 when the NJC compulsorily retired 10 judges over alleged age falsification The post NIGERIA @ 66: Scandalised? – How NJC’
posts.content:
By Clifford Ndujihe, Politics Editor

Since Nigeria attained independence in 1960, the nation’s judiciary has not been immune to misconduct, with several high-ranking judges and justices sanctioned, suspended, compulsorily retired or recommended for dismissal over allegations ranging from corruption and abuse of judicial powers to age falsification and controversial handling of cases.

The National Judicial Council, NJC, the principal body responsible for disciplining judicial officers, has over the years wielded its disciplinary powers against serving and senior judicial officers at both the federal and state levels.

posts.title: Judiciary Under Military, Civilian Rule: From ouster clauses to constitutional checks
posts.excerpt: The contrast is particularly evident in the judiciary’s relationship with executive power, access to justice, judicial independence and the determination of political disputes The post Judiciary Under
posts.content:
By Henry Ojelu, Assistant Judicial Editor

Nigeria’s judiciary has undergone profound changes since independence, moving from an institution operating under successive military governments and restrictive decrees to a constitutional arm of government with broader powers of judicial review under the Fourth Republic.

The contrast is particularly evident in the judiciary’s relationship with executive power, access to justice, judicial independence and the determination of political disputes.

Under military rule, the regular courts remained in existence, but their powers were frequently curtailed by military decrees.

posts.title: October 1: ‘Your speech turned Independence Day to lamentation’ – Dele Momodu tackles Tinubu
posts.excerpt: A chieftain of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Dele Momodu, has tackled President Bola Tinubu over his nationwide broadcast to mark Nigeria’s 66th Independence Anniversary. In a post on his veri
posts.content:
A chieftain of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Dele Momodu, has tackled President Bola Tinubu over his nationwide broadcast to mark Nigeria’s 66th Independence Anniversary.

In a post on his verified X handle on Thursday, Momodu said Tinubu’s speech turned Independence Day into a day of lamentation.

He said his heart bled as the President went into the analogy of Nigeria as a cancer patient who merely survived on painkillers before his arrival as a celebrated surgeon.

According to him, the President was expected to stabilise Nigeria and not metastasise it into stage-four cancer.

The publisher of Ovation Magazine lamented that Nigeria has made more money, amassed more loans, while insecurity has increased, poverty has escalated and politicians have remained insensitive.

“Dear Mr President, please permit me to wish you a Happy Independence Day on our 66th anniversary.

“Today is supposed to be a day of celebration, but your speech turned it into a day of lamentation.

“You specifically mentioned morphine as the drug of choice by your predecessors. I’m not sure this analogy was appropriate. At the time you assumed power, Nigeria probably had stage-two cancer, at the worst,” he wrote.

October 1: ‘Your speech turned Independence Day to lamentation’ – Dele Momodu tackles Tinubu

posts.title: AFCON qualifiers: Super Eagles reveal why Ola Aina didn’t play against Guinea-Bissau
posts.excerpt: The Super Eagles media officer, Promise Efoghe has provided clarification regarding the absence of Nottingham Forest defender Ola Aina from Nigeria’s 3-0 loss to Guinea-Bissau in Tuesday’s 2027 Africa
posts.content:
The Super Eagles media officer, Promise Efoghe has provided clarification regarding the absence of Nottingham Forest defender Ola Aina from Nigeria’s 3-0 loss to Guinea-Bissau in Tuesday’s 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying match.

The Djurtus flogged the Super Eagles of Nigeria 3-0 to claim an unexpected victory over the three-time African champions.

Aina, who rejoined the Super Eagles squad earlier this month, remained on the bench as Birmingham City’s Bright Osayi-Samuel assumed the right-back position.

Osayi-Samuel endured a challenging performance, finding it difficult to contain Guinea-Bissau captain Mama Baldé, whose pace and technical ability created significant difficulties for Nigeria’s defensive line.

Following the match, Efoghe attributed Aina’s absence to fitness concerns and expressed apprehension about the poor condition of the Stade du 24 Septembre playing surface.

He noted that the decision was informed by Aina’s previous experience at the Free State Stadium in Bloemfontein, where he sustained an injury that resulted in an extended absence from football.

“They are very similar. You wonder why Ola Aina could not play the game yesterday; it is a physiological thing,” Efoghe told News Central TV.

“Remember, it was on a bad pitch against South Africa that Ola Aina picked up an injury that took him out of football for almost one year.”

Efoghe also advocated for improved standards across African football, calling on relevant stakeholders to address concerns about playing conditions across the continent.

“We must discontinue these questionable practices in African football. If we want the sport to advance on the continent, we must conduct ourselves appropriately,” he concluded.

Aina sustained the injury during the first half of the Super Eagles’ crucial 2026 FIFA World Cup qualifying fixture against South Africa.

The Super Eagles will subsequently seek to bounce back from the disappointing result when they face Russia in an international friendly scheduled for October 6.

AFCON qualifiers: Super Eagles reveal why Ola Aina didn’t play against Guinea-Bissau

posts.title: October 1: Gov Idris urges Nigerians to uphold unity, democracy
posts.excerpt: Kebbi State governor, Nasir Idris has urged Nigerians to uphold national unity, democratic values and peaceful coexistence as the country marks its 66th Independence Anniversary. The governor made the
posts.content:
Kebbi State governor, Nasir Idris has urged Nigerians to uphold national unity, democratic values and peaceful coexistence as the country marks its 66th Independence Anniversary.

The governor made the call in an Independence Day message issued on Thursday by his Special Adviser on Media and Publicity, Yahaya Sarki.

Idris said Nigeria’s diversity should remain a source of strength, urging citizens to avoid political, religious and ethnic differences that could undermine national unity.

He also called on Nigerians to protect democratic gains, uphold the rule of law and support good governance as the country continues to address its challenges.

“We are stronger in unity, and our prosperity lies in upholding togetherness as one indivisible entity,” he said.

The governor urged citizens to draw inspiration from the sacrifices and patriotism of the country’s founding fathers and place the national interest above narrow considerations.

He also called for sustained prayers for the peace, stability and prosperity of Nigeria, saying the country’s challenges require collective responsibility, resilience and mutual understanding.

Idris said his administration remained committed to strengthening security in Kebbi State and implementing programmes aimed at improving the welfare of residents.

He urged citizens to cooperate with the government and security agencies in efforts to protect lives and property, particularly amid the security challenges confronting parts of the country.

October 1: Gov Idris urges Nigerians to uphold unity, democracy

posts.title: Mutfwang grants absolute pardon to 134 prison inmates on Independence Day
posts.excerpt: Plateau State governor, Caleb Manasseh Mutfwang, has exercised the prerogative of mercy entrenched in the Nigerian Constitution by granting an “absolute pardon” to 134 prison inmates as part of activi
posts.content:
Plateau State governor, Caleb Manasseh Mutfwang, has exercised the prerogative of mercy entrenched in the Nigerian Constitution by granting an “absolute pardon” to 134 prison inmates as part of activities marking Nigeria’s 66th Independence Anniversary on October 1, 2026.

Mutfwang, who announced the pardon in his speech to mark the country’s Independence Day anniversary, commuted the sentences of four inmates on death row to life imprisonment, while the others were granted absolute pardons.

The governor said the gesture followed consultations with the State Advisory Council on the Prerogative of Mercy, stressing the need for justice, humanity and hope as Nigerians reflect on the nation’s journey.

In the goodwill message signed by the governor’s Director of Press Affairs, Bere Gyang, Mutfwang said the pardoned inmates had exhibited remorse and become model prisoners, with many of them undertaking reforms that distinguished them.

Bere gave the names of the death-row inmates whose sentences were commuted to life imprisonment as Zuhumnan Musa, Jeremiah Aese, Pam Lang and Thoma Danboyi.

Mutfwang grants absolute pardon to 134 prison inmates on Independence Day

posts.title: October 1: Cost of living will come down – Tinubu promises Nigerian
posts.excerpt: President Bola Tinubu has assured Nigerians that his administration will bring down the cost of living. Tinubu made the promise on Thursday during his nationwide broadcast to mark Nigeria’s 66th Indep
posts.content:
President Bola Tinubu has assured Nigerians that his administration will bring down the cost of living.

Tinubu made the promise on Thursday during his nationwide broadcast to mark Nigeria’s 66th Independence Day anniversary.

According to him, Nigeria has enough land and people to feed the entire nation, stressing that his administration is focused on expanding mechanised irrigation and dry-season farming.

The President also promised that his government would improve access to seeds and fertiliser, increase mechanisation holistically, and invest in storage and transportation.

He added that his administration is building and completing the roads, railways and ports that connect farms and factories to markets.

“Our priority is to bring down the cost of living. We will achieve this by lowering the cost of producing and moving the things Nigerians consume.

“Our logic is simple. When a farmer produces more cheaply, when fewer crops are lost between the farm and the market, when a manufacturer spends less on electricity, when a truck reaches its destination faster, and when the business environment fosters fair competition, all those savings will ultimately find their way into the price of goods in the market.

“But prosperity requires more than cheaper goods. It requires productive work,” the President said.

posts.title: Haaland sues airline over ponytail image
posts.excerpt: Norwegian football superstar Erling Haaland is suing airline Norwegian Air Shuttle for unlawfully using his likeness, a lawsuit which the airline claims is incomprehensible and "regrettable", the two
posts.content:
Norwegian football superstar Erling Haaland is suing airline Norwegian Air Shuttle for unlawfully using his likeness, a lawsuit which the airline claims is incomprehensible and “regrettable”, the two parties said Thursday.

“The case concerns Norwegian’s unlawful use of Haaland’s distinctive signs in its promotion of plane tickets during the football World Cup,” Haaland’s lawyer, Thomas Hagen, said in an email to AFP.

Haaland, who plays for Manchester City, inspired Norway to reach the World Cup quarter-finals this summer, in their first appearance in football’s showpiece event since 1998, before losing 2-1 to England.

The exact subject of the dispute is not known, but newspaper Verdens Gang (VG) reported that Norwegian has removed a photo montage showing one of its planes sporting a ponytail, which until he recently cut his hair was characteristic of Haaland, from social media.

“We’ve never looked more Norwegian,” the caption of the image read.

The airline confirmed it had received a writ “which we find hard to understand”.

“Like almost all of Norway, we supported the national team this summer, through a few spontaneous posts inspired by trends on social media,” spokeswoman Catharina Solli told AFP.

“It is regrettable that this support has been met with legal action, but we hope to have a reasonable dialogue so that we can continue, in the future as well, to support our common sport heroes,” she added.

According to VG, a hearing at Oslo District Court is scheduled for October 9.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/haaland-sues-airline-over-ponytail-image/

posts.title: Elon Musk returns to US govt for Pentagon war study
posts.excerpt: Tech billionaire Elon Musk will make a return to officially advising US President Donald Trump's government by co-leading what the Pentagon called a study on the future of war. The post Elon Musk retu
posts.content:
Tech billionaire Elon Musk will make a return to officially advising US President Donald Trump’s government by co-leading what the Pentagon called a study on the future of war.

Musk served as the head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) before departing in May 2025, having publicly fallen out with Trump.

In a speech at the Quantico military base, Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth said “Project Meridian” will be “an effort led by America’s best minds to study the future of warfare”.

“We are leveraging a unique source of American advantage, one our adversaries do not have: our innovators, our senior leaders and our technologists,” Hegseth said.

Musk will be a co-leader of Project Meridian alongside Palmer Luckey, the 34-year-old co-founder of defense technology company Anduril Industries, and Newt Gingrich, the 83-year-old Republican former House speaker.

Musk threw his support behind Trump and helped his return to the White House, but the men later had a high-profile blow-up over the president’s spending legislation.

He later resumed giving to Republican causes, including multimillion-dollar donations to individual candidates and conservative political groups.

Hegseth said the project’s purpose is to “creatively look to the future and identify the domains that we must conquer and capabilities we must master”.

Project members will include hand-picked private sector leaders and subject matter experts from across the innovation, academic and policy ecosystems.

Hegseth said he has directed Project Meridian’s findings to be completed and submitted within 120 days.

AFP

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/elon-musk-returns-to-us-govt-for-pentagon-war-study/

posts.title: Messi to receive honorary doctorate from Argentine university
posts.excerpt: “Beyond what all Argentinians know about Messi, regardless of the numbers and statistics that attest to his status as an athlete, we also want to recognise a humble, persevering person, an example and
posts.content:
Retiring Argentina captain Lionel Messi is set to receive an honorary doctorate from the University of Buenos Aires (UBA) in recognition of his football career and contribution to the country.

The university’s Higher Council unanimously approved the conferment of the honorary degree, which is its highest honorary distinction. The award will be presented to Messi on Tuesday, October 6, ahead of Argentina’s farewell match against Benin at the Monumental Stadium.

UBA said Messi’s career represented “excellence, perseverance, humility and ethical practice”, while also highlighting his commitment to representing Argentina.

The university cited his role in Argentina’s major international triumphs, including the 2021 Copa América, 2022 Finalissima, 2022 FIFA World Cup and 2024 Copa América. It also recognised Argentina’s run to the 2026 World Cup final.

UBA Rector Ricardo Gelpi said the institution wanted the recognition to go beyond Messi’s statistics and achievements on the football pitch.

“Beyond what all Argentinians know about Messi, regardless of the numbers and statistics that attest to his status as an athlete, we also want to recognise a humble, persevering person, an example and ambassador of our popular culture and national identity,” Gelpi said.

He added that the honour was also intended to acknowledge Messi’s broader influence through sport and his representation of Argentina.

UBA Vice-Rector Emiliano Yacobitti said the distinction recognised the values Messi had displayed while representing the national team.

“Leo Messi knew how to convey the values of the Argentine jersey and represent it with courage and respect, and thus managed to take it to the highest level of world football.

“But this Honorary Doctorate is a recognition that transcends his football career. It is a tribute and a thank you that we offer him from the UBA, on behalf of all of Argentine society,” Yacobitti said.

The university said honorary doctorates are part of a long-standing tradition among leading institutions of higher education, allowing them to recognise individuals whose achievements and influence extend beyond their professional fields.

The honour comes as Messi prepares for his Argentina farewell against Benin on October 6 at the Monumental Stadium. The match is expected to mark his final appearance for the national team.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/messi-to-receive-honorary-doctorate-from-argentine-university/

posts.excerpt: The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has urged Nigerians to keep the hope alive in spite of the present challenges, saying the future of Nigeria is bright. The post Nigeria ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‌⁠⁠‍‌​​‍‌‌​at 66: Our
posts.content:
The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has urged Nigerians to keep the hope alive in spite of the present challenges, saying the future of Nigeria is bright.

PDP National Publicity Secretary Mr Jungudo Mohammed stated this in a statement issued by the party to mark Nigeria’s 66th Independence Anniversary on Thursday in Abuja.

Mohammed said that the PDP acknowledged that, as a nation and as a people, Nigeria and Nigerians were not yet where they aspired to be; however, they must not despair.

“The future of Nigeria remains bright, and our collective hope must remain stronger than our present challenges.

“Nigeria is a blessed nation, endowed with enormous human and natural resources.

“Let us harness these resources, alongside our rich ethnic, cultural and religious diversity, into an instrument of unity, creativity and national progress,” he said.

Mohammed called on all Nigerians to continue to preach peace, unity and national cohesion.

He also called on leaders and followers alike to remain patriotic, reject violence and corruption, and always place the interests of Nigeria above personal and sectional considerations.

“Above all, let us build a nation where our young people can dream, aspire and look to the future with confidence and hope,” he said.

The national publicity secretary pledged the PDP’s continued commitment to democracy, good governance and the welfare of the Nigerian people.

“We are poised to provide the alternative platform and leadership needed to help Nigeria realise her full potential and achieve the dreams and aspirations of her citizens.

“As we celebrate our nation, let us honour the sacrifices of our founding fathers and all those who have contributed to our national development, and ensure that the labour of our heroes past shall not be in vain.

“Together, let us renew our commitment to building a better Nigeria and restoring hope for the younger generations.

“Nigeria has what it takes to rise! Nigeria shall be great!” Mohammed said. (NAN)

posts.title: Alausa orders Okebukola-led panel to rank Nigerian tertiary institutions
posts.excerpt: Minister of Education, Dr. Tunji Alausa, has directed the Nigeria Tertiary Education Ranking Advisory Committee, NiTERAC, led by Prof. Peter Okebukola, to commence the 2026 national ranking of Nigeria
posts.content:
By Joseph Erunke, Abuja

Minister of Education, Dr. Tunji Alausa, has directed the Nigeria Tertiary Education Ranking Advisory Committee, NiTERAC, led by Prof. Peter Okebukola, to commence the 2026 national ranking of Nigerian universities, polytechnics and colleges of education, as the country records increased representation in the global university ranking.

The directive comes as 29 Nigerian universities have secured places in the 2027 Times Higher Education (THE) World University Rankings, up from 24 institutions in the 2026 edition.

Nigeria’s 29 ranked universities represent the highest number from any country in Sub-Saharan Africa, with five Nigerian institutions entering the global ranking for the first time.

The Federal Ministry of Education said the national ranking framework being developed by NiTERAC, in consultation with stakeholders, would assess tertiary institutions using 22 indicators designed to stimulate healthy competition, improve institutional visibility and strengthen their capacity to compete globally.

The ministry disclosed this in a statement issued on Thursday by its Director, Press and Public Relations, Boriowo Folasade, which linked the increased global representation of Nigerian universities to ongoing reforms under the leadership of Alausa.

According to the ministry, the reforms are focused on research excellence, innovation, institutional performance and international competitiveness under the Nigerian Education Sector Renewal Initiative ,NESRI.

The latest THE ranking shows that Nigeria’s federal universities account for a significant proportion of the country’s improved performance.

Five of the seven Nigerian universities placed within the global top 1,200 are federal institutions, representing 71.4 per cent of Nigeria’s universities in that band.

The University of Ibadan and University of Lagos retained positions in the 801–1000 band, while Ahmadu Bello University and University of Ilorin advanced into the 1001–1200 band, joining Bayero University, which retained its position in the same band.

Covenant University also retained a position in the 801–1000 band.

The ministry further disclosed that federal universities occupied all six Nigerian positions in the 1401–1600 band.

Five of the seven Nigerian universities that recorded clear upward movement were also federal institutions– Ahmadu Bello University, University of Ilorin, Nnamdi Azikiwe University, Obafemi Awolowo University and University of Benin.

Beyond the 29 institutions ranked globally, another 32 Nigerian universities were listed in THE Reporter category, bringing the total number of Nigerian institutions engaged with the ranking exercise to 61.

The ministry said the 2027 THE ranking identified Research Quality as the strongest performance pillar for Nigerian universities, while Research Environment and Teaching remained areas requiring further attention.

It said continued improvement in academic reputation, research output and productivity, doctoral output, international collaboration and institutional data reporting would be critical to sustaining the progress recorded.

The ministry described the growing participation of Nigerian universities in global rankings as more than recognition, saying the exercise would serve as a mechanism for benchmarking performance, identifying institutional gaps and accelerating continuous improvement across the tertiary education sector.

It reaffirmed its commitment to reforms aimed at advancing research excellence, teaching quality, innovation, international engagement and institutional competitiveness.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/alausa-orders-okebukola-led-panel-to-rank-nigerian-tertiary-institutions/

posts.title: ‘East Of Eden’ review: brutal American epic powered by Florence Pugh
posts.excerpt: Zoe Kazan delivers an unflinchingly bold take on the literary classic The post ‘East Of Eden’ review: brutal American epic powered by Florence Pugh appeared first on NME.
posts.content:
It hardly needs to be said at this point but the easiest way to make anything better is to add Florence Pugh. East Of Eden proves this once more. The Netflix miniseries starts with her character Cathy, beaten and bloody, dragging herself over the threshold of the Trask brothers’ house. Appalled, they take her in but soon they’re arguing over this mystery woman’s motives, while Cathy sits upstairs and eavesdrops on them both. What’s going on behind her eyes? Pugh makes sure we’re kept guessing.

READ MORE: The best TV shows of 2026… so far!

So begins the latest adaptation of John Steinbeck’s Cain and Abel-inspired fable: an epic tale of suffering and self-determination in which almost all the characters end up roundly miserable. Written and executive-produced by Hollywood star Zoe Kazan (whose grandfather, Elia, directed the celebrated 1955 film adaptation), this is a version that goes heavy with its mournful string soundtrack and all-star cast.

But they’re worth the investment, because there’s plenty of meat in this multigenerational saga. Cathy’s arrival merely accelerates the slow-burning rift between Adam and Charles Trask, here played with a touching reserve by Christopher Abbott and a furious defiance by Mike Faist.

Mike Faist, Christopher Abbott, Florence Pugh in ‘East Of Eden’. CREDIT: NetflixSlow and sedate, the show’s pacing gives every facet of the story time to breathe. Abused by their Civil War veteran father Cyrus growing up, Adam and Charles’ childhood closeness is shattered when he sends the shy Adam off to war and tells the boisterous Charles to work the family farm. Fifteen years later, the estranged pair discover that Cyrus left them a small fortune – and their disagreement over how to spend it is inflamed by Cathy’s arrival.

There’s more to Cathy than meets the eye – and most of it quite dark. In search of an easy score, she seduces and marries Adam. But, unhappy with his plans for them both, she sets about carving her own path in the most destructive way possible. “Marriage isn’t so easy to undo,” Charles tells Cathy at one point. “No,” she replies. “But perhaps it can be slipped out of, like a poorly made knot.”

Make no mistake: alongside moments of lyricism, East Of Eden can be harrowing. In one scene, Cathy is beaten almost to death by her abusive lover. Later on, she performs an attempted abortion with a knitting needle while an oblivious Adam shops for their dream home.

Pugh is consistently stupendous. While the book paints Cathy as a fallen woman, Kazan handles her far more deftly. This Cathy has an almost slippery quality to her: unknowable to the viewer and the two hapless men in thrall to her. But she’s also constrained by the attitudes of the time, some of which reverberate ominously into the present day. After her attempted abortion, the doctor first threatens to charge her then advises not to try any “nasty tricks” again. Even Adam, supposedly a good man, wastes no time laying down the law. “With time, you will be happy,” he tells her, explaining his decision to move them both to California. Never mind what she wants in this situation.

As the show moves from Connecticut to the Salinas Valley, the colour palette changes from soft greens to gorgeous sun-dappled browns; we meet Lee (Hoon Lee) and Samuel Hamilton (Ciarán Hinds), as well as Cathy and Adam’s children (Cal and Aron) who seem doomed to inherit the sins of their parents.

It’s all very literary, with a capital L: a sprawling tale of the sort that suits the wide-open landscapes and infinite possibility of the American dream. Kazan has made a worthy successor to her grandfather’s seminal masterpiece; this is East Of Eden for a 21st-century audience.

‘East Of Eden’ is out October 1 on Netflix

Source: https://www.nme.com/reviews/tv-reviews/east-of-eden-review-florence-pugh-zoe-kazan-netflix-3971392?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=east-of-eden-review-florence-pugh-zoe-kazan-netflix

posts.title: Rebecca Hall & Dan Stevens’ $572M Monster Blockbuster Finds New Streaming Home
posts.excerpt: A $572 million monster blockbuster just found a new streaming home ahead of its highly anticipated sequel. The Rebecca Hall and Dan Stevens-led MonsterVerse hit arrives on a major streaming platform t
posts.content:
Photo Credit: Legendary PicturesA $572 million monster blockbuster just found a new streaming home ahead of its highly anticipated sequel. The Rebecca Hall and Dan Stevens-led MonsterVerse hit arrives on a major streaming platform this October.

The MonsterVerse hit is coming to Prime Video next week

Godzilla x Kong: The New Empire arrives on Prime Video on October 4. The 2024 MonsterVerse blockbuster joins a stacked slate of new additions to the streaming platform this month.

Adam Wingard returned to direct the sequel to 2021’s Godzilla vs. Kong. Rebecca Hall, Brian Tyree Henry, and Kaylee Hottle returned from the previous film. Dan Stevens, Alex Ferns, and Fala Chen joined the franchise as newcomers. The plot centers on Kong uncovering a hidden tribe of his kind within the Hollow Earth. He then teams up with Godzilla once again to defeat the ruthless Skar King and his captive Titan, Shimo.

The film earned $572.5 million worldwide against a production budget of $135 to $150 million. It became the highest-grossing entry in both the Godzilla and King Kong franchises. On Rotten Tomatoes, 54% of 251 critics gave positive reviews, with an average rating of 5.7 out of 10. Audiences polled by CinemaScore awarded the film an A-minus grade. The movie opened domestically at $80 million, marking the second-best opening weekend in the Monsterverse series.

Hottle’s appearance marks her final film role before her death in 2026 at age 18. Filming took place primarily on the Gold Coast in Queensland, Australia, starting in July 2022. Weta FX handled the visual effects for the Hollow Earth sequences and the ape tribe. Scanline VFX created the climactic battle scenes in Egypt and Rio de Janeiro.

Legendary Pictures has already greenlit a follow-up titled Godzilla x Kong: Supernova. Grant Sputore will direct the next installment, which is currently set to release on March 26, 2027.

posts.title: Ariana Madix’s Next TV Role Is Nothing Like Love Island USA
posts.excerpt: Ariana Madix is leaving the villa behind for a distant asteroid colony. The Vanderpump Rules alum and Emmy-nominated Love Island USA host has signed on to lead a new sci-fi series, which is a pivot fr
posts.content:
Photo Credit: PeacockAriana Madix is leaving the villa behind for a distant asteroid colony. The Vanderpump Rules alum and Emmy-nominated Love Island USA host has signed on to lead a new sci-fi series, which is a pivot from the reality dating franchise that raised her to stardom.

Ariana Madix to star in Seth MacFarlane’s Future Housewives

Madix will headline Future Housewives, a Peacock project created by Brannon Braga, the writer-producer behind Star Trek: Voyager. She also takes an executive producer credit through her Over Fences banner.

Seth MacFarlane executive-produces via Fuzzy Door Productions with Erica Huggins, reuniting with Braga after their work together on The Orville. Jaron Lanier co-executive-produces, while Fuzzy Door’s Rachel Hargreaves-Heald and Emily Kochman oversee development. Universal Global Television serves as the studio.

The series drops Ariana Madix into New Beverly Hills, a wealthy asteroid colony where socialites chase bioengineered beauty treatments, bitter feuds, and interplanetary scandals. Her character, a wide-eyed outsider, comes and disrupts their insulated world, exposing how far the residents have drifted from a society moving past surface-level glamour. The logline frames it as a satirical yet heartfelt reinvention of the reality TV format.

That premise makes Future Housewives deemed a natural fit for Madix, who built her career inside the reality genre. Here, though, she plays a scripted role rather than herself. Braga brings serious sci-fi credentials.

He has written and produced across multiple Star Trek series and films, The Orville and ABC’s Flashforward, among other projects. Pairing that background with Madix’s reality TV instincts gives the show an unusual hybrid identity.

Moreover, the casting continues Madix’s post-Vanderpump Rules expansion. She has appeared on Broadway in Just in Time and Chicago, guested on NBC’s St. Denis Medical and ABC’s Will Trent, and performed in CollegeHumor and Dropout sketches early in her career. Peacock has not announced a release date yet (via The Hollywood Reporter).

Source: https://www.comingsoon.net/tv/news/2200488-love-island-usa-ariana-madix-seth-macfarlane-future-housewives-peacock

posts.title: Will Neagley Return to Alan Ritchson’s Reacher? Maria Sten Has Answered
posts.excerpt: Maria Sten is not closing the book on Frances Neagley’s future in Reacher. Asked whether she could return to the parent series, Sten pointed to the franchise’s flexible setup and hints that there’s a
posts.content:
Photo Credit: Prime VideoMaria Sten is not closing the book on Frances Neagley’s future in Reacher. Asked whether she could return to the parent series, Sten pointed to the franchise’s flexible setup and hints that there’s a possibility.

Maria Sten leaves door open for Neagley’s Reacher return

During a Screenrant interview, Maria Sten said “there’s always a door open,” hinting that there’s a chance for Neagley to cross paths with Jack Reacher again. Sten’s reasoning comes down to the way the franchise moves through Lee Child’s novels. Sten noted that Reacher follows an anthology model, so a potential comeback depends on which book the series chooses to adapt.

During this week's #CoffeeChats episode, #Neagley star #MariaSten addresses the chances of her return to #Reacher despite the success of her new spinoff show.

Watch the full episode: https://t.co/9x8ioUaI97#AlanRitchson #PrimeVideo pic.twitter.com/k7uDaBB5FZ

— ScreenRant (@screenrant) September 30, 2026

“So it really just depends on what, what book they want to do. There are more Neely books, or more books, Reacher books with Neagley in them,” Sten said. She also stressed that Neagley appears in additional Reacher books, giving the writers more material to draw from.

Sten also sees the TV universe as something that can run on separate tracks without locking its characters apart. She said the worlds can operate “independently and sort of parallel with each other,” while still allowing a crossover later. So, Neagley’s current solo chapter does not automatically shut the door on another reunion with Alan Ritchson’s Reacher.

The franchise has already opened another door with Neagley, giving Maria Sten’s character a spotlight of her own on Prime Video. Sten plays Frances Neagley, a Chicago-based private investigator whose military past ties her directly to Reacher. The spinoff also features Greyston Holt as Detective Hudson Riley and Adeline Rudolph as Renée Birdwhistle, while Alan Ritchson also appear as Reacher in a guest appearance.

Across eight episodes, Neagley steps out of Reacher’s shadow and leads her own mission with a team around her. The story draws from Lee Child’s characters and folds in her experience with the 110 Special Investigators. Where she goes next could depend on the franchise’s next storyline and whether the writers can carve out another opening for her.

Rotten Tomatoes currently lists Neagley at 94% from critics and 82% from audiences. IMDb gives the series a 7.7/10 user rating.

Source: https://www.comingsoon.net/tv/news/2200536-maria-sten-discusses-neagley-reacher-return-alan-ritchson

posts.title: Dragon Ball Super Fans Won’t Have To Wait Much Longer for Its Us Return
posts.excerpt: The wait for Dragon Ball Super in the U.S. is finally getting a clear endpoint. Netflix has confirmed that Dragon Ball Super: Beerus, the enhanced remake of the popular anime, will arrive for American
posts.content:
Photo Credit: @ToeiAnimationjp/YouTubeThe wait for Dragon Ball Super in the U.S. is finally getting a clear endpoint. Netflix has confirmed that Dragon Ball Super: Beerus, the enhanced remake of the popular anime, will arrive for American viewers this month, giving fans a firm date to circle on their calendars.

Netflix brings Dragon Ball Super: Beerus to US viewers on October 17

Netflix will add Dragon Ball Super: Beerus to its U.S. lineup on Oct. 17. Japan will get the remake first on Oct. 11, creating a six-day gap between the two releases. Netflix also marked the announcement with a fresh trailer, officially putting the streaming date in the spotlight (via Comicbook).

The remake comes from Toei Animation and features Tadayoshi Yamamuro as director. Matsuto Seya handles composition and direction arrangement, while Eichi Nishimura works as editor and Yosuke Motoki serves as compositing director. Norihito Sumitomo returns to the musical side, with new theme songs also lined up for the series.

Those songs include “ONOGAMI” by MEGATERA・ZERO as the opening theme and “Kan Peki No Peki” by VK Blanka for the ending. The refreshed production also promises a substantially reworked presentation of the original anime, rather than simply putting the existing episodes back on screen.

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus isn’t simply dusting off old footage. Toei is rebuilding the material with reworked scenes, fresh cuts and completely re-rendered visuals, while new dubbing, music and sound effects give the production more polish. The story kicks off with Battle of Gods, then rolls into Resurrection F and the Universe 6 storyline.

Fans can also catch the new version before Netflix gets it. A New York Comic Con 2026 panel will spotlight the project on Oct. 8, with Monica Rial hosting alongside Jason Douglas and Ian Sinclair, the English voices of Bulma, Beerus and Whis, respectively.

Netflix remains the confirmed U.S. streaming home for the Oct. 17 launch. However, other platforms and their release dates had not yet been confirmed.

Source: https://www.comingsoon.net/anime/news/2200548-dragon-ball-super-beerus-netflix-usa-october-17

posts.title: Ben Affleck Isn’t Buying the Skynet Fears Surrounding AI
posts.excerpt: Ben Affleck joined Donald Trump‘s White House lunch with tech chiefs this week, yet he struck a much calmer note on artificial intelligence than the executives beside him, waving off Skynet-style nigh
posts.content:
Photo Credit: NetflixBen Affleck joined Donald Trump‘s White House lunch with tech chiefs this week, yet he struck a much calmer note on artificial intelligence than the executives beside him, waving off Skynet-style nightmares and arguing that Hollywood has little to fear.

Ben Affleck pushes back on AI doomsday fears

Speaking at a Bloomberg Screentime event on AI and entertainment, the Oscar winner said the film business ranks among the sectors least likely to be replaced by the technology. His real worries are closer to home, starting with schools.

Affleck, who founded the AI company InterPositive, flagged a 30% jump in the number of A’s handed out at colleges over three years. “I worry about learned helplessness. I worry about responsible use,” he said. Killer-machine scenarios do not keep him up at night. “I don’t worry about Skynet, and I don’t think that it’s going to take over this business in any meaningful way,” he said.

He believes anxiety drops once creators actually use the tools. Filmmakers who gain control and understanding, Affleck said, stop seeing a menacing, abstract force and start seeing software. He likened it to earlier technological leaps in film and television, describing AI as “another form of computing that does tools.” Regular users also discover its limits, he added. The flaws and clumsy moments pile up until the technology feels ordinary. In his words, “It becomes a knowable thing.”

Affleck’s optimism comes with a recent financial gain. Netflix acquired InterPositive this spring for $587 million, a figure confirmed after the deal. The company builds AI tools designed by and for filmmakers. Its team of fewer than 20 people moved to the streamer, and Affleck stayed on as an advisor.

The actor and director also discussed Artist Equity, which he started in 2022 alongside Matt Damon and Redbird Capital’s Gerry Cardinale. The company wants to turn profit sharing from an occasional bonus into the core of its business model, helping workers earn reasonable returns as technology and audience habits shift (via Deadline).

Source: https://www.comingsoon.net/movies/news/2200527-ben-affleck-skynet-ai-hollywood

posts.title: NFL rookie drops incredible cliché as he tries to help Bucs avoid 0-4 start against Packers
posts.excerpt: Jalon Daniels shared the advice Baker Mayfield gave him ahead of his first NFL start as the Buccaneers face a potential 0-4 hole against the Packers.
posts.content:
Tampa Bay Buccaneers rookie Jalon Daniels will make the first start of his career on Sunday as he goes under center for an injured Baker Mayfield.

Now, before we get to that, let’s remember that the NFL world is filled with cliches. Players and coaches love saying, "We gotta take it one quarter at a time," "Each week is a season," "We’re trying to go 1-0 each week" – well, you get the picture.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Well, the former Kansas Jayhawks star dropped a new one on Wednesday as he talked to reporters ahead of the Buccaneers’ Week 4 game against the Green Bay Packers. He was asked if he was going to be able to stay calm when it’s his turn to take the field.

"Absolutely. I think that one thing I learned in college was, you can't be the thermometer, you have to be the thermostat," he said. "You have to be someone who comes in and is able to set the temperature of the room, not test the room and try to be able to blend in with it. If a team is low, I have to be able to pick it up to be able to make sure that they're even.

"If we're high, then I have to be able to be low to be able to make sure that we're even. I try to be as even-keel as possible. I think that being able to go out there and have that even-keeled feel, the team around you feels that."

Love it when a new cliché drops, especially one you can use randomly in everyday life.

But there’s another cliché to use when it comes to the Buccaneers’ Week 4 game – "must win."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

It’s usually reserved for a team that is vying for a playoff spot. However, for Tampa Bay, it’s used here to save the season. The Buccaneers face the stark reality of dropping to 0-4 and a Mount Everest-type climb to get back into contention with Mayfield out for the next three weeks at least with a dislocated right thumb.

Daniels will get a real shot to show what he’s made of against the Packers.

"For us, it's just trying to get a win," coach Todd Bowles said when asked about trying to get a win. "(Jalon Daniels) is not playing by himself. Everybody has to do their job. We've got to coach it the right way on both sides of the ball, including special teams. He's got to play and just do his job.

"We've got 21 other guys that (are) going to be out there playing with him, so he's not by himself. It's (a) nervous (feeling) but it's exciting at the same time because you get to see somebody play. No matter where you come from, your first NFL game has to come at some point, whether you're a first-round pick or whether you're a free agent. You've got to touch the field for the first time at some point, and then you've got to play. He's just got to play."

Of course, Daniels tapped Mayfield for some advice before the pivotal matchup.

"He simply put it as: you've been dreaming of this opportunity, just stay composed, play as yourself," Daniels said. "Don't try to be anybody else besides you, and go out there and just go make football plays."

The way the Bucs look this season – it’s easier said than done.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/outkick-sports/nfl-rookie-drops-incredible-cliche-helps-bucs-avoid-0-4-start-against-packers

posts.title: Mullin tells Ruthless podcast that the Trump administration has apprehended 2,210 terrorists
posts.excerpt: Markwayne Mullin told the "Ruthless Podcast" that President Donald Trump shifted border security from defense to offense, aggressively pursuing terrorists nationwide.
posts.content:
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told the "Ruthless Podcast" that 2,210 terrorists have been apprehended under the Trump administration’s aggressive approach to solving illegal immigration.

"Underneath President Trump, we’ve arrested, so far as my numbers walking into here, 2,210 terrorists in this country," Mullin said in an exclusive interview released Thursday morning. "Most of them came over and claimed asylum, gave a fake name. Some of them we caught, but a lot of them came in and … the Biden administration was just cutting them loose."

Mullin said that under the Biden administration, 97% of individuals DHS encountered were released within 27 hours.

Earlier this month, ahead of the 25th anniversary of the September 11th attacks, DHS had announced that it had detained 2,150 known or suspected terrorists.

TRUMP ADMIN MARKS 15 STRAIGHT MONTHS WITH ZERO BORDER RELEASES AS APPREHENSIONS PLUNGE 94%

Mullin noted that these individuals were classified as terrorists. "There's a difference between a suspected terrorist and a terrorist watch list," the secretary explained to the co-hosts. "These were terrorists."

Mullin said the arrests resulted from a new administration-wide approach to illegal immigration.

"One directive we had is we're no longer just playing defense," Mullin told the hosts. "We're on the offense. President Trump has given us the authority to go on the offensive. For instance, cybersecurity. We're no longer sitting there and just protecting as you try to attack us. We're swimming upstream now. We're going after the people that are coming after us. We're aggressively going after individuals. I want to put you on offense."

Mullin rose quickly to the Cabinet post. He served in the House before winning election to the Senate in 2022. President Donald Trump nominated him to lead DHS in March, and the Senate confirmed him 54-45 on March 23.

TRUMP REAFFIRMS ICE ARREST POLICY AFTER CONFUSING GUIDANCE SPARKS ALARM AMONG AGENTS

"I thought I was busy as a Senator," Mullin said of his move to DHS. "I haven't slept through the night. I'm not joking when I say this. I haven't slept through the night in six months," the Oklahoman added.

With just over a month to go until the November midterm elections, podcast co-host Josh Holmes commended the secretary for his job performance as immigration remains a polarizing political issue.

"You also inherited a department that the reason it was shut down is that Democrats have demagogued everything to do with border security and ICE in particular," Holmes told Mullin. "Under the previous DHS administration, there was some kind of prioritization of the lowest-hanging fruit of deportations rather than what you're talking about, which is that people need to get the hell out of here as fast as possible."

posts.title: Former Arizona fraternity leader sentenced to jail time after pledge dies in off-campus hazing
posts.excerpt: Carter Eslick, former Northern Arizona University fraternity leader, pleaded guilty to felony hazing in the alcohol poisoning death of a pledge.
posts.content:
A former fraternity leader at Northern Arizona University was sentenced to two months in jail on Wednesday for his role in a hazing incident that led to the death of a student.

Carter Eslick, 20, pleaded guilty to a felony hazing charge in Coconino County Superior Court for the Jan. 31 death of Colin Daniel Martinez. Eslick served as the Delta Tau Delta pledge master at the time of the incident.

Martinez died at a Delta Tau Delta off-campus house due to alcohol poisoning, with an autopsy finding a blood-alcohol content of 0.45% shortly after his death.

LSU FRAT PLEDGES ALLEGEDLY WATERBOARDED, FORCED TO CHUG MILK IN HAZING RITUALS: REPORT

During the hazing, Martinez was among a group of four pledges who drank two bottles of vodka to ensure that they vomited, according to NBC News.

Hazing witnesses said they attempted to monitor the sleeping Martinez for signs of alcohol poisoning, adjusting his sleeping position multiple times.

Eslick told the court, where Martinez's parents were present, that he takes "full responsibility for the hand I played in that ritual."

The sentencing comes amid headlines regarding the mysterious deaths of two students at Ole Miss — one of whom was in a fraternity — and an alleged frat cocaine distribution ring at Penn State.

PENN STATE FRATERNITY COCAINE DEALS GREW TO KILO LOADS AS PLEDGES HELPED PACKAGE DRUGS, WITNESSES TESTIFY

One of the Ole Miss students who was found dead this past week, Robert Strang, was a Phi Delta Theta fraternity brother. He was found at an off-campus home. Authorities found packages of kratom, a commercially available drug that has been derided as "gas station heroin," at the sites of both deaths. However, its role in either death was not immediately clear.

Phi Delta Theta has not been accused of any wrongdoing.

posts.title: October 1: Nigerians protest at Federal High Court, demand judicial freedom
posts.excerpt: Nigerians on Thursday gathered outside the Federal High Court, calling for greater independence of Nigeria’s judiciary and stronger protection of citizens’ rights. The protesters said they chose Indep
posts.content:
Nigerians on Thursday gathered outside the Federal High Court, calling for greater independence of Nigeria’s judiciary and stronger protection of citizens’ rights.

The protesters said they chose Independence Day for the demonstration to highlight the importance of freedom, insisting that the judiciary must be free from executive manipulation.

Addressing protesters at the gathering, one of them, who identified himself as Henry Pwajok Lodam, said the demonstration was not limited to political cases but was also intended to draw attention to Nigerians who, according to him, remain in detention for prolonged periods without trial.

He alleged that some detainees had spent years in custody without their cases being properly concluded.

“The judiciary in Nigeria is broken,” Lodam said, while calling on judicial authorities to strengthen the protection of citizens and ensure due process.

According to him, the judiciary should be able to protect the rights of ordinary Nigerians, regardless of their political affiliation, social status or circumstances.

Lodam also raised concerns about what he described as undue influence of the executive arm of government on the judiciary, arguing that judicial independence was essential to the survival of democracy.

“We want independence of the judiciary, which is very important for democracy. If the judiciary is not allowed to function independently of the executive arm of government, then there is no democracy,” he said.

He described the continued legal proceedings and detention surrounding some individuals as matters that deserve closer scrutiny, while calling for every person who is unlawfully detained to be given access to justice and due process.

Lodam acknowledged that different groups have grievances against former Kaduna State Governor Nasir El-Rufai, particularly over issues surrounding his administration.

However, he argued that such disagreements should not prevent anyone from receiving a fair hearing under the law.

“We are not saying that we believe that his government was fair to all. But what we are saying is that we need the justice system of this country to be cleaned up,” he said.

He described what he considered the continued detention of El-Rufai as an example of what the group believes should be subjected to proper judicial scrutiny.

The group subsequently called for El-Rufai’s release, while stressing that its demand should also apply to other Nigerians who may be unlawfully detained.

October 1: Nigerians protest at Federal High Court, demand judicial freedom

posts.title: Independence Day: ‘2027 election must be free, fair, no more gambling’ – APM warn
posts.excerpt: The Allied People’s Movement, APM, has said that the current economic hardship bedevilling the country can be traced to poor leadership. The party said it was an aberration in a democratic system of g
posts.content:
The Allied People’s Movement, APM, has said that the current economic hardship bedevilling the country can be traced to poor leadership.

The party said it was an aberration in a democratic system of governance for such economic challenges to persist, adding that citizens deserved a fair deal from the government they voted into office.

APM said citizens needed to enjoy the dividends of democracy, not carnage. The party stated this in its message to Nigerians on the occasion of the 66th Independence anniversary.

“In 66 years, Nigerians have witnessed unprecedented political, economic and social challenges, and prevailed – a testament to citizens’ resilience and abiding faith in God and the fatherland,” a statement signed by Dr Yusuf Mamman Dantalle, APM National Chairman, said.

The party commended the nation’s founding fathers, who, according to it, despite all odds, secured the much-needed independence from Britain on October 1, 1960.

“It is time to reset Nigeria. It is time for a national rebirth and a greater future for all citizens,” it added.

“The elections must be credible and transparent, and the will of the people respected by all stakeholders in the democratic process.

“The era of gambling with our national destiny is over. It is what puts us in this governance quagmire of perennial insecurity and economic hardship. Nigerians are no longer safe in their own country and not sure where the next meal will come from.

“The upcoming 2027 general election offers us another opportunity to vote for competent leaders who will put Nigeria first.

“As we celebrate the nation’s 66th Independence, let us aspire for a new Nigeria built on unity, peace, progress and development. Let us continue to stand together as one nation. Together, we will reset Nigeria to fulfil its manifest destiny of greatness and prosperity.”
