posts.title: 2027: Shun vote-buying, money politics, violence – Ogun PDP’s Sowunmi-Kolapo tells Muslims
posts.excerpt: The deputy governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, in Ogun State, Lateefat Yemi Sowunmi-Kolapo, has urged Muslims in the state to shun vote-buying and violence and to actively par
posts.content:
The deputy governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, in Ogun State, Lateefat Yemi Sowunmi-Kolapo, has urged Muslims in the state to shun vote-buying and violence and to actively participate in elections to elect morally upright leaders.

Sowunmi-Kolapo said Muslim leaders, families and youths must recognise the importance of political participation in protecting their interests and heritage in the state.

According to her, religious leaders and members of the community should not assume that their interests would be automatically protected without active involvement in the political process.

“Let us tell our wards and our children, there should be no violence. Everybody should go out to exercise their civic rights and ensure that those they want actually emerge,” she said.

She made the call on Thursday in Ake, Abeokuta, shortly after her decoration as Grand Matron of the Ogun State Muslim Council (OMC), Egba Zone, describing the honour as a demonstration of the confidence and affection of the Muslim community.

She also cautioned against money politics, noting that politicians who distribute money during elections may seek greater favours after assuming office.

“So, everybody should ensure that this time around, they participate in the election. They shouldn’t sit back and say, ‘Oh, they will write the votes, somebody will write the votes.’ It is what you do that will count,” she added.

She urged the Muslim community to come out en masse during elections, exercise their civic rights peacefully and vote for candidates of their choice, while also canvassing support for the PDP governorship candidate, Ladi Adebutu.

In his keynote lecture, the Mufti of Ilorin, Sheikh Farouq Sulaiman Onikijipa, urged governments at all levels to invest more in education, noting that it remains critical to national stability.

Onikijipa also decried the high cost of education at both private and public institutions and called on government to make education more accessible to promote stability.

Speaking on the theme, “Socio-economic Stability: A Fortress for Global Security,” he said morality must be prioritised in leadership selection.

“For us to have stability in anything, we must choose a leader who is morally upright; who will not pocket public funds or take advantage of others for personal benefit,” he said.

He called on politicians to shun campaigns of calumny and urged youths to embrace knowledge acquisition so as not to be used as tools of destruction for political interests.

Earlier in her remarks, the PDP senatorial candidate for Ogun Central, Senator Iyabo Obasanjo, described Kolapo-Sowunmi as a community builder and moulder of greater generations for Egbaland.

She said the current political struggle is not about fighting but about reorganising the affairs of the state and not mortgaging the future of Ogun State for money.

posts.title: The president’s disappointing October 1 message, by Adekunle Adekoya
posts.excerpt: NOT a few Nigerians, especially me, expected that there would be something to hold on to when the President made his speech commemorating our National Day, October 1, yesterday morning. As a newspaper
posts.content:
NOT a few Nigerians, especially me, expected that there would be something to hold on to when the President made his speech commemorating our National Day, October 1, yesterday morning. As a newspaperman, I read the message more than three times, looking for that strand of a message that could give hope that at the end of the tunnel in which we have been thrown, there would be a glimmer of light, signalling hope that things would begin a turnaround for the better.

Alas, like so many other countrymen and women, numbering in scores of millions, it was not to be as the president opted to grandstand on what he thinks are achievements. The same old chorus, now sounding like a broken record, was recited to us — necessity of reforms, NELFUND, Credicorp, and all that. There was no talk about how we would soon pay less for petrol, diesel, cooking gas, or electricity.

Let me backtrack a bit. When Nigeria was Nigeria, we eagerly looked forward to October 1. As schoolchildren in the glorious 60s and 70s, every October 1, our teachers told us to come to school with our plates and spoons. Everyone of us got a plate of rice and a chunky piece of meat, with a bottle of mineral drink to drown it in. Government worked so well in those days that the headmasters of primary schools got the funds with which to prepare these meals for their pupils well ahead of time. And it was a time when there was nothing like bank transfers, internet banking. The POS operator was an alien figure. Yet, things worked. If it were now, the funds will never get to the school headmasters, and the children would never get any food.

That time too, was when Nigeria was arguably the most secure country in the world, compared to what now obtains. A little over 50 years ago, in April 1976, I was in Class III in secondary school. Our Geography teacher, Mr Bayo Ogunnupe, decided to organise an excursion. That excursion took us to Kainji Dam in today’s Niger State. Each of us paid 30 kobo — three 10 kobo coins for the trip, from our school, Remo Divisional High School in Sagamu, Ogun State. We went safely and returned safely, four days after we set out. If it were now, we would probably have been kidnapped, taken hostage, and ransom demanded for our return. In any case, no teacher would dream of such an excursion today, and no parent would allow his/her child/ward to participate. That is how bad things have turned out.

And talking about how bad things have turned out, one had hoped that the president would tell us a little of the good things he has done or plans to do to make things better. In particular, I expected a response to the threat of a warning strike by the Joint National Public Service Negotiating Council, JNPSNC. The JPNSC is made up of eight public sector unions — the Nigerian Civil Service Union, NCSU; Medical and Health Workers Union, M&HWU; Association of Senior Civil Servants of Nigeria, ASCSN; and National Association of Nigerian Nurses and Midwives, NANNM.

Others are the Amalgamated Union of Public Corporations, Civil Service Technical and Recreational Employees, AUPCTRE; Nigeria Union of Public Service, Reportorial, Secretarial, Data Processors and Allied Workers, NUPSRAW; National Union of Printing, Publishing and Paper Products Workers, NUPPPPROW; and the National Union of Agriculture and Allied Employees, NUAEE. On September 21, the public servants wrote to the president, beseeching him to find ways to bring the price of petrol down to N500, and also demanded a wage award, and commencement of negotiations for a new minimum national wage.

I support the demands of the unions, because it might make government really take action that will benefit all of us, including the insensitive ones in the corridors of power. If somehow petrol can be made to sell for N500, that would be a huge relief to all of us, rich or poor. If a new national minimum wage is negotiated, it means more cash in the bank accounts of workers and increased purchasing power, which will translate to reduced industrial inventory and other benefits to the economy. But there was no word from the president on this issue. Maybe because he had been away from the country in the last three weeks. But if it was really the working vacation we were told it was, it means the president was getting information about the things that needed his attention on a daily basis. Or the threat of strike by public servants did not need the attention of the president? In all, the optics of government’s performance, as it relates to the welfare of the governed, is rather disppointing. The disappointment is even deeper when you consider that we are in election season, a period when normal politicians should be doing anything within their power to please the people. Not so here. The contempt that those in government have for those they are governing is so thick and heavy one can almost feel it the way a porter feels the weight of a load. If not, roads would not remain potholed for months and streets get clogged with garbage for months as is the case in Lagos. Is it because these people know they will be back in office after next year’s elections, whether we vote or not? If that, why not some eye service, which will be better than no service? TGIF.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/the-presidents-disappointing-october-1-message-by-adekunle-adekoya/

posts.title: Giving ex-prisoners another chance
posts.excerpt: The appeal by rehabilitated female ex-inmates for society to reject stigma is a timely reminder that punishment should not become a life sentence after release. The Nigerian Correctional Service (NCoS
posts.content:
The appeal by rehabilitated female ex-inmates for society to reject stigma is a timely reminder that punishment should not become a life sentence after release. The Nigerian Correctional Service (NCoS) itself now has a statutory mandate to reform, rehabilitate and reintegrate offenders, while its programmes include education, vocational training and income generation through farms and industries.

In November 2025, the Service distributed aftercare starter packs to 24 ex-offenders trained in tailoring, laundry, hairdressing, barbing, welding and carpentry, while urging Nigerians to end discrimination. That is the proper peg for a national conversation on second chances. An ex-convict, a former inmate or an ex-offender is a person who has been convicted of an offence and served a sentence imposed by a court. But no one should be permanently defined by their worst chapter of life.

Some are first offenders. Some may have been victims of poverty, manipulation, bad company or circumstance. Some may have been wrongly convicted or suffered miscarriages of justice. Even where guilt is established, a completed sentence should not occasion endless social exclusion or permanent denial of dignity and opportunity. Stigmatisation can defeat the very purpose of correctional reform. If a released person cannot secure employment, accommodation, credit or acceptance because of a past conviction, desperation may deepen and the temptation to return to crime may grow.

The NCoS has itself warned that stigma can frustrate reintegration and increase the risk of reoffending. Compassion is part of crime prevention and safety. Government must urgently strengthen aftercare by providing starter equipment, grants, apprenticeships, counselling, documentation, job-placement partnerships and access to affordable finance. Employers should consider qualified rehabilitated persons on their present abilities, subject to legitimate security requirements.

Communities, religious organisations and civil society should support family reconciliation and mentorship. There should also be structured follow-up for released inmates. The skills acquired behind the walls must not become idle certificates. They include farming and animal production, market gardening, tractor operation and maintenance, carpentry, electrical installation, tailoring, welding, soap making, hairdressing, laundry, barbing and other crafts. Agriculture deserves special attention.

The Correctional Service says it has access to more than 12,263 hectares of arable land, making farming a natural bridge from rehabilitation to food production and self-employment. Released inmates should receive land access, inputs, tools, extension services and market connections. Former inmates themselves can also become ambassadors of rehabilitation. Those who have rebuilt their lives should establish advisory blogs or advocacy platforms offering hope to those behind bars, explaining lawful pathways to early release, education, skills and reintegration.

Rehabilitation is incomplete when society refuses to receive the rehabilitated. A second chance, properly supported, can turn a former inmate from a burden into a worker, entrepreneur, farmer, mentor and productive citizen. The nation should choose restoration over rejection, without abandoning accountability, public safety and dignity.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/giving-ex-prisoners-another-chance/

posts.title: Troops rescue 10 prospective corps members abducted in Imo
posts.excerpt: Troops of the Nigerian Army have neutralised 16 terrorists and recovered weapons after repelling simultaneous attacks in Adamawa. The post Troops rescue 10 prospective corps members abducted in Imo ap
posts.content:
Troops of the Nigerian Army have neutralised 16 terrorists and recovered weapons after repelling simultaneous attacks in Adamawa.

The terrorists attacked troops of 226 Battalion (Motorised) at Garkida, Gombi Local Government Area, and 232 Battalion at Garaha, Hong Local Government Area.

An operational report made available to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) said the attacks occurred at about 1 a.m. on Thursday.

The report said the troops repelled the attacks, forcing the terrorists to flee towards Garkida on motorcycles.

According to the report, the Nigerian Army’s Spartan element subsequently trailed and conducted strikes on the fleeing terrorists, neutralising 16 of them.

“Troops recovered three AK-47 rifles, two pump-action guns, one Dane gun and six AK-47 magazines, alongside some cartridges.

“Troops are currently conducting follow-up operations and reorganising their defensive locations,” the report said.

The report also revealed that troops of Operation UDO KA rescued 10 prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members abducted in Imo.

It said the troops of 34 Artillery Brigade responded to a kidnap incident at Umonuwa village along the Onitsha-Owerri Road in Mbaise Local Government Area at about 6:30 a.m. on Thursday.

The report said the victims were abducted from two commercial buses by suspected kidnappers.

It said troops, in conjunction with personnel of the Nigerian Navy, Nigerian Air Force, Nigeria Police Force and Department of State Services, were trailing the criminals to rescue the remaining victims.

“Meanwhile, troops of Operation WHIRL STROKE responded to a suspected terrorist attack on Gwamagira settlement in Karim Lamido Local Government Area of Taraba.

“The attackers, operating on motorcycles, were engaged by troops and forced to retreat, abandoning rustled cattle.

“The troops recovered the cattle and returned them to their owners, but the attackers had killed one civilian and abducted three others.

“Efforts were ongoing to rescue the abducted victims and apprehend the perpetrators,” it added.

In the North-East, the report said the troops of Sector 3, Operation HADIN KAI, arrested a suspected Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) terrorist at Babbangida, Tarmuwa Local Government Area of Yobe.

It added that the suspect, arrested at about 12:30 p.m. on Sept. 29, claimed to be an Islamic cleric operating in the Sahara area of the Niger Republic.

According to the report, preliminary investigation indicated that he travelled by truck from the Zarmadu-Sahara general area of Niger Republic into Nigeria before proceeding to Borno.

It said the troops recovered a mobile phone, prayer mat, blanket, jacket, slate, detergent and N396,200 from him.

“Also, troops of Sector 4, in conjunction with Rangers and Hybrid Forces, arrested four suspected terrorists during a fighting patrol in parts of Hong Local Government Area of Adamawa,” it added.

The report further revealed that troops of Operation FANSAN YAMMA engaged terrorists along the Kwanar Isa-Shinkafi Road in Isa Local Government Area of Sokoto.

It said the troops forced the terrorists to withdraw and subsequently dominated the area through patrols. (NAN)

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/troops-rescue-10-prospective-corps-members-abducted-in-imo/

posts.title: Tinubu, Akpabio, Govs, Others Grace MKO Documentary Premiere
posts.excerpt: The documentary, MKO, examines Abiola’s rise as a businessman, publisher and politician, his participation in the 1993 presidential election, the annulment of the election by the military government a
posts.content:
President Bola Tinubu on Thursday led top government officials and other dignitaries to the national premiere of MKO, a documentary on the life and political legacy of the late businessman and politician, Moshood Abiola.

The premiere was held at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, formerly the National Theatre, in Iganmu, Lagos, as part of activities marking Nigeria’s 66th Independence Anniversary.

Tinubu attended the event with his wife, Oluremi Tinubu.

Among those present were Senate President Godswill Akpabio, Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, Ogun State Governor Dapo Abiodun, and Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila.

Also at the premiere were Deputy Senate President Jibrin Barau, Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives Benjamin Kalu, Minister of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy Hannatu Musawa, and former Ogun State Governor Segun Osoba.

The documentary was produced and directed by Nigerian-American filmmaker Ose Oyamendan, who said the film was aimed at preserving the story of Abiola and the events surrounding the June 12, 1993 presidential election.

Speaking at the premiere, Oyamendan paid tribute to Tinubu and recalled his involvement in the pro-democracy struggle that followed the annulment of the election.

MKO examines Abiola’s rise as a businessman, publisher, and politician, his participation in the 1993 presidential election, the annulment of the election by the military government, and the pro-democracy struggle that followed.

The filmmaker said Tinubu’s decision to serve as Chief Host of the premiere was significant because of his connection to the events documented in the film.

Oyamendan said the President and others who participated in the struggle against military rule made personal sacrifices in demanding the recognition of the June 12 mandate.

He also reflected on his own experience of the period, having worked as a journalist with Weekend Concord, a newspaper founded by Abiola.

According to him, making the documentary provided an opportunity to revisit the events surrounding Abiola’s political journey and present them to Nigerians who were either too young to remember the period or were born after the events.

MKO examines Abiola’s rise as a businessman, publisher, and politician, his participation in the 1993 presidential election, the annulment of the election by the military government, and the pro-democracy struggle that followed.

The documentary also covers Abiola’s detention and his death in custody in 1998.

It features archival footage and accounts from several people associated with the period, including former military Head of State Ibrahim Babangida, former Head of State Abdulsalami Abubakar, former President Olusegun Obasanjo, Nobel laureate Wole Soyinka, and Abiola’s running mate in the 1993 election, Baba Gana Kingibe.

Former United States ambassador to Nigeria Walter Carrington, former US Deputy Secretary of State Thomas Pickering, former Canadian High Commissioner Gerald Ohlsen and members of the Abiola family also feature in the documentary.

Tinubu was among those featured in the film, reflecting his involvement in the pro-democracy movement during the period.

The 108-minute documentary had its international premiere at the Sheffield International Documentary Festival in the United Kingdom on June 12, 2026, before its national premiere in Lagos.

The film is scheduled to begin its commercial cinema run across Nigeria on Friday, October 2.

The premiere also marked Tinubu’s return to a major public engagement in Nigeria after his four-week working visit to Europe.

The President returned to Lagos on September 29 and was scheduled to participate in activities marking the Independence anniversary.

The event brought together political leaders, members of the creative industry, and personalities connected to Nigeria’s political history to revisit one of the defining episodes in the country’s democratic journey.

Source: https://www.channelstv.com/2026/10/01/tinubu-akpabio-govs-others-grace-mko-documentary-premiere/

posts.title: Independence Day: Nigeria Is Moving From Reform To Prosperity, Tinubu Assures Nigerians
posts.excerpt: The President gave the assurance in his address to the nation on Thursday, October 1, as the country marks its 66th Independence Day anniversary. The post Independence Day: Nigeria Is Moving From Refo
posts.content:
President Bola Tinubu has assured Nigerians that the series of economic reforms will surely lead to better days.

Tinubu gave the assurance in his address to the nation on Thursday, October 1, as the country marks its 66th Independence Day anniversary.

Tinubu noted that the reforms did not weaken the economy as widely believed. He assured that the promises he made to Nigerians are finally being fulfilled.

“When this Administration assumed office, we resolved to do things differently. We chose to excise the cancer. The reforms that followed were difficult. The side effects were real. Yet, we must never confuse the medicine with the disease.

“Our reforms did not create the weaknesses in our economy. They confronted them. Now, as certain influential but regressive voices would have us abandon the treatment and return ourselves to the abuse of addictive subsidies, we must resist their siren song. We must remember why we began this journey and how far we have already come.

“Three and a half years later, the evidence that Nigeria’s economic outlook has improved is undeniable. Our economy has grown by over 4 per cent this year. Both oil and non-oil sectors have contributed to the renewed period of stable growth.”

The President noted that oil theft in producing countries has dropped; likewise, inflation has fallen “substantially”.

“Oil theft is down. Inflation has fallen substantially from its peak. Our foreign reserves have been rebuilt.

“Our foreign exchange market has stabilised, and in 2025 this country recorded its highest revenue from non-oil exports in its history, exceeding $6 billion. This is real money being made by real Nigerian businesses.

“These are not idle claims. International observers, journalists, NGOs and multilateral institutions can see the change. Each has concluded that our reforms have strengthened Nigeria’s economic stability and resilience. The private sector has long since delivered its verdict, and foreign direct investment continues to rise each year.”

He emphasised that the country had reached a turning point of prosperity.

“The emergency treatment is over. The foundation has been repaired. The central economic task before us has changed. For three years, our overriding purpose was to correct our nation’s course.

“Now, our purpose is simple: shared and widespread prosperity.

“When I speak of prosperity, I do not speak merely of a larger economy, abstract numbers or better statistics. I mean something much more personal.

“I mean a Nigeria in which the farmer can cultivate his land safely, produce more at lower cost, and earn a decent return for his labour.

“A Nigeria in which factories have reliable power, businesses can obtain credit, and young people can find productive work.

“A Nigeria in which food and transportation are affordable, education is within reach, and hard-working families can look towards the future with confidence”, he added.

The President reeled out Nigeria’s journey after Independence 66 years ago and the resilience of Nigerians through thick and thin.

“Sixty-six years ago today, our flag was raised, for the first time, over a free and sovereign nation. Since then, we have journeyed together as one nation, bound by our collective trust in the great promise of Nigeria: that a country of our size, our bountiful resources, our cultural diversity and, above all, our extraordinary people can build a giant in Africa; that in this blessed and fertile land we can build a united, strong and prosperous nation; a land of regional authority and global consequence.

“Our journey has not always been easy. In truth, it has generally been too hard for too many. We have known moments of great hope and periods of profound disappointment.

“We have endured war, military rule, economic crises, insecurity, and political upheaval. Yet through it all, Nigeria, with the indomitable spirit of its people, has endured.

“It has endured through the efforts of the farmer who rises before dawn to work his land. The trader who opens her shop each morning, hopeful for a productive day.

“The teacher who believes in the children entrusted to her care and the young entrepreneur who refuses to surrender ambition to circumstance. We are grateful for the men and women of our Armed Forces and security services who place themselves in harm’s way so that the rest of us may live in peace.

He thanked Nigerians for believing in the country, adding that the economy is on the right trajectory.

“Through every difficulty, generations of Nigerians have continued to believe in one thing: that this country of ours will be better.

“This faith, which sustains us all, is the inheritance of independence.

“Our founding fathers did not struggle merely for a flag, an anthem or a place among the nations of the world. Independence carried a larger promise: that Nigerians would have the freedom to shape their own destiny and build a nation capable of providing opportunity, dignity and a better life for its people.

“Sixty-six years later, Almighty God has made it our responsibility to deliver that promise.

“Today, as we celebrate our independence, we must speak honestly about the journey so far, the choices we made, and the country we are determined to build from here”, he added.

Source: https://www.channelstv.com/2026/10/01/independence-day-nigeria-is-moving-from-reform-to-prosperity-tinubu-assures-nigerians/

posts.title: Hasan Piker vows he will pressure James Talarico to govern as a leftist, not a moderate
posts.excerpt: Hasan Piker vowed to pressure James Talarico to govern as a leftist if elected, not a moderate Democrat, raising questions about the Texas Senate race.
posts.content:
Left-wing streamer Hasan Piker vowed Wednesday that he would push Democratic Texas Senate candidate James Talarico to govern as a leftist rather than a moderate Democrat if Talarico was elected.

"Hopefully after James Talarico wins, we’ve got to hold him to account," Piker said during a campus event at the University of Texas at Austin. "We've got to make sure that he doesn’t become another, ‘do nothing Democrat’ ‘business as usual’ and we've got to keep up that pressure."

"We have to remind him that we are the force that backed him both early on," he continued. "We are the force that allowed him to win this seat of power and if he wants to maintain it, he’s got to play ball. Right?"

"And, that’s good to build a resilient movement anyway, so job’s not done even after he wins," Piker added. "So, just remember that, and you know, remember that we do hold a lot of power in mass organizing."

UNIVERSITY EVENT WITH HASAN PIKER IN TEXAS DRAWS BACKLASH FROM BOTH SIDES OF THE AISLE

Fox News Digital reached out to Talarico's campaign for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

Talarico has moderated his rhetoric during his run for Senate, disavowing some of his past statements.

Piker, an internet personality popular on the Twitch platform, has become a major player in left-wing politics in recent years and has a long history of controversial comments, ranging from saying "America deserved 9/11" to praising an official in New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's administration after a clip showed her saying she wanted to "impoverish the White middle-class."

Proximity to Piker has been a lightning rod for Democrats. Since the left-wing streamer appeared with Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed on the campaign trail, the candidate repeatedly tried to shrug off Piker’s controversial remarks.

TALARICO’S ‘PROUD CAPITALIST’ ABOUT-FACE COLLIDES WITH RESURFACED CALL TO ‘DISMANTLE’ CAPITALISM

Jesse Arm, a Manhattan Institute vice president and pollster from Michigan, wondered whether Talarico’s avowed moderation will stick.

"Talarico is wise to acknowledge, in effect, that many of his past comments on key policy questions were absurd, but Texans have reason to wonder whether his convictions have changed or merely his political incentives," he told Fox News Digital. "If he is as wise a lawmaker as he is a crafty politician, he will govern as the more moderate liberal he currently purports to be."

"Hasan Piker’s faction can certainly exert pressure," he added. "And I would expect it to push Talarico back toward his earlier, more radical positions on policing, gender, race, immigration, and energy."

A better indicator, he argued, was the fact that genuinely moderate Democrats have been driven out of office.

"We cannot know how Talarico would govern, but the broader Democratic Party gives us plenty of reason for skepticism: Joe Manchin and Kyrsten Sinema were driven out, and John Fetterman faces endless hostility for breaking with its activist orthodoxy," he said. "Governing as a genuine moderate would give Talarico a better chance of keeping a Texas Senate seat beyond an unusually favorable Democratic election cycle, but Piker is already openly demanding that he ‘play ball’ with the far left."

Arm suggested that Piker might actually be making a tactical mistake by suggesting Democrats are only campaigning as moderates, but will govern like leftists.

"Above perhaps all else, this episode exposes Piker’s political stupidity: publicly suggesting that a candidate’s moderation is temporary and that radicals will call the shots threatens the very victory he claims to want," Arm said. "In truth, I suspect Piker would prefer an election cycle in which Talarico comes up short but El-Sayed gets across the finish line. That would help advance Piker’s position that radicalism is the only viable path forward for the Democratic Party."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Former Democratic advisor Dan Turrentine suggested that Piker has vastly overestimated his importance both now and after the election.

"Hasan Piker is living in fantasy world," he said. "He did not elect Talarico in the primary. Progressives were split, with many going for Jasmine Crockett."

"If Talarico wins the general, it will be because he appealed to a significant number of R’s in a state Trump won by 14% in ’24," Turrentine continued. "If Talarico wins, it will be in spite of Piker, not because of him."

"Same, if they win, for Roy Cooper in NC, Josh Turek in IA, Mary Peltola in AK, and Sherrod Brown in OH," he added. "The Senate majority runs through the middle of the electorate, not Twitch."

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/media/hasan-piker-vows-he-pressure-james-talarico-govern-leftist-not-moderate

posts.title: College professor accused of sending explicit Snapchat messages in child solicitation case: sheriff's office
posts.excerpt: Aaron Wood, a Texas professor, allegedly sent sexually explicit photos and messages online to an undercover Florida officer he believed was a 14-year-old boy.
posts.content:
Texas officials last week arrested a Dallas-area community college professor accused of sending sexually explicit photos and messages online to an individual he believed was a 14-year-old boy.

Aaron Wood, 34, who taught drama for two years at North Central Texas College (NCTC), allegedly sent the messages on Snapchat to an undercover agent in Florida May 22.

The Denton County Sheriff’s Office arrested Wood Friday and charged him with solicitation of a minor via computer, according to county records.

The school confirmed his arrest in a statement, saying he was no longer employed as of Monday.

FORMER TEXAS HIGH SCHOOL TEACHER ARRESTED AFTER PROBE INTO INAPPROPRIATE STUDENT RELATIONSHIP

NCTC added the alleged offense did not involve any school staff or students.

"To our knowledge, the alleged offense does not involve NCTC, its students or staff," the college said. "We can verify that he has had no contact with NCTC students, faculty or staff since his arrest on September 25, 2026."

According to an arrest affidavit, Wood allegedly engaged in an online conversation on Snapchat with an undercover officer from the Orange County Sheriff’s Office in Florida, FOX 4 Dallas reported.

During their interaction, Wood reportedly told the undercover officer he teaches students around the same age as the person he believed he was speaking with.

FLORIDA MIDDLE SCHOOL TEACHER ADMITS TO YEARS OF 'INAPPROPRIATE' CONVERSATIONS WITH FORMER STUDENT: DEPUTIES

When asked about his students, Wood allegedly told the officer he had "been into a few over the years" and that he was nervous but still interested in chatting with the undercover officer.

The affidavit says Wood sent a picture of male genitals, along with other sexually explicit messages, to the officer and asked to see theirs, FOX 4 reported.

Authorities tracked Wood through the IP address used during the interaction, which led them to an apartment in Denton.

FORMER NORTH TEXAS POLICE OFFICER GIVEN THREE LIFE SENTENCES FOR CHILD PORNOGRAPHY, SOLICITATION OF MINOR

The affidavit noted that the Orange County Sheriff’s Office had probable cause to charge Wood with transmission of harmful material to minors and unlawful use of a two-way communication device, FOX 4 reported.

While the allegations reportedly did not involve any NCTC students, the school emphasized that "the safety of our students and staff are of the utmost importance and concern."

Fox News Digital reached out to NCTC for additional information.

posts.title: GREGG JARRETT: My mother’s advice led me to the career of a lifetime
posts.excerpt: Former trial lawyer Gregg Jarrett reflects on leaving his legal career behind and finding purpose during nearly 25 years at the network's news operation.
posts.content:
Decades ago, when I was agonizing over the decision to forsake my profession as a trial lawyer to pursue a far riskier and more uncertain career in television news, my mother offered sage advice. "The worst thing you can do is choose the easy course and be haunted by regret over what might have been."

I embraced her counsel, realizing that the only thing scarier than change is the absence of imagination. I quit my secure and lucrative job as an attorney in San Francisco and moved forward into the unknown. Fortunately, I was too naive to understand that the chances of success were remote.

I discovered that change hurts. It can be difficult and discouraging. But the fear of failure forced me to persevere. My early ventures up the ladder from local news channels to larger network operations felt like Churchill’s "wilderness years." It was a long slog in search of advancement and fulfillment. Self-doubt was always hovering nearby.

DANA PERINO: THE UNTOLD STORY OF THE REMARKABLE PEOPLE WHO MAKE FOX NEWS POSSIBLE

But all of that vanished when I landed at Fox News nearly a quarter of a century ago. I have been grateful ever since to have played a small role in a network that has changed the face of television news for the better.

I could tell at the outset that the people at Fox were different. They were dedicated and passionate. The common denominator was an unwavering commitment to excellence. We supported one another.

But the heart and soul of our network are the viewers themselves. They watch with consistency because they trust what they see and hear. They feel engaged. In turn, those of us on air and the many people behind the scenes do our level best to maintain that trust by providing the highest-quality news and information available.

As a 24-hour news operation, that level of devotion and diligence is not easy to sustain. Yet I am consistently impressed by the energy, creativity, and intelligence that my colleagues bring to the on-air product every hour of every day. They are tireless and enthusiastic even when they have every right not to be. Those are rare qualities.

MARTHA MACCALLUM: AFTER 22 YEARS, HERE'S WHY I'M GRATEFUL TO CALL FOX HOME

During my many years at Fox, I have covered a multitude of stories—the War on Terror, hurricanes, disasters, presidential elections, the dot-com crash, financial calamities, social upheavals, cultural controversies, criminal trials, Supreme Court decisions, and the COVID-19 pandemic, to name a few.

Fox never said "no" when I wanted to venture beyond the newsroom. They encouraged it.

Having previously reported from conflict zones in the Middle East, I volunteered in 2003 as a correspondent during the Iraq War. For a time, I was embedded with the 3rd Infantry Division. These were courageous young soldiers who took good care of me. The experience gave me a renewed respect and admiration for our nation’s military. There are none better anywhere.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

The world has changed dramatically since I first stepped into the Fox studios back in 2002. America has become more digital, diverse, and technologically advanced. Smartphones, e-commerce, social media, cloud computing, and now AI have transformed our lives. The Dow Jones Industrial Average hovered around 10,000 back then. It now exceeds 50,000.

In my time at Fox News, I have served as an anchor, reporter, documentary host, opinion columnist, and, most recently, legal analyst for the network. I penned four books along the way. I have grown and evolved in ways that I never imagined. Fox made that possible. And I’ve enjoyed every minute of it.

It has certainly been a different life than what I envisioned as a young man exiting law school so long ago. Far more rewarding. During the journey, I learned some valuable lessons. Sometimes it pays to take a chance. And to listen to your mother.

So, may I offer my sincere thanks to Fox News and a hearty congratulations on its 30th anniversary!

CLICK HERE TO READ MORE FROM GREGG JARRETT

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/opinion/gregg-jarrett-mothers-advice-led-career-lifetime

posts.title: DOE employee charged with trying to aid Iran-backed Houthis, feds say
posts.excerpt: Ashton Hamed Ellaboudy allegedly used his electrical engineering expertise in an attempt to aid Houthi communications, drones and homemade explosives production.
posts.content:
A U.S. Department of Energy worker from Richland, Washington, was arrested Thursday and charged with attempting to provide "material support" to the Iran-backed Houthis, according to the Department of Justice (DOJ).

Ashton Hamed Ellaboudy, 51, is accused of attempting to use his electrical engineering knowledge and background to support the terrorist group in improving its mobile communications infrastructure, secure components for drones as well as chemicals for homemade explosives.

"As alleged, a U.S. government employee traveled overseas and used his specialized expertise in an attempt to aid the Houthis, a designated Foreign Terrorist Organization backed by Iran," Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A. Eisenberg said in a statement.

"Additionally, Ellaboudy acquired materials for the construction of explosive material and drones capable of delivering these explosives. These allegations are so deeply disturbing that they almost defy imagination."

IRAN’S PROXY WAR HAS CROSSED OCEANS AND IS NOW KNOCKING ON AMERICA’S DOOR

Federal authorities took Ellaboudy into custody after an investigation by the FBI’s Inland Northwest Joint Terrorism Task Force.

According to court records, Ellaboudy first attracted the FBI’s attention after he allegedly bought precursor chemicals, or starting ingredients, and components often used in homemade explosives, as well as parts to make drones.

The DOJ said that, in 2024, Ellaboudy took sick leave from his Department of Energy job and said he had been exposed to highly concentrated nitric acid, a key chemical compound used in explosive manufacturing.

FBI OFFERS $200K REWARD FOR FORMER AIR FORCE INTELLIGENCE AGENT ACCUSED OF SPYING FOR IRAN

In 2025, prosecutors allege, Ellaboudy used an official passport from his previous role with the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers to travel from Washington state to Oman.

He then crossed into Yemen. After returning to the U.S., Ellaboudy allegedly told border officers his trip was authorized government business.

Investigators also said Ellaboudy advised an undercover FBI confidential human source posing as a representative of a Houthi colonel.

For the Houthis, Ellaboudy allegedly tested solar generators, modified power systems, created circuit schematics and provided support to the group’s communications, the statement said.

NAVY VETERAN AMONG TRIO WHO ALLEGEDLY WANTED TO BEHEAD SOLDIER AND FUND ISIS DRONE ATTACKS ON AMERICANS

"This individual allegedly betrayed the U.S. and attempted to aid the Houthis, a designated foreign terrorist organization, but thanks to the work of the men and women of the FBI, his actions were detected, and he is now in custody," Assistant Director Jarod Brown of the FBI’s Counterterrorism Division said.

Officials also confirmed Ellaboudy's alleged activities did not target local nuclear sites.

"This matter did not involve an attempt to harm the Hanford Site or its workforce, and at no time was there a threat to the safety or security of the site," said Ray Geimer, office manager of the Department of Energy Hanford Field Office.

Ellaboudy faces a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison if convicted.

He is scheduled to make his initial court appearance before a federal magistrate judge at 11 a.m. Oct. 2 in Richland, according to the Justice Department.

posts.title: Trump admin wants to require tax filers to disclose citizenship status to IRS
posts.excerpt: A Trump administration proposal would require tax filers to certify their immigration status to the IRS, which critics argue could be used as a tool for immigration enforcement.
posts.content:
The Trump administration has proposed requiring U.S. taxpayers to disclose their citizenship and work authorization status to the IRS on the annual tax form that nearly all workers file each year.

The administration claims the proposed requirement would help federal officials stop illegal migrants from collecting federal benefits they are not eligible for, which officials argue could save taxpayers up to $2 billion.

The IRS posted its draft 1040 form for 2026 in late August, which includes the question, "At the time you file your return, are you, and your spouse if filing jointly, a U.S. citizen, U.S. national, or an alien lawfully authorized to work in the U.S.?" The form has "Yes" and "No" checkboxes for both the filer and their spouse.

A draft of a second form, Schedule 3-A, which is used to claim refundable tax credits, features a similar question.

APPEALS COURT UPHOLDS ORDER BLOCKING IRS FROM SHARING TAXPAYER DATA WITH ICE

Under the proposal, every tax filer must certify their immigration or citizenship status to the IRS under penalty of law to file their return.

The Treasury Department said the new question aims to keep illegal migrants from taking advantage of refundable tax credits like the Earned Income Tax Credit or the Additional Child Tax Credit, that low- and middle-income workers and families may qualify for and that often result in a refund for eligible taxpayers.

The information collected will be "subject to a variety of privacy, disclosure and other legal protections," a Treasury official said in a statement without disclosing whether the information would be shared with federal immigration enforcement to target a person for arrest and deportation.

While illegal migrants are not authorized to live and work in the U.S., they still do pay taxes. For example, illegal migrants typically pay into Social Security but generally cannot collect Social Security benefits unless they later become eligible under federal law.

In 2024, the National Taxpayer Advocate found 3.8 million tax returns where a taxpayer used an Individual Tax Identification Number, or ITIN. An ITIN can be issued for multiple purposes, but undocumented workers who cannot obtain a Social Security number are among the people who use them.

According to IRS data, taxpayers who filed those nearly 4 million returns paid $14.4 billion in income taxes and $6.5 billion in Social Security and Medicare taxes.

A valid Social Security Number is required to qualify for the Earned Income Tax Credit, while workers with only an ITIN do not qualify. The IRS checks Social Security Numbers against Social Security Administration records for each claim of the Earned Income Tax Credit.

Illegal migrants are generally not eligible for federal benefits. Eligibility for refundable tax credits depends on federal tax law and immigration status. Current law generally requires a valid Social Security number for the Earned Income Tax Credit, while eligibility for the Additional Child Tax Credit varies based on statutory requirements. The Trump administration's proposal would further limit eligibility by applying standards under the Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act to certain refundable tax credits.

However, some migrants in the U.S. who are currently for some of these credits would not be eligible under the new policy, such as people covered under the Obama administration's Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals, those with temporary protected status and temporary workers in the country under H1-B visas.

The Trump administration claims that the Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act, which governs who is eligible for benefit programs, should also be applied to refundable tax credits.

A research paper published this week estimates that 671,000 people, including 309,000 children, would lose the Earned Income Tax Credit under this proposal. Another 1.1 million people, including 574,000 children, would lose the Additional Child Tax Credit.

Most of the children who would lose eligibility to these credits are U.S. citizens due to at least one of their parents' citizenship or immigration status, according to the researchers at Boston University, Columbia University and the Institute on Taxation and Economic Policy.

Critics of the new policy view it as a new checkbox that gives the federal government even more information on taxpayers. Illegal migrants would face a complicated choice to either declare on a tax return that they are unlawfully in the U.S., which could potentially make them a target for immigration-related arrests, or lie on the return, which is a felony.

Some migrants may opt for a third option and stop filing their taxes altogether.

"It could be used as an immigration enforcement tool and that is probably the reason why they are doing this," David Bier, director of immigration studies at the libertarian-leaning Cato Institute, told The Associated Press.

TRUMP ADMIN SCORES COURT WIN TO END DEPORTATION PROTECTIONS FOR ETHIOPIAN MIGRANTS

"It’s dragging the IRS into this administration’s immigration policies," said Nina Olson, executive director for the Center for Taxpayer Rights.

The Trump administration has previously attempted to use the IRS to carry out its immigration agenda.

Last year, the Treasury Department agreed to share confidential taxpayer information of migrants with Immigration and Customs Enforcement to help the agency identify people for deportation.

The data-sharing agreement was blocked by a federal judge, ruling that it violated federal taxpayer privacy laws. But before it was stopped, the IRS had already given ICE the addresses of 47,000 people.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/politics/trump-admin-wants-require-tax-filers-disclose-citizenship-status-irs

posts.title: Browns’ late field goal spoils Aaron Rodgers’ Thursday night finale, seals Cleveland's third straight win
posts.excerpt: Aaron Rodgers' final Thursday night football game ended with the Cleveland Browns extending their seven-game winning streak over the Steelers.
posts.content:
Future Pro Football Hall of Famer Aaron Rodgers’ NFL farewell tour continued Thursday night as the Pittsburgh Steelers faced the Cleveland Browns in what was scheduled to be his final Thursday night game.

The ending was not what Rodgers likely envisioned, as the Browns continued their strong start to the season with a victory over their AFC North rivals. Deshaun Watson, an early NFL comeback of the year candidate, was efficient, throwing for 268 yards and a touchdown.

Rodgers entered the night one victory shy of tying Tom Brady’s record of 14 Thursday night wins, while Pittsburgh’s road struggles against AFC North opponents continued as the Steelers fell to 0-10 in such games.

DESHAUN WATSON IS BEGINNING TO CRAFT ONE OF THE MOST IMPROBABLE COMEBACK STORIES IN SPORTS HISTORY

Rodgers finished with 299 passing yards, three touchdowns and two interceptions in Pittsburgh’s 27-24 loss.

After the Steelers’ eight-play, 80-yard fourth-quarter drive tied the game at 24, the Browns answered with a seven-play possession of their own. Watson moved Cleveland into field-goal range before Andre Szmyt drilled a 56-yard kick to give the Browns a 27-24 lead.

JAYDEN DANIELS DOES NOT DISMISS PLAYING SUNDAY AGAINST THE COLTS IN LONDON AFTER UGLY ELBOW DISLOCATION INJURY

Rodgers entered Thursday with a 13-7 record in Thursday Night games. The 27-24 loss dropped him to 13-8. Steelers coach Mike McCarthy is 11-5 on Thursday nights, including wins in four of his past five games.

Thursday night also marked the 150th meeting of all-time between the rivals, which are separated by only 135 miles.

"I just suck it up for those three hours and then know you get a reward on the back end. I think it’s part of the game now because of the money that’s in it. I think I’m just excited about the weekend," Rodgers told reporters before Thursday night’s game.

The Browns entered Week 4 with a 2-1 record for the first time since 2023. Thursday’s victory moved Cleveland into first place in the AFC North.

Both the Browns and Steelers will have extra rest before Cleveland visits the New York Jets in Week 5. The Steelers will return home to host the Indianapolis Colts on Oct. 11.

posts.title: Season's over: Caitlin Clark leaves it all on court with bloody mouth as Fever fall in Game 3
posts.excerpt: Caitlin Clark scored 18 points but the Indiana Fever fell 94-83 to A'ja Wilson's 36-point explosion in a decisive Game 3 elimination in Las Vegas.
posts.content:
It was win-or-go-home for Caitlin Clark, and she went down swinging.

The season came to an end for Clark and the Indiana Fever with a 94-83 loss to A'ja Wilson and the reigning champion Las Vegas Aces in Thursday's decisive Game 3.

Wilson led the charge with 36 points in the winning effort, dropping 21 by halftime.

The Fever kept it within single digits until the final two minutes, but the shots just didn't fall down the stretch. Clark — the AP Comeback Player of the Year — finished with 18 points on 6-of-18 shooting.

Still, Indiana fought hard to save their season against the reigning champs, headlined by Clark's raw grit.

Down 82-77 in the fourth quarter with 3:16 remaining, Clark took a sharp elbow to the face from Jewell Loyd.

With her mouth bleeding profusely, she quickly ran back onto the court, fiercely fighting back against head coach Stephanie White and game officials just to stay on the floor.

Drama was at a fever pitch coming into Thursday's decisive game in Vegas.

A'ja Wilson's technical foul in Game 2 was the talk of the town, largely overshadowing Caitlin Clark's historic postseason milestones.

CAITLIN CLARK'S TECHNICAL FOUL SPARKS FURIOUS RALLY AS FEVER AVOID ELIMINATION AGAINST ACES

Aces coach Becky Hammon was asked about the Wilson aftermath, which saw her step over and beyond the sideline to confront a fan in the stands. Though clear arguments were made for a suspension, the WNBA made a business decision, looking the other way to leave Wilson untouched by the incident.

Speaking on Thursday, Hammon doubled down on her support for her superstar:

WNBA REVEALS WHY A'JA WILSON WAS NOT EJECTED FOR APPROACHING FEVER FAN DURING PLAYOFF GAME

"I think you saw A'ja get pushed and shoved and there was no response. So there just comes a certain point where a lot of variables come into the exchange that happened the other night.

"I stand 10 toes down with the character of A'ja Wilson. And it's like if someone said, 'hey, your brother went and did something.' Like, no, I know the person in the situation, so I trust that person in any situation. And she'll be great tonight. I have no doubt."

The biggest loser in all of this? Fever head coach Stephanie White.

In her second season back in Indiana, White proved she's just a corporate stooge when things get ugly. While opponents treated Caitlin Clark and Sophie Cunningham like punching bags, White hid behind spineless PR fluff instead of defending her stars.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

In a league that constantly ignores dirty play against its top draw, White refused to go to bat for her team, showing a complete lack of backbone when her players needed a fighter on the bench.

FEVER COACH STEPHANIE WHITE LAUNCHES FIERY DEFENSE OF HERSELF AFTER SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM HIT

Despite the coaching headaches, the Fever roster still had enough talent to finish 28-16 as the sixth seed.

In what could be her final game for Indiana, guard Sophie Cunningham played 24 minutes, scoring just five points (2-of-4 FG). Her biggest impact this season went far beyond the score, gaining widespread notoriety for standing firm for her values off the court.

The Fever played out their final minutes in frustration, knowing a hard-fought year was coming to an end.

Across the three-game series, Clark averaged 20.0 points, 9.7 assists and 4.0 rebounds per game.

That came on the heels of a dominant Year 3 regular season where she averaged 22.3 points, 8.3 assists, and 4.0 rebounds per game. Still searching for her first career playoff series win, Clark has already set the stage for a full-on revenge tour in Year 4.

posts.title: Braves dominate Phillies with big home runs to set up huge NLDS against Los Angeles Dodgers
posts.excerpt: Michael Harris II's three-run homer sparked the Atlanta Braves to a game three win over the Philadelphia Phillies at Truist Park on Thursday.
posts.content:
While the three other wild card series ended in two-game sweeps, the matchup between the Atlanta Braves and Philadelphia Phillies has delivered exceptional postseason drama.

In game one, the Braves trailed late while trying to mount a comeback against typically dominant closer Jhoan Duran. With two outs in the bottom of the 8th down 3-2, third baseman Austin Riley delivered, launching a game-changing homer to give Atlanta a 5-3 lead. Raisel Iglesias closed it out to give them a 1-0 series lead.

Philadelphia turned the tables in game two, just when it seemed like the Braves would close out the sweep. With the score tied at one, Bryce Harper misplayed a routine fly ball to right field in the bottom of the 7th, allowing a run to score and setting up another to come in on a sacrifice fly. In the 8th, he made up for it. After Kyle Schwarber demolished a ball to make it 3-2, Harper followed it up with one of his own to tie it at 3. Alec Bohm broke the tie in the 10th, and Andrew Painter finished out the save for Philly.

PHILLIES AND BRAVES REACH WILD CARD GAME 3 AFTER TWO MASTERPIECE CONTESTS NO OTHER SERIES MATCHED

The late-inning heroics set up a winner-take-all game three back at Truist Park on Thursday night. Division rivals. Primetime. Win or go home. Packed house. That's what playoff baseball is all about. And the Braves stars made sure the home fans would go home happy.

Philadelphia started the game at a bit of a disadvantage thanks to their late-season pitching plans. Because the Arizona Diamondbacks refused to exit the wild card race, the Phillies were forced to start Zack Wheeler on Sunday afternoon and punch their ticket to the postseason. While it worked to send them to Atlanta, that put Wheeler on short rest for Thursday's must-win game three.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Instead, the Phillies turned to veteran starter Aaron Nola, coming off the worst season of his career but on more rest than Wheeler. In the first inning, it backfired. After back-to-back walks to Ronald Acuna Jr. and Matt Olson, Michael Harris II hit a three-run homer to right center field to put Atlanta up 3-0 in the blink of an eye.

Backing themselves into a corner with their pitching options, Atlanta turned to Ray Kerr, a reliever with just 18 regular season innings this year, to open the game against the powerful Phillies lineup. And because baseball remains baseball and thus unpredictable, Kerr went 3.1 innings with just one hit, one walk, two strikeouts, and no runs allowed.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

Grant Holmes and a parade of relievers helped keep the Phillies mostly at bay heading into the middle innings, when Ozzie Albies gave Atlanta some breathing room with a two-run homer off Wheeler, pitching in relief.

The Phillies put two runners in scoring position with one out in the 6th, but could only bring in a single run on an Alec Bohm ground out. Matt Olson got it right back with a solo homer in the 7th, to extend the lead to 6-1. Philly clawed back a run on a Trea Turner sac fly in the 8th, and Braves manager Walt Weiss, instead of turning to closer Raisel Iglesias, brought in superstar starter Chris Sale to close it out.

Atlanta's win sets up a clash of the titans against the defending champion Los Angeles Dodgers in the NLDS, with star-studded lineups and pitching staffs on both sides. LA, at first glance, has the advantage thanks to the rest a first-round bye provides.

The Dodgers will be able to set up the rotation the way they'd prefer, enjoy a fully rested bullpen, while the extra time off allowed injured players like Shohei Ohtani to heal ahead of the series. On the other hand, Atlanta has played three straight competitive games in intense, playoff environments. Going from 0–100 has proven challenging for some teams coming off bye weeks, which might negate some of LA's advantage.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Still, Atlanta will have to piece together a pitching plan for the first game of the series. Sale started game one of the wild card series, but coming in to close out game three negates any chance of pitching on short rest on Saturday. Tyler Mahle pitched on Wednesday, which would seem to knock him out until game three at the earliest. Grant Holmes pitched two innings on Thursday, putting his availability in doubt.

But the Braves' offense remains dangerous thanks to star-level performance and depth with Olson, Riley, Albies, Acuna, Harris, and Drake Baldwin. Iglesias had a very good season at the back of the bullpen, and Sale is a force of nature.

LA's offense has surprisingly struggled this year, but their rotation is outstanding, to say the least. Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, and Tyler Glasnow are as good as anyone.

Should be must-see TV.

posts.title: Lawyers, experts urge Tennessee governor to commute Christa Pike’s sentence after botched execution
posts.excerpt: Christa Pike survived two doses of pentobarbital in a botched Tennessee execution, and her lawyers now urge Gov. Bill Lee to commute her death sentence.
posts.content:
Christa Pike's lawyers are calling on Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee to commute her death sentence to life in prison after she remained alive following two doses of lethal injection drugs in what one death penalty expert described as an unprecedented event.

Pike, who was sentenced to death for a 1995 murder of a classmate, was rushed to a hospital Wednesday night after surviving her planned execution. Her lawyers said on Thursday that she remains in critical condition and is receiving "lifesaving medical care."

"We don’t have a sense of her prognosis or much update on her health at the moment," attorney Randy Spivey said during a news conference. "But we know she is alive right now."

The botched execution prompted Lee to halt any further efforts to carry out Pike's execution and the state’s other execution scheduled this year. He also ordered a third-party review into Pike's execution, which he called "deeply disturbing."

CHRISTA PIKE'S ATTORNEYS SAY SHE'S IN CRITICAL CONDITION AFTER BOTCHED LETHAL INJECTIONS

Pike's lawyers are now calling for her death sentence to be commuted.

Her lawyers filed an emergency motion with the Tennessee Supreme Court seeking to immediately halt and stay the execution, noting that she was in "unnecessary agony" and arguing that putting her through another attempted execution violated her right to be put to death without cruel and unusual punishment.

Death Penalty Information Center Executive Director Robin Maher, who called the failed execution "completely unprecedented," also urged the governor to commute Pike's sentence.

"Given the experience that Christa Pike went through last night, after a childhood and young adulthood that was full of gender based violence and abuse, it would be irresponsible for state officials to put her through another attempt at execution. I really hope that in light of what she's experienced, that the governor will decide to commute her sentence to a life in prison and not put her through another torturous experience in the execution chamber," Maher told Fox News Digital.

Before the planned execution, about 25,000 people had signed a petition to Lee asking him to commute Pike's death sentence to life in prison.

An appeals court had halted her execution early on Wednesday, but the U.S. Supreme Court overturned that stay hours later to clear the way for her to be put to death.

Pike, 50, would have been the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than 200 years. She would have been the 30th person executed in the U.S. this year, driven largely by Florida's record increase in inmates put to death since 2025.

Since the Supreme Court resumed the death penalty in 1976, only 18 women have been executed in the U.S., making up about 1% of all executions in the country.

This was the second time this year that Tennessee had a failed execution. In May, Tony Carruthers, who was convicted of kidnapping and murdering three people in 1994, was not executed because officials could not find a suitable vein for an IV line, so the drugs were not administered. Multiple states have previously paused executions after cases of officials being unable to find a suitable vein for an IV line.

In 2024, Tennessee switched from a three-drug series to a single drug, pentobarbital, for lethal injections. About two years earlier, the state abruptly halted the execution of Oscar Smith, who was convicted of first-degree murder, and acknowledged it had failed to ensure its lethal injection drugs had been tested properly. He was eventually put to death by lethal injection last year.

Several others have survived medical problems linked to a failure to access a vein to administer lethal injection drugs, but no one had stayed alive after receiving the drugs until Pike on Wednesday.

"This, unfortunately, is not the first time that Tennessee officials have botched an execution. There is really a quite shameful history in Tennessee of executions going wrong, although Christa Pikes really stands out. There's never been someone who has received lethal doses of execution drugs and survived until last night. This is a completely unprecedented event, even in the context of Tennessee's other botched executions," Maher said.

The Death Penalty Information Center lists 65 botched executions across the U.S. in the modern era.

In the execution chamber, Pike said she was at peace and "ready to be free."

"This is a happy day," she said.

But she remained awake, and even complained about a feeling in her arm. Witnesses reported that Pike complained of pain in her arm and remained conscious after the first dose.

An hour after officials first raised the curtains, witnesses said that a second dose of pentobarbital was administered. Pike could still be heard snoring behind a closed curtain until the microphone was cut off nearly 30 minutes later.

WHAT TO KNOW ABOUT PENTOBARBITAL AFTER DEATH ROW INMATE SURVIVES 2 LETHAL INJECTION DOSES

Pike, who was 18 at the time of the crime, and her then-17-year-old boyfriend Tadaryl Shipp, were convicted of the fatal stabbing of a classmate, 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer. Shipp was sentenced to life in prison with the possibility of parole, as he was a minor and not eligible for the death penalty.

The third defendant, then-18-year-old Shadolla Peterson, who acted as a lookout while her two friends carried out the attack, testified for the state and avoided the death penalty.

Pike did not dispute that she helped kill Slemmer, but supporters argued that her mental illness and allegations of severe sexual abuse when she was young should be considered. She was diagnosed with bipolar disorder and post-traumatic stress disorder after the killing.

"I was a mentally ill 18-year-old kid. It took me numerous years to even realize the gravity of what I’d done," she previously said. "It sickens me now to think I had the ability to commit such a crime."

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/us/lawyers-experts-urge-tennessee-governor-commute-christa-pikes-sentence-botched-execution

posts.title: Plateau group kicks against state of emergency suggestion
posts.excerpt: A good governance advocacy group, One Plateau, One Voice, has kicked against suggestions that a state of emergency should be imposed on the state due to the recurring violent attacks and killings for
posts.content:
A good governance advocacy group, One Plateau, One Voice, has kicked against suggestions that a state of emergency should be imposed on the state due to the recurring violent attacks and killings for over two decades.

The calls were made by a group known as the Hausa-Fulani Unity in a video shared on social media platforms on Thursday, demanding the Federal Government to declare a state of emergency in the state, as well as the disbandment of Operation Rainbow and removal of the Director of the Department of State Services, DSS, in the state.

But in responding to the demands, the One Plateau, One Voice said it rejects the suggestion, noting that a state of emergency was not what the state needs at the moment, but rather concerted efforts to revamp the security structure to adequately tackle insecurity in the state.

In the statement signed on Friday by the convener of the advocacy group, Dogo Nanzing, the association said a state of emergency would not address the longstanding security challenges confronting communities across the state, insisting that priority should instead be given to protecting residents, restoring stability and facilitating the return of displaced persons.

Nanzing emphasized that though Plateau had experienced years of violence, displacement and loss of lives, the focus should now be on strengthening security and restoring affected communities.

“For 25 years, they have been killing our people and taking over our villages. Plateau has lost thousands of its citizens, but all through that time, those responsible for the attacks and their sympathisers never asked that a state of emergency be imposed on Plateau until now,” Nanzing said.

He further questioned the genuineness of calls for the disbandment of Operation Rainbow, stating that the security outfit was created as part of the state’s response to insecurity and that its mandate should be respected.

He added that the DSS and other security agencies have always maintained neutrality in tackling security concerns in the state and have done a lot to maintain peace.

The organisation argued that calling for their disbandment was taking the whole scenario to a ridiculous level and called on the Hausa-Fulani Unity group to be cautious in their demands, as that was not what Plateau State needs.

“The DSS has been in Plateau for as long as the state exists. From the beginning of the killings to this day, they never doubted the agency’s credibility and neutrality,” Nanzing said.

The group added that recent developments should be viewed against the background of prolonged violence and displacement, arguing that affected residents deserved protection and an opportunity to return to their communities.

It also called for the restoration of lands and communities from which residents had been displaced, stressing that any such process should be handled through lawful and peaceful mechanisms.

“We demand the return of our lands to the people who are the original owners,” the group said, urging the government, security agencies, traditional institutions and community leaders to work together to address the security situation and prevent further loss of lives.

posts.title: ‘Rescue my daughter, 18 other prospective NYSC members’ – Ibadan woman begs Tinubu, police
posts.excerpt: An Ibadan-based woman, Mrs Alimot Akande has urged President Bola Tinubu, the Nigeria Police Force and other security agencies to rescue her daughter and 18 other abducted persons. Akande made the app
posts.content:
An Ibadan-based woman, Mrs Alimot Akande has urged President Bola Tinubu, the Nigeria Police Force and other security agencies to rescue her daughter and 18 other abducted persons.

Akande made the appeal while speaking with journalists on Thursday in Ibadan, the Oyo State capital.

DAILY POST gathered that 19 prospective members of the National Youth Service Corps, NYSC, were abducted on their way to Abia State on Thursday.

It was learnt that the prospective NYSC members left Ibadan on Wednesday and were kidnapped between Anambra and Abia States in the early hours of Thursday.

Akande’s daughter is among the 19 prospective NYSC members who were abducted.

Speaking, she appealed to Tinubu and the security agencies to rescue the victims unhurt.

Akande added that efforts to reach her daughter had been unsuccessful since then.

According to her: “I am Mrs Alimot Akande. I am the parent of one of the victims. The prospective corps members boarded a bus belonging to a commercial transport company in the Sango area for the long journey to Abia State.

“The passengers had a stopover on Wednesday night in Onitsha at about 10 p.m., and the journey continued on Thursday morning before she quickly dropped a message that simply said, ‘kidnappers!’ indicating that the bus had been attacked by suspected armed kidnappers.

“I appeal to the Federal Government, the NYSC, the police and other security agencies to rescue my daughter and the others unhurt.”

posts.title: Friendly: Simon to lead second-string Super Eagles against Russia
posts.excerpt: Moses Simon is set to lead a new-look Super Eagles side when Nigeria face Russia in an international friendly next Tuesday. The Paris FC winger was among the Nigerian players who departed the Nnamdi A
posts.content:
Moses Simon is set to lead a new-look Super Eagles side when Nigeria face Russia in an international friendly next Tuesday.

The Paris FC winger was among the Nigerian players who departed the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, for Moscow on Thursday night ahead of the encounter.

Home-based players Chibuzor Atata, Aderemi Adeoye and Kenneth Igboke were also part of the travelling squad.

With captain, Wilfred Ndidi withdrawing from the game, Simon becomes the most experienced player in the squad and is expected to provide leadership against the Russians.

Head coach, Éric Chelle has opted for a blend of established players and fresh faces as he continues to assess his options ahead of upcoming international assignments.

Goalkeeper, Stanley Nwabali is included alongside defenders Emmanuel Fernandez, Benjamin Fredrick and Bright Osayi-Samuel. Raphael Onyedika and Akor Adams are also part of the squad.

Chelle has further strengthened the attack with the return of experienced forward Kelechi Iheanacho, who has enjoyed a positive start to his spell with Turkish side Bursaspor.

Several players are in line for their first taste of senior international football, including Akpe Victory, Suleiman Mubarak, Peter Edokpolor, Abdullahi Umar and Chibuzo Nwoko.

The match will be played at the Nizhny Novgorod Stadium and will mark the second meeting between Nigeria and Russia in 16 months.

posts.title: Man City confirm appeal after Premier League charges verdict
posts.excerpt: Manchester City confirmed on Friday that it had launched a "comprehensive appeal" after an independent commission ruled the club had broken Premier League financial rules. The post Man City confirm ap
posts.content:
Manchester City confirmed on Friday that it had launched a “comprehensive appeal” after an independent commission ruled the club had broken Premier League financial rules.

The Premier League announced on Tuesday that an independent commission had found the Abu Dhabi-backed club guilty on more than 100 charges.

The 10-time English champions, who have always vehemently denied wrongdoing, said in a statement on Friday they had lodged an appeal on Thursday — a day before the deadline.

“Manchester City Football Club can confirm that at 7:00 pm (1800 GMT) on Thursday 1st October 2026 the club lodged its comprehensive appeal against the opinion of the Premier League commission, in relation to the Premier League disciplinary matter,” the club said.

“The club’s firm position is that, on multiple grounds, the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe.

“The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case.

“We will continue to respect due process and are necessarily restricted in what we can say further until all proceedings are complete.”

AFP

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/man-city-confirm-appeal-after-premier-league-charges-verdict/

posts.title: US to increase immigration fees for asylum, work permits, from October 16
posts.excerpt: The United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) will increase fees for certain immigration-related applications from October 16, 2026, following an inflation adjustment required under H
posts.content:
The United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) will increase fees for certain immigration-related applications from October 16, 2026, following an inflation adjustment required under H.R. 1.

The fee changes will affect applications and services relating to asylum, immigration parole, employment authorisation and

Temporary Protected Status (TPS).

USCIS said the adjustments are based on inflation between July 2025 and July 2026. The Department of Homeland Security is required under H.R. 1 to adjust certain immigration-related fees annually for inflation, beginning in fiscal year 2026.

The new fees will apply to qualifying requests postmarked on or after October 16, 2026. Applications requiring one of the affected fees that are submitted without the correct payment may be rejected.

Under the new adjustment, the Annual Asylum Application Fee will rise from $102 to $105.

The immigration parole fee associated with Form I-131, Application for Travel Documents, Parole Documents, and Arrival/Departure Records, will increase from $1,020 to $1,050.

The fee for Form I-765, Application for Employment Authorization, for an initial employment authorization document for asylum applicants, parolees or TPS applicants will increase from $560 to $570.

Meanwhile, the fee for Form I-821, Application for Temporary Protected Status, will rise from $510 to $520.

USCIS initially announced the implementation of the H.R. 1 immigration-related fees in a Federal Register notice published on July 22, 2025.

The latest adjustments are part of the annual inflation-based changes required under the law and will remain in effect for fiscal year 2027.

Vanguard News
