posts.title: Actress Chioma Chukwuka-Akpotha announces father’s death
posts.excerpt: Reflecting on the pain that comes with losing a parent, regardless of how long they lived, Chukwuka said there is always a desire for more time with loved ones. The post Actress Chioma Chukwuka-Akpoth
posts.content:
Nollywood actress Chioma Chukwuka-Akpotha has announced the death of her father, Leonard Ndukaife Chukwuka.

The actress said in an Instagram post on Friday that the loss was particularly painful because she lost her mother 13 years ago and was now facing life without either parent.

“My beloved father, Leonard Ndukaife Chukwuka, has gone to be with the Lord,” she wrote.

“I lost my mother 13 years ago and now that my father is gone, the thought that I have neither parent here anymore breaks my heart in a way I cannot fully explain. So na only me bayi?”

The actress fondly remembered her father as “my daddy, papa’m, obara’m, my comfort” and expressed gratitude that he lived long enough to witness his children and grandchildren.

“I am so thankful you lived a long life, and I am grateful to God you saw your children and grandchildren. We had hoped you would meet your great-grandchildren too, mana nya diba!” she said.

Reflecting on the pain that comes with losing a parent, regardless of how long they lived, Chukwuka said there is always a desire for more time with loved ones.

“No matter how many years we are given with a parent, we still want one more conversation, one more embrace, one more day,” she wrote.

She also expressed appreciation for the memories and moments she shared with her father, particularly during the final period of his life.

According to the actress, she chose not to immediately make the loss public because she needed time to process her grief.

“I have held this news close while trying to understand my own grief,” she said.

Chukwuka appealed to fans, friends and well-wishers to pray for her, her siblings and the entire Chukwuka family.

She added that the family would announce details of her father’s funeral arrangements in due time.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/actress-chioma-chukwuka-akpotha-announces-fathers-death/

posts.title: Video: Hamzat, Lagos First Lady, Amosun, others attend Olu Jacobs’ funeral
posts.excerpt: Lagos State Deputy Governor Obafemi Hamzat, First Lady Ibijoke Sanwo-Olu and former Ogun State Governor Ibikunle Amosun are among the dignitaries attending the funeral service of veteran Nollywood act
posts.content:
Lagos State Deputy Governor Obafemi Hamzat, First Lady Ibijoke Sanwo-Olu and former Ogun State Governor Ibikunle Amosun are among the dignitaries attending the funeral service of veteran Nollywood actor Olu Jacobs in Lagos on Friday.

The funeral service is being held at This Present House, Freedom Way, Lekki Phase 1, Lagos, where family members, friends, colleagues and other dignitaries have gathered to pay their final respects to the late actor.

The video shows Hamzat, the Lagos First Lady and Amosun among guests who arrived for the ceremony as the Nigerian entertainment industry bids farewell to one of its most respected actors.

Entertainment entrepreneur Dare Art Alade was also present and performed “Pray for Me”, a song he recorded with Olu Jacobs and his wife, veteran actress Joke Silva. Jacobs’ son, Olugbenga Jacobs, also presented his father’s biography during the funeral programme.

The funeral follows a Night of Tributes and Service of Songs held at Glover Memorial Hall, Lagos Island, on Wednesday.

The event brought together several leading figures in Nollywood, including Richard Mofe-Damijo, Sola Sobowale, Funke Akindele, Jide Kosoko, Adebayo Salami, Hilda Dokubo, Rita Dominic and Segun Arinze.

At the tribute ceremony, colleagues reflected on Jacobs’ decades-long contribution to theatre, television and film. Richard Mofe-Damijo recalled a lesson the late actor taught him about the importance of every role in a production, while Sola Sobowale spoke emotionally about Jacobs’ encouragement early in her career.

Known as the “Lion of Lufodo”, Jacobs had a career spanning more than five decades. He trained at the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in London before working in British theatre and television and later becoming one of Nigeria’s most recognisable actors.

He and Joke Silva, whom he married in 1989, co-founded the Lufodo Group and Lufodo Academy of Performing Arts, contributing to film production and the training of performers. Jacobs was also honoured with the national award of Member of the Order of the Federal Republic in 2011.

Jacobs died on September 16, 2026, at the age of 84. His death triggered tributes from actors, filmmakers, political leaders and admirers across Nigeria and beyond, with many reflecting on his influence on generations of performers.

The funeral service is expected to be followed by a private burial. Guests attending the funeral were asked to wear shades of green, while the earlier Night of Tributes had a shade of blue dress code.

posts.title: North Korean leader’s sister calls Seoul ‘despicable’ after DMZ apology demand
posts.excerpt: Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of North Korea's leader, called South Korea "despicable" Friday after Seoul demanded an apology over a demilitarised zone blast that wounded three of its soldiers. The
posts.content:
Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of North Korea’s leader, called South Korea “despicable” Friday after Seoul demanded an apology over a demilitarised zone blast that wounded three of its soldiers.

Pyongyang this week denied being behind a landmine blast that caused severe injuries to three soldiers last month inside the Demilitarised Zone (DMZ), the heavily mined buffer dividing the two Koreas since their 1953 armistice.

South Korea’s military demanded an official apology this week, calling the incident “a clear violation of the Armistice Agreement”.

In the first public response from Pyongyang, Kim Yo Jong, the sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un said South Korea “even called for an apology” and added it is “really despicable”.

The powerful North Korean figure’s statement could dampen any hopes of smoother relations between the neighbours after South Korea’s dovish President Lee Jae Myung had urged Pyongyang to return to dialogue despite his military’s call for an apology.

Seoul and Pyongyang remain technically at war since the 1950-53 Korean War ended in a truce, not a peace treaty.

Since 2024, after North Korean leader Kim Jong Un designated South Korea as his country’s “principal enemy,” Pyongyang’s military has laid mines and built anti-tank barriers along the frontier as part of efforts to permanently seal it off.

The North Korean mines were believed to have been laid as part of Pyongyang’s border fortification work, according to South Korea’s defence minister Kang Shin-chul.

The US-led United Nations Command, which oversees the Korean War armistice and the southern side of the DMZ, also said Wednesday it had found an active North Korean anti-personnel mine on the South Korean side of the border.

– ‘Farce’

South Korea’s Lee has reversed the stance of his hawkish predecessor Yoon Suk Yeol since taking power in June 2025, offering nuclear-armed Pyongyang talks without preconditions.

He said Thursday that he hoped the North would “join us now on the path of restoring trust and resuming dialogue, following a long interruption” — a day after the military demanded an apology.

“My administration will consistently pursue practical measures to reduce military tensions between the two Koreas,” Lee said.

However, Kim Yo Jong ridiculed Lee’s latest overture, calling it “the climax of the farce that everyone should watch.”

Resuming blaring K-pop music — which the isolated North has long bristled at — across the border has been floated by analysts as a possible response to last month’s blast.

But others say Seoul has few realistic options for retaliation without further burdening border residents already exposed to disruption and danger.

The flare up comes as US President Donald Trump’s recent overtures to Pyongyang raised concerns that Seoul, an ally of Washington, could be sidelined in potential nuclear talks involving the North, which is backed by Russia as well as China.

Lee said last month that Washington should seek a freeze, rather than the immediate elimination, of North Korea’s nuclear programme and offer sanctions relief in return.

AFP

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/north-korean-leaders-sister-calls-seoul-despicable-after-dmz-apology-demand/

posts.title: Tinubu, Akpabio, Govs, Others Grace MKO Documentary Premiere
posts.excerpt: The documentary, MKO, examines Abiola’s rise as a businessman, publisher and politician, his participation in the 1993 presidential election, the annulment of the election by the military government a
posts.content:
President Bola Tinubu on Thursday led top government officials and other dignitaries to the national premiere of MKO, a documentary on the life and political legacy of the late businessman and politician, Moshood Abiola.

The premiere was held at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, formerly the National Theatre, in Iganmu, Lagos, as part of activities marking Nigeria’s 66th Independence Anniversary.

Tinubu attended the event with his wife, Oluremi Tinubu.

Among those present were Senate President Godswill Akpabio, Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, Ogun State Governor Dapo Abiodun, and Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila.

Also at the premiere were Deputy Senate President Jibrin Barau, Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives Benjamin Kalu, Minister of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy Hannatu Musawa, and former Ogun State Governor Segun Osoba.

The documentary was produced and directed by Nigerian-American filmmaker Ose Oyamendan, who said the film was aimed at preserving the story of Abiola and the events surrounding the June 12, 1993 presidential election.

Speaking at the premiere, Oyamendan paid tribute to Tinubu and recalled his involvement in the pro-democracy struggle that followed the annulment of the election.

MKO examines Abiola’s rise as a businessman, publisher, and politician, his participation in the 1993 presidential election, the annulment of the election by the military government, and the pro-democracy struggle that followed.

The filmmaker said Tinubu’s decision to serve as Chief Host of the premiere was significant because of his connection to the events documented in the film.

Oyamendan said the President and others who participated in the struggle against military rule made personal sacrifices in demanding the recognition of the June 12 mandate.

He also reflected on his own experience of the period, having worked as a journalist with Weekend Concord, a newspaper founded by Abiola.

According to him, making the documentary provided an opportunity to revisit the events surrounding Abiola’s political journey and present them to Nigerians who were either too young to remember the period or were born after the events.

MKO examines Abiola’s rise as a businessman, publisher, and politician, his participation in the 1993 presidential election, the annulment of the election by the military government, and the pro-democracy struggle that followed.

The documentary also covers Abiola’s detention and his death in custody in 1998.

Cover of the MKO Abiola documentary by Ose Oyamendan

It features archival footage and accounts from several people associated with the period, including former military Head of State Ibrahim Babangida, former Head of State Abdulsalami Abubakar, former President Olusegun Obasanjo, Nobel laureate Wole Soyinka, and Abiola’s running mate in the 1993 election, Baba Gana Kingibe.

Former United States ambassador to Nigeria Walter Carrington, former US Deputy Secretary of State Thomas Pickering, former Canadian High Commissioner Gerald Ohlsen and members of the Abiola family also feature in the documentary.

Tinubu was among those featured in the film, reflecting his involvement in the pro-democracy movement during the period.

The 108-minute documentary had its international premiere at the Sheffield International Documentary Festival in the United Kingdom on June 12, 2026, before its national premiere in Lagos.

The film is scheduled to begin its commercial cinema run across Nigeria on Friday, October 2.

The premiere also marked Tinubu’s return to a major public engagement in Nigeria after his four-week working visit to Europe.

The President returned to Lagos on September 29 and was scheduled to participate in activities marking the Independence anniversary.

The event brought together political leaders, members of the creative industry, and personalities connected to Nigeria’s political history to revisit one of the defining episodes in the country’s democratic journey.

Source: https://www.channelstv.com/2026/10/01/tinubu-akpabio-govs-others-grace-mko-documentary-premiere/

posts.title: Independence Day: Nigeria Is Moving From Reform To Prosperity, Tinubu Assures Nigerians
posts.excerpt: The President gave the assurance in his address to the nation on Thursday, October 1, as the country marks its 66th Independence Day anniversary. The post Independence Day: Nigeria Is Moving From Refo
posts.content:
President Bola Tinubu has assured Nigerians that the series of economic reforms will surely lead to better days.

Tinubu gave the assurance in his address to the nation on Thursday, October 1, as the country marks its 66th Independence Day anniversary.

Tinubu noted that the reforms did not weaken the economy as widely believed. He assured that the promises he made to Nigerians are finally being fulfilled.

“When this Administration assumed office, we resolved to do things differently. We chose to excise the cancer. The reforms that followed were difficult. The side effects were real. Yet, we must never confuse the medicine with the disease.

“Our reforms did not create the weaknesses in our economy. They confronted them. Now, as certain influential but regressive voices would have us abandon the treatment and return ourselves to the abuse of addictive subsidies, we must resist their siren song. We must remember why we began this journey and how far we have already come.

“Three and a half years later, the evidence that Nigeria’s economic outlook has improved is undeniable. Our economy has grown by over 4 per cent this year. Both oil and non-oil sectors have contributed to the renewed period of stable growth.”

The President noted that oil theft in producing countries has dropped; likewise, inflation has fallen “substantially”.

“Oil theft is down. Inflation has fallen substantially from its peak. Our foreign reserves have been rebuilt.

“Our foreign exchange market has stabilised, and in 2025 this country recorded its highest revenue from non-oil exports in its history, exceeding $6 billion. This is real money being made by real Nigerian businesses.

“These are not idle claims. International observers, journalists, NGOs and multilateral institutions can see the change. Each has concluded that our reforms have strengthened Nigeria’s economic stability and resilience. The private sector has long since delivered its verdict, and foreign direct investment continues to rise each year.”

He emphasised that the country had reached a turning point of prosperity.

“The emergency treatment is over. The foundation has been repaired. The central economic task before us has changed. For three years, our overriding purpose was to correct our nation’s course.

“Now, our purpose is simple: shared and widespread prosperity.

“When I speak of prosperity, I do not speak merely of a larger economy, abstract numbers or better statistics. I mean something much more personal.

“I mean a Nigeria in which the farmer can cultivate his land safely, produce more at lower cost, and earn a decent return for his labour.

“A Nigeria in which factories have reliable power, businesses can obtain credit, and young people can find productive work.

“A Nigeria in which food and transportation are affordable, education is within reach, and hard-working families can look towards the future with confidence”, he added.

The President reeled out Nigeria’s journey after Independence 66 years ago and the resilience of Nigerians through thick and thin.

“Sixty-six years ago today, our flag was raised, for the first time, over a free and sovereign nation. Since then, we have journeyed together as one nation, bound by our collective trust in the great promise of Nigeria: that a country of our size, our bountiful resources, our cultural diversity and, above all, our extraordinary people can build a giant in Africa; that in this blessed and fertile land we can build a united, strong and prosperous nation; a land of regional authority and global consequence.

“Our journey has not always been easy. In truth, it has generally been too hard for too many. We have known moments of great hope and periods of profound disappointment.

“We have endured war, military rule, economic crises, insecurity, and political upheaval. Yet through it all, Nigeria, with the indomitable spirit of its people, has endured.

“It has endured through the efforts of the farmer who rises before dawn to work his land. The trader who opens her shop each morning, hopeful for a productive day.

“The teacher who believes in the children entrusted to her care and the young entrepreneur who refuses to surrender ambition to circumstance. We are grateful for the men and women of our Armed Forces and security services who place themselves in harm’s way so that the rest of us may live in peace.

He thanked Nigerians for believing in the country, adding that the economy is on the right trajectory.

“Through every difficulty, generations of Nigerians have continued to believe in one thing: that this country of ours will be better.

“This faith, which sustains us all, is the inheritance of independence.

“Our founding fathers did not struggle merely for a flag, an anthem or a place among the nations of the world. Independence carried a larger promise: that Nigerians would have the freedom to shape their own destiny and build a nation capable of providing opportunity, dignity and a better life for its people.

“Sixty-six years later, Almighty God has made it our responsibility to deliver that promise.

“Today, as we celebrate our independence, we must speak honestly about the journey so far, the choices we made, and the country we are determined to build from here”, he added.

Source: https://www.channelstv.com/2026/10/01/independence-day-nigeria-is-moving-from-reform-to-prosperity-tinubu-assures-nigerians/

posts.title: Ogun PDP Deputy Gov Candidate, Sowunmi-Kolapo, Installed as Muslim Council Grand Matron
posts.excerpt: Ĥ.Urges Ogun indigenes to shun money politics, protect their heritage The Ogun State Muslim Council has installed the Peoples Democratic Party’s deputy governorship candidate for the 2027 election, Ha
posts.content:
Ĥ.Urges Ogun indigenes to shun money politics, protect their heritage

The Ogun State Muslim Council has installed the Peoples Democratic Party’s deputy governorship candidate for the 2027 election, Hajia Lateefat ‘Yemi Sowunmi-Kolapo, as its Grand Matron (Egba Zone).

Sowunmi-Kolapo, who is the Iya Sunnah of Egbaland and Ameerah of Ogun State, was installed and decorated at the Ake Palace, Abeokuta, on Thursday, October 1, 2026.

The ceremony, which attracted Muslim leaders, political stakeholders, traditional figures and other members of the community, was held under the theme, “Socio-Economic Stability: A Fortress for Global Security.”

The installation has assumed political significance, coming ahead of the 2027 governorship election, with Sowunmi-Kolapo using the occasion to call for increased civic participation among Muslims and urging voters to reject electoral violence, vote-buying and political apathy.

She also urged Muslims across the state to take an active role in determining the political leadership of the country. Speaking in an interview after her installation, the new Grand Matron described the honour as a demonstration of confidence and support from the Muslim community.

She said, “It’s a great honour for me because when people appreciate you and they show it, you can only be thankful to God and them.

“I thank the Ogun State Muslim Council for this great honour. As we were told, the Iya Sunnah of Egbaland is expected to be decorated OMC Grand Matron (Egba Zone). Our late revered mother, late Chief Khadijah Adebisi Edionseri, was the Iya Sunnah of Egbaland and OMC Grand Matron.”

“Stepping into her shoes is a big deal for me. I pray Almighty Allah guides my steps and makes the journey fruitful,” the deputy governorship candidate added.

She also expressed appreciation to members of the Muslim community for the support she had received, from the beginning of her political journey, and throughout the process leading to her installation.

“To the Muslim community, I can only say thank you to them because the shower of love and support that I got from them from the beginning of this journey is unprecedented and I don’t take it for granted,” she said.

She, however, used the occasion to broaden her message from religious leadership to civic and political participation, urging Muslims to recognise the importance of political power in protecting their interests and heritage.

The new Grand Matron said the Muslim community must not remain passive in matters concerning its future.

“An elder statesman was telling me something when I went to visit him. He said religious leaders should not sit back and think that they will hand over everything they seek to them on a platter of gold.

“If you don’t struggle for power, some oppressors will use the same power to destroy you, which is why we say our power is in our votes.”

The PDP candidate urged Muslim parents, leaders and community stakeholders to educate their children and wards on responsible democratic participation.

She said electoral participation should be peaceful and driven by citizens’ choices rather than inducements.

Earlier at the ceremony, the OMC, Egba Zone, used the occasion to draw attention to the connection between socio-economic conditions, education, security and global stability.

Earlier at the ceremony, the OMC, Egba Zone, used the occasion to draw attention to the connection between socio-economic conditions, education, security and global stability.

The guest lecturer, Sheikh Sulaimon Faruq Onikijipa, OON, who spoke on the theme, “Socio-Economic Stability: A Fortress for Global Security,” urged governments to give greater priority to security, education and the economic wellbeing of citizens.

Onikijipa said a stable society could not be achieved when citizens were denied access to quality education, security and the basic socio-economic conditions necessary for dignified living.

Also speaking at the ceremony, Senator Prof. Iyabo Obasanjo commended the Ogun State Muslim Community for honouring Sowunmi-Kolapo and giving her the blessing to serve as the PDP deputy governorship candidate.

Obasanjo described the new Grand Matron as humble, faithful and kind, while acknowledging her contributions to the Muslim community.

posts.title: Official: Alvini wins Serie A coach of the month after flying Frosinone start to 2026-27
posts.excerpt: Massimiliano Alvini has been crowned the Serie A coach of the month for the period...
posts.content:
Massimiliano Alvini has been crowned the Serie A coach of the month for the period spanning August and September after a flying start with his newly-promoted Frosinone side, who have picked up 10 points from their first five matches back in the Italian top flight.

Alvini wins Serie A coach of the month for August-September

Alvini was appointed head coach of Frosinone ahead of the 2025-26 season after a disappointing 15th-place Serie B finish the year before, finishing second and earning promotion back to the top flight in his first season in charge.

He and Frosinone now sit in sixth place in Serie A with 10 points to their name after the first five matches of the 2026-27 season and are currently on a four-match unbeaten run in the league.

FROSINONE, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 06: Antonio Raimondo of Frosinone Calcio scores goal 2-0 during the Serie A match between Frosinone Calcio and Venezia FC at Stadio Benito Stirpe on September 06, 2026 in Frosinone, Italy. (Photo by Giuseppe Bellini/Getty Images)Their campaign began with a narrow 1-0 defeat against Juventus before hammering a then-struggling Fiorentina 3-0 away from home the following week. A 3-2 victory over fellow Serie A newcomers Venezia and a 1-1 draw away against Genoa followed.

Their most recent result was perhaps their most impressive, claiming a 2-0 victory over Champions League outfit Como just before the international break.

Alvini has also earned praise across Italy for his use of young Italian players at the start of the 2026-27 Serie A season. Five of the players included in the Frosinone squad for their 2-0 win over Como have been called up to Silvio Baldini’s Italy U21 side, including Antonio Raimondo, who was awarded the Serie A rising star of the month award for August and September.

These results see Alvini honoured with his first ever Serie A coach of the month award. He will be awarded with the trophy ahead of Frosinone’s next home match, which will be against Sassuolo on Friday, October 16.

GENOA, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 12: Massimiliano Alvini, head coach of Frosinone, reacts during the Serie A match between Genoa CFC and Frosinone Calcio at Stadio Luigi Ferraris on September 12, 2026 in Genoa, Italy. (Photo by Simone Arveda/Getty Images)Given that there were only five rounds of Serie A fixtures prior to the September-October international break, the first coach of the month award spanned the period across the months of both August and September.

That was also the case for the Serie A player of the month award, which was claimed by Roma’s Donyell Malen on Thursday.

Source: https://football-italia.net/official-alvini-coach-of-the-month-sep-2026/

posts.title: Bastoni on Dembélé: ‘I’m the last person you should ask’ – video
posts.excerpt: Italy star Alessandro Bastoni jokes that he should be the ‘last person you should ask’...
posts.content:
Italy star Alessandro Bastoni jokes that he should be the ‘last person you should ask’ about facing France’s Ousmane Dembélé: ‘You saw how it went the last time.’

Italy and Inter star Bastoni made a funny and honest admission about facing star striker Dembélé, the latest Ballon d’Or winner.

FLORENCE, ITALY – OCTOBER 08: Alessandro Bastoni of Italy looks on prior to the Italy training session at Centro Tecnico Federale di Coverciano on October 08, 2024 in Florence, Italy. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images)During a pre-match press conference on the eve of tonight’s game against France, Bastoni said.

“You probably saw how it went last time. I’m the last person you should ask; it’s really not easy. He’s an incredible player, just like all of his teammates in that unit.

“We need a great performance from a defensive standpoint, definitely a collective one that involves everyone, all eleven on the pitch. But I think the only way to put France in trouble is to actually play, without being afraid to keep the ball. So I believe our possession phase can make the difference.”

WROCLAW, POLAND – SEPTEMBER 5: Ousmane Dembele of France looks on during the FIFA World Cup 2026 qualifier match between Ukraine and France at Tarczynski Arena on September 5, 2025 in Wroclaw, Poland. (Photo by Mateusz Slodkowski/Getty Images)Bastoni’s reference was to the 2025 Champions League Final, which his Inter side lost 5-0 to Dembélé’s PSG.

Bastoni started Friday’s away game against Turkiye and scored the winning goal for the Azzurri.

Tonight, he’s expected to start against France in the Nations League group phase, Round 3.

Bastoni on facing Dembélé: “You saw how it went last time… I’m the last person to ask. It’s really not easy. He’s an incredible player, like all his teammates.”

posts.title: Stones sets out Inter ambition: ‘I want to be remembered for winning’
posts.excerpt: John Stones has described the emotions of joining Inter and set out how he wants...
posts.content:
John Stones has described the emotions of joining Inter and set out how he wants to be remembered at San Siro.

Speaking in an interview with DAZN, via TuttoMercatoWeb, the England defender reflected on the move that took him from Manchester to Milan in the summer.

“I felt a lot of emotions, it was an overwhelming feeling of happiness and pride,” Stones said. “I’m really grateful for this opportunity, I’m excited to be here. I’d describe myself as kind, happy and competitive. As a child I was never still, always moving, I was really active.”

MILAN, ITALY – AUGUST 22: John Stones of Internazionale looks on during the Serie A match between FC Internazionale and AC Monza at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on August 22, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)Stones still finding his place in the Inter dressing room

He is usually a vocal presence, though he is holding back while he settles.

“I talk a lot in the dressing room, even if right now I’m observing and trying to find my place in the group. The technical aspect I do best is passing, for the rest I have to improve in everything.”

On the demands of playing for a club of Inter’s size, he was relaxed. “When you play the pressure is always there, it’s positive. It lets you give your best if you manage it well, and you end up getting used to it. It’s about knowing what you’ve done in the past and during the week so you feel good in the game.”

MILAN, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 05: Curtis Jones and John Stones of Internazionale pose for a photo on the bench before during the Serie A match between FC Internazionale and SSC Napoli at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on September 05, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images)Stones is currently sidelined with the muscle injury that forced him off against Udinese, though he posted earlier this week that he is already working towards a return after the international break.

He missed the 2-2 draw at Roma, where Inter recovered from two goals down, exactly the kind of start Cristian Chivu will want his most experienced defender available to prevent.

“I always give 100 per cent, I’m competitive, I love winning and I leave everything on the pitch,” he said. “I think I’ve grown a lot as a person and as a player. I had so much success and built so many friendships and memories at City. When I scored for Inter in a friendly it felt almost unreal. I was really happy, it was a special day.

“I’d like to be remembered by the fans for having given everything for the team, for the club and for the shirt. And for having won.”

Source: https://football-italia.net/stones-sets-out-inter-ambition/

posts.title: France vs. Italy: Where to watch on TV, latest team news and probable line-ups
posts.excerpt: Italy face their biggest test of Roberto Mancini’s second spell in charge of the national...
posts.content:
Italy face their biggest test of Roberto Mancini’s second spell in charge of the national team away against France in the Nations League on Friday evening, and pre-match reports indicate that both Riccardo Calafiori and Nicolo Barella are set to return to the starting line-up.

Kick-off this evening is due at 19.45 BST.

Mancini got his second spell as head coach of the Italy national team underway with a 2-0 defeat on home soil against Belgium last Friday, but bounced back with a more encouraging 4-1 victory away against Vincenzo Montella’s Turkey on Monday.

Francesco Pio Esposito celebrates with his brother Sebastiano Esposito during Turkiye vs. Italy in the Nations League (@azzurri)The Azzurri are in Paris and are preparing to take on France in what will be Zinedine Zidane’s first home match at the Stade de France since taking over as head coach from Didier Deschamps over the summer. Les Bleues have beaten both Turkey and France away from home by 1-0 scorelines over the last week.

Mancini originally named a squad of 34 players for the extra-long September-October international break, but that was cut down to 32 after Nicolo Zaniolo and Giacomo Raspadori withdrew from the camp without being replaced.

Teams are only allowed to name 23 players in their matchday squads in the Nations League, though, which meant that another nine players had to be dropped.

BURSA, TURKEY – SEPTEMBER 28: Roberto Mancini, Head Coach of Italy, looks on before the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Türkiye and Italy at Atatürk Spor Kompleksi Matli Stadyumu on September 28, 2026 in Bursa, Turkey. (Photo by Ahmad Mora/Getty Images)Massimo Pessina, Diego Coppola, Daniele Ghilardi, Honest Ahanor, Eddy Kouadio, Alessandro Romano, Rolando Mandragora, Nicolo Cambiaghi and Samuele Inacio have not travelled.

As of Friday, Ahanor is no longer part of the squad and will instead be available to the Italy U21s ahead of a crucial European Championship qualifier against Poland on Monday night.

Italy squad to take on France

Goalkeepers: Gianluigi Donnarumma, Marco Carnesecchi, Guglielmo Vicario.

Defenders: Michael Kayode, Giovanni Di Lorenzo, Riccardo Calafiori, Alessandro Bastoni, Giorgio Scalvini, Gianluca Mancini, Matteo Ruggeri.

Midfielders: Samuele Ricci, Sandro Tonali, Nicolo Fagioli, Nicolo Barella, Issa Doumbia, Davide Frattesi.

Forwards: Pio Esposito, Moise Kean, Gianluca Scamacca, Mohamed Ali Zoma, Daniel Maldini, Sebastiano Esposito, Antonio Vergara.

Italy team news

BURSA, TURKEY – SEPTEMBER 28: Riccardo Calafiori of Italy inspects the pitch before with teammates before the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Türkiye and Italy at Atatürk Spor Kompleksi Matli Stadyumu on September 28, 2026 in Bursa, Turkey. (Photo by Ahmad Mora/Getty Images)Following the 4-1 win away against Turkey earlier this week, it looks as though Gianluigi Donnarumma, Michael Kayode, Giorgio Scalvini and Alessandro Bastoni will keep their places at the back, with Calafiori set to replace Matteo Ruggeri at left-back. There is a chance that Gianluca Mancini is preferred to Scalvini on the right side of centre-back and a small chance of Giovanni Di Lorenzo being selected at right-back.

Barella is set to return to the midfield three, likely alongside Sandro Tonali and Nicolo Fagioli, although Davide Frattesi is also hoping for a starting spot after his goalscoring display in Bursa earlier this week.

There are a few more doubts in attack. There had been suggestions that Moise Kean would be given his first start of the international break at centre-forward, but the latest updates from Sky claim that his condition will need to be assessed and that Pio Esposito is more likely to keep hold of his starting spot.

He will likely be joined by his brother Sebastiano in the Italy attack, with either Daniel Maldini or debutant Antonio Vergara on the right wing.

France vs. Italy: Probable line-ups

BURSA, TURKEY – SEPTEMBER 28: Italy pose for a team photograph before the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Türkiye and Italy at Atatürk Spor Kompleksi Matli Stadyumu on September 28, 2026 in Bursa, Turkey. (Photo by Ahmad Mora/Getty Images)France (4-3-3): Maignan; Kounde, Upamecano, Jacquet, Truffert; Cherki, Kone, Rabiot; Olise, Dembele, Doue.

Italy (4-3-3): Donnarumma; Kayode, Scalvini, Bastoni, Calafiori; Barella, Tonali, Fagioli; Vergara, P. Esposito, S. Esposito.

Where to watch France vs. Italy on TV

Tonight’s game will be available to watch live in the UK on Amazon Prime. Supporters in the USA are able to tune in via Fox Sports 1 and through fuboTV. France vs. Italy will be shown on DAZN and fuboTV in Canada and on beIN Sports 3 in Australia.

Join us for all the pre-match build-up, in-game coverage and post-match reactions on the Football Italia Liveblog.

Source: https://football-italia.net/france-vs-italy-where-to-watch-on-tv/

posts.title: MAGA mom's dire warning over tech guardrails as Trump puts pedal to the metal on race with China
posts.excerpt: Amy Kremer's Humans First organization demands AI guardrails to protect children from chatbot dangers and prevent mass displacement of American workers.
posts.content:
A conservative political activist who has been deeply entrenched in right-wing politics for decades is calling on the government to implement safety guardrails on artificial intelligence (AI), especially when it comes to protecting children and ensuring that the booming technology doesn't displace American workers en masse.

"If something happens with one of these companies, whether it's a child taking their own life due to suicide by manipulation with a chatbot, these companies are not required to report it to the federal government," Amy Kremer told Fox News Digital.

Kremer is the chairwoman of Humans First, a gorup that advocates for government safeguards on the technology and says it gives the American people a voice in the AI conversation, rather than leaving all the power in the hands of what it calls "Big AI globalists" who have little concern for ordinary Americans.

MIKE JOHNSON REJECTS AI MORATORIUM OVER CHINA THREAT AS CONSERVATIVE ACTIVIST DEMANDS GUARDRAILS

"We are a grassroots organization focused on putting guardrails and safety mechanisms in place around AI technology in order to protect the American people, our children, jobs and so forth, and also to put those guardrails in place to to make sure that the people have a seat at the table and a voice in the conversation about what goes into their community," Kremer said.

Kremer, who is known by the political right for her time as a Tea Party advocate and ferocious fighter for President Donald Trump's MAGA movement, mentioned the 2025 mass shooting at Florida State University, which claimed the lives of two people and injured six others, as an instance of AI gone wrong.

Court documents in that case claim that the alleged shooter, Phoenix Ikner, used ChatGPT to plan aspects of the shooting. The company was sued by the wife of one of the deceased victims, and the state of Florida took the rare step of opening a criminal investigation into the company.

"If a chatbot is used in planning a school shooting like what happened at Florida State University in April of 2025, they're not required to report that to the federal government," said Kremer. "The only reason we know about a number of these things that have happened is because of lawsuits that have been filed by the victims and/or their families."

She argued that as a former flight attendant, she had to report every issue on an airliner to the government. And just as hospitals, pharmaceutical companies and hordes of other industries are regulated under the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), Kremer believes that AI companies should face similar scrutiny.

FOX NEWS POLL: VOTERS QUESTION WHETHER AI’S PROMISE OUTWEIGHS ITS RISKS

AI is a hotly-contested issue ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, with some Democrats looking to reign in the technology while the Trump administration hoping to keep competition and innovation flowing in the effort to win the AI race with China.

But Kremer is far from a Democrat, and she wants also wants the United States to crush China in the race for technological dominance.

"I want America to win this AI race, I absolutely I do. I'm America first, always have been, and we've led the world on innovation and ingenuity," she said. "But again ... I go back to, you don't have to forego safety to have innovation and ingenuity."

"I'm not siding with the Democrats," Kremer said. "I am not a tech person. I'm not anti-AI. I'm not anti-technology. I'm not anti-data center."

"I am a mom with common sense and I'm a conservative, and it only makes sense that guardrails are put in place," she added.

After all, Kremer said, AI companies aren't partisan actors.

TRUMP'S AI RACE WITH CHINA COULD BECOME THE BIGGEST MISTAKE OF OUR TIME

"They don't care about Republicans, they don't care about Democrats, they don't care about Americans. At the end of the day, I think they care about their own companies and their technology, and that's what, what drives them," she said. "And so, everything with these guys I think is contractual, you know, it's not, 'these are my friends, these are the people, I have the same ideology.' It's contractual, it's what benefits them and I think that's why they've cozied up to President Trump and Republicans in this administration and Congress."

In a high-stakes summit in Washington, D.C., last week, AI was a hot topic of discussing between Chinese President Xi Jinping and Trump, though what exactly was discussed remains under wraps.

"The Trump administration’s priority is to ensure there is a booming economy so that workers have many opportunities and experience limited volatility from any short-term disruptions," a White House official told Fox News Digital. "The goal is for workers to continue to have access to high paying jobs and that workers can easily adapt to new technologies and processes."

OBAMA CRITICIZES TRUMP ON APPROACH TO AI, ESCALATES WARNING FOR STRONGER REGULATION

As for children's safety, the official pointed Fox News Digital to its National Policy Framework on Artificial Intelligence.

That framework calls on Congress to implement a number of AI child safety measures, including empowering parents with tools to control their children's content exposure, privacy settings, content exposure and account controls.

It also asks the lawmaking body to "establish commercially reasonable, privacy protective, age assurance requirements (such as parental attestation) for AI platforms and services likely to be accessed by minors," and ensure that AI platforms implement safeguards against child sexual exploitation and self-harm.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/politics/maga-mom-dire-warning-tech-guardrails-trump-pedal-metal-race-china

posts.title: One group of married Americans is having more sex — and happier marriages
posts.excerpt: Institute for Family Studies research finds regular churchgoers report more frequent sex and greater sexual satisfaction than nonreligious spouses.
posts.content:
Married couples who regularly attend church report having more frequent sex and greater sexual satisfaction than those who attend less often or not at all, according to a new report from the Institute for Family Studies (IFS) in Charlottesville, Virginia.

Researchers analyzed findings from multiple datasets, including the 2026 IFS Religion and Family Survey of 3,125 married adults ages 18–54, the long-running nationally representative General Social Survey, and a separate survey of 1,219 alumni of FOCUS, a Catholic campus ministry.

Regular churchgoers reported having more frequent sex than less religious or non-religious married adults, with regularly attending Catholics reporting some of the highest levels of sexual frequency. The association remained even after accounting for demographic differences.

COMMON MARRIAGE HABIT COULD QUIETLY KILL YOUR SEX LIFE, EXPERT WARNS

Among married adults ages 20 to 54, 62% of regular churchgoers reported having sex at least once a week, compared with 48% of nonreligious spouses, according to the report.

In addition to frequency, sexual satisfaction was also higher among church attendants. Catholics and Protestants who regularly attended religious services were more likely to rate their sex lives positively than those who attended less often or had no religious affiliation.

Daily prayer was linked to greater sexual satisfaction among married Catholics and Protestants, though it was not associated with more frequent sex.

Among churchgoers, 55% of Catholics and 45% of Protestants rated their sex lives as "excellent" or "very good," compared with 45% of nominal Catholics, 35% of nominal Protestants and 40% of religiously unaffiliated respondents.

‘QUIET QUITTING’ IN MARRIAGE: THE SUBTLE SIGNS A SPOUSE HAS EMOTIONALLY CHECKED OUT

Those who viewed marriage as a permanent commitment were more likely to report both frequent and satisfying sex. That belief, along with shared values, was also strongly associated with overall marital quality.

Because the analysis was observational, it cannot determine whether religious practice directly causes better marital or sexual outcomes, the authors acknowledged.

Additionally, the marital outcomes were self-reported, and other unmeasured differences between religious and non-religious respondents could have influenced the results.

Differences in factors such as age and length of marriage could also make it challenging to strike comparisons with the broader population.

The study was funded by FOCUS, the Fellowship of Catholic University Students.

Jessica Steinman, a licensed marriage and family therapist and certified sex addiction therapist in Los Angeles, spoke with Fox News Digital about the potential relationship between religious activity and the quality of a couple’s sex life.

"When we think of people who are really involved in religion … we might think they're not having a lot of sex or that they're having very constricted views on their sex lives," she said. "And this article and research show that's changing."

WHY COUPLES SHOULD FLIRT WITH EACH OTHER EVERY DAY — PLUS THE ‘RED FLAG’ TO AVOID

People who actively participate in a shared spiritual or religious life may also feel more connected to one another as partners, according to Steinman, who is also the chief clinical officer for No Matter What Recovery in Los Angeles, Chicago and Austin.

"If they're showing up and looking at things outside themselves — things that are spiritual, things that are religious, things are having them look inward, things that are having them look into larger morals and values within their marriages and partnerships — I think they're going to possibly have happier marriages and partnerships," the therapist said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

They may also be more vulnerable and open with one another, which could contribute to a more active sex life, she added.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

The rituals and shared practices associated with religious life likely play a role in strengthening that connection, the expert suggested.

"Certain religious settings are really focused on rituals and traditions," Steinman said. "And if you're looking at partnership and marriage … engaging in sexual connection and sexual intimacy can really become a ritual itself."

The research highlighted what has been described as an ongoing "sex recession," where people are not engaging in sexual intimacy as much as they once did.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Regardless of religious affiliation, Steinman encourages people to find ways to connect with their partners.

"Get off the phones, get off of the internet, turn the TV off and start really connecting with your partner," she advised.

Steinman suggested that partners engage with one another and build connections that go deeper than simply asking, "How was your day?"

That can include building emotional openness and discussing how partners want to connect sexually, she said.

posts.title: JACK CARR: The lesson from FlyDubai is simple. Be ready to save yourself
posts.excerpt: The FlyDubai Flight 1073 knife attack over Saudi Arabia exposes critical gaps in pilot screening and cockpit security that demand new reforms.
posts.content:
The events on FlyDubai Flight 1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv on 30 September 2026 reads like something out of one of my thrillers. But what occurred in the skies over Saudi Arabia was not fiction, it was real world and highlights an adage I learned long ago and has been repeated in various incarnations across social channels with differing attributions over the years — hope is not a course of action, in most cases, no one is coming to save you, you will need to be your own cavalry.

That means be prepared.

I am actually surprised that this or something like this has not happened previously — an unhinged pilot or co-pilot killing the other, perhaps suicidal, perhaps in search of martyrdom, as what some terrorist organizations call an istishhadi or "martyrdom seeker."

FORMER ISRAELI PM HAILS ‘HEROISM’ AFTER PASSENGERS HELP THWART ALLEGED COCKPIT ATTACK

With prior planning it is possible for pilots to work together in a "martyrdom operation" that would be much harder to thwart. Or a single pilot or co-pilot could work with other "muscle" sitting in first class to prevent passengers from doing what they did on September 30, giving the terrorist in the cockpit time to kill them all or once again turn an airliner into a weapon focused on a specific target.

I think about scenarios like this every time I fly.

I look at and evaluate the passengers, the flight attendants, and I always look in on the pilots as I enter the aircraft, searching for anything that does not look or feel right, remembering something a Vietnam-era Project Delta Army Special Forces soldier told me decades ago: "if it doesn’t look right, it’s probably not."

Trust your instincts — you have them for a reason.

I am also identifying assets and liabilities among those groups. Who is a potential asset if things go south? I’m noting shoes, belts, shirts, watches, hats, bags, sunglasses, tattoos, cauliflower ear, and filing away what that tells me about each person. Which of them are likely to help — and which of them may hinder in the event of an incident.

On September 30, the skies over Saudi Arabia were full of miracles. The pilot, Captain Smit Machchhar, was not immediately incapacitated in the initial knife attack and managed to open the cockpit door before collapsing. Passengers with the instinct to act, fight, and prevail were sitting near the front of the plane, one of the passengers had the wherewithal to pull back on the controls — something he remembered from watching a television show.

HERO FLYDUBAI PILOT SAYS HE WAS 'FIGHTING FOR MY LIFE' AS PLANE PLUNGED AFTER COPILOT ATTACK

And there happened to be a pilot or pilots onboard who were able land the plane. Incredible.

If any one of those things had not happened, we would be talking about a very different incident, one in which every single person on that flight is dead.

I weave a lot of history and the history of terrorism into my thrillers, and I also have a series of non-fiction books on terrorism, the second of which is on Pan Am 103, a plane that exploded over Lockerbie, Scotland, on December 21, 1988, killing 259 passengers and crew and 11 residents on the ground. In that attack, there was no warning — a bomb detonated in the cargo hold at 31,000 feet.

The destruction of Pan Am 103 horrified the world — and led to important changes in airline security, thanks in large part to pressure from victims’ families who pushed lawmakers to pass the Aviation Security Improvement Act of 1990. That legislation heightened the focus on domestic and international security, including placing federal security managers at major airports and requiring background checks on all air carrier workers. The law demanded the FAA work in tandem with the FBI, expanded scrutiny of overseas airports, and improved the flow of terrorist threat information.

AMERICA BUILT A FORTRESS AFTER 9/11. THEN THE THREAT STARTED HIDING IN PLAIN SIGHT

The recent FlyDubai event should lead to changes as well, namely enhanced pilot screenings. It is not just about qualifications and your ability to fly a plane — it’s about your background, associations, and your mental stability.

If, for example, a background check finds that instead of funding your 401(k) each month, you are diverting funds to Hezbollah or a charity funding terrorist organizations — an obvious red flag — you should not be a pilot and certainly should not be flying a plane full of Israelis into Tel Aviv.

This is common sense to most, but common sense seems to be in limited supply these days.

The model for hijackings and the use of terror focused on airlines was different before September 11, 2001. Typically, in the 1970s and 1980s, planes were hijacked and the passengers were exchanged for prisoners or ransomed — sometimes a passenger or passengers were killed to make a point.

SEN MCCORMICK: THE HEROIC PASSENGERS OF FLIGHT 93 SHOWED AMERICA HOW TO STAND UNITED

From a tactical security standpoint that meant that you would want a window seat so you were not in the aisle where you could be struck and injured or grabbed by a terrorist — you wanted to be able to survey the situation, bide your time, and act when appropriate.

On September 11, 2001, that paradigm shifted — planes and passengers were not being hijacked to bring about a political end or for a ransom, they were being turned into weapons. That adaptation by terrorists meant protectors needed to act quickly in the event of a hijacking. They moved from window seats to aisle seats to be in an advantageous position to recognize the threat and take immediate decisive action. And by "protectors" I do not mean military or law enforcement, I mean citizens. I am referring to those who have not suppressed the will to fight and have not outsourced their protection to a government or outside entity who is not coming to save them.

Protecting those who cannot protect themselves is our responsibility as citizens, as husbands, as fathers. The FlyDubai incident is an example of that duty and of the warrior mindset — from the pilot to the passengers who all acted heroically to save the day.

Col. John Boyd developed something called the OODA Loop — Observe, Orient, Decide, Act. In combat, in most cases, whoever does that faster than their opponent — or who can disrupt their enemy in the middle of their loop — will be victorious. That is what the pilot and passengers did on the FlyDubai flight. They stepped up and tapped into that primal urge to live and to protect that is in all of our DNA — and they prevailed.

The enemy will learn and adapt to September 30, 2026.

Next time it might be both pilots or it might be one incapacitating the other, working in conjunction with a passenger or passengers who will block access to the cockpit. We must adapt as well to ensure those with mental disorders or associations with terrorist organizations or those who fund them are kept from the ranks of the aviators we all trust with our lives.

As John Steinbeck writes in The Acts of King Arthur and his Noble Knights, "‘Now — I will lay down the law, and you will learn it word by word, and every word must be edged with fire. This is the law. The purpose of fighting is to win. There is no possible victory in defense. The sword is more important than the shield, and skill is more important than either. The final weapon is the brain, all else is supplementary.’"

Remember — hope is not a course of action.

In most cases, no one is coming to save you. Your mind is the ultimate weapon, and you will need it, coupled with the will to fight, to save yourself and your loved ones, and in this case, an entire plane full of innocent people.

Be prepared.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/opinion/jack-carr-lesson-flydubai-simple-ready-save-yourself

posts.title: 'Digger' Review: Tom Cruise destroys the planet in Alejandro Iñárritu's grandiose, messy political satire
posts.excerpt: Fox News Digital reviews Warner Bros. Pictures' "Digger" starring Tom Cruise, John Goodman, Riz Ahmed, Sandra Hüller and Jesse Plemons. Directed by Alejandro Iñárritu.
posts.content:
A great satire must be two things: innovative and funny. Unfortunately for Tom Cruise and Oscar-winning director Alejandro G. Iñárritu, "Digger" is neither of those things.

Cruise is nearly unrecognizable, buried under layers upon layers of prosthetics transforming himself into Digger Rockwell, an eccentric oil tycoon who has affection for his wealth and his chronically ill robotic-like cat Maggie.

Digger doesn't like to take no for an answer, even as he's repeatedly warned that a crack at his oil drilling site in Greenland could lead to catastrophe.

‘PRIMETIME’ REVIEW: ROBERT PATTINSON CHANNELS CHRIS HANSEN IN RIVETING DRAMATIZATION OF ‘TO CATCH A PREDATOR’

Well, catastrophe quickly takes shape — what started as a small crack turned into an explosion seemingly in the blink of an eye, causing a massive ice shelf to break off and head straight to Europe. The worst fears of a tsunami and mass flooding impacting tens of millions of Europeans may become a reality.

The international dilemma puts Digger in the crosshairs — with President Compson (John Goodman) and his evangelical cabinet rushing to his remote taxidermy-filled estate to do damage control.

‘RESIDENT EVIL’ REVIEW: DIRECTOR ZACH CREGGER DELIVERS INFECTIOUS REBOOT TO GORY VIDEO GAME FRANCHISE

What's frustrating about "Digger" is that it has all the pieces of a great film. As much as there is to admire Cruise as an actor, his performance here feels like a mishmash of his past performances (see Les Grossman in "Tropic Thunder," or Frank T.J. Mackey in "Magnolia"). This has been positioned as the role that could finally earn him a competitive Oscar, but he and the rest of the top-tier cast give one-note performances, most of which involve yelling hysterically.

'THE DOG STARS' REVIEW: JACOB ELORDI FIGHTS FOR SURVIVAL IN RIDLEY SCOTT'S DULL POST-APOCALYPTIC WESTERN

Goodman's Compson clearly borrows elements from Donald Trump, but love or hate Trump, at least he's a nuanced man. Oscar-nominated German actress Sandra Hüller ("Anatomy of a Fall," "Project Hail Mary") is utterly wasted playing Digger's half sister Emma, spending all her screen time complaining how Digger's global disaster will negatively impact her environmental non-profit (which he funds anyway). The only cast member who remotely gives a compelling performance is Riz Ahmed, who plays the soft-spoken scientist who has been sounding the alarm about the consequences of Rockwell Corp's costly drilling.

Iñárritu, who directed and co-wrote 2014's Best Picture winner "Birdman or (The Unexpected Virtue of Ignorance)" — an actual great satire about showbiz — attempts to swing big here but ultimately strikes out. Unlike "Birdman," the laughs here are few and far between. Iñárritu takes bold narrative risks with plot twists that are commendable, yet there isn't enough for an audience to engage with.

"Digger" clearly tries to emulate Stanley Kubrick's 1964 Oscar-nominated classic "Dr. Strangelove or: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb," which is regarded as one of the greatest movie satires of all time. Instead, it's more like 2021's "Don't Look Up," the insufferable satire from Adam McKay that's a giant metaphor for climate change (of course, the Academy gave it a Best Picture nod). Both sacrifice humor for over-the-top preachiness.

The most redeeming aspect of "Digger" is that it was still incredibly well-crafted between the stunning visuals from Oscar-winning cinematographer Emmanuel Lubezki and the whimsical score from Cosmo Sheldrake.

BOX OFFICE COMEBACK: HOW SUMMER 2026 OFFERS A GLIMMER OF HOPE FOR HOLLYWOOD IN THE POST-COVID ERA

CLICK HERE FOR THE LATEST MEDIA AND CULTURE NEWS

Despite Cruise and Iñárritu's best efforts, "Digger" is truly a mess of a film that's unworthy of the work we're used to seeing from the two of them. You're better off revisiting "Dr. Strangelove," "Birdman" or any Cruise classic. It's easily the biggest misfire of awards season.

"Digger" is rated R for pervasive language. Running time: 2 hours, 9 minutes. In theaters now.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/opinion/digger-review-tom-cruise-destroys-planet-alejandro-inarritus-grandiose-messy-political-satire

posts.title: Virginia Tech's controversial missed field goal sparks fiery debate as different angles tell a different story
posts.excerpt: Fan video from around the stadium captures Virginia Tech Hokies kicker John Love's razor-thin field goal attempt in the 35-33 loss to Pittsburgh.
posts.content:
The Virginia Tech Hokies dropped their first game of the season Friday night, losing to Pittsburgh, 35-33, in an absolute thriller.

The Hokies led early. Pittsburgh stormed back. Both teams traded blows in the second half. Ultimately, the Hokies missed what would've been a game-winning kick wide to the left in the waning seconds.

And by "wide to the left," I mean ... well, I'm not sure.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The ball appeared to slip just inside the left upright by the slimmest of margins. I'm talking razor thin. I'm talking Florida-in-the-2000-election thin.

The fans, as you'll see, thought Va. Tech kicker John Love made the kick, thus sending the Hokies to the program's first 5-0 start in years. Love himself thought he made it, too.

The refs, though, threw a wet blanket on the whole thing.

Take a look:

Thoughts? First impressions?

Initially, I thought it was good. I was watching this game live, and couldn't figure out why the ESPN announcers weren't saying anything about it. They completely glossed over the entire thing. There was barely even a replay. It was insane.

I was screaming at my TV. I was sure it went in. I might still be?

MICHIGAN-WESTERN MICHIGAN CLOCK CONTROVERSY LEAVES PLAYERS, FANS AND A RULES ANALYST PUZZLED

Obviously, because we live in the social media era, other angles have emerged of the kick. Some help Virginia Tech's case, like this was taken from a fan directly behind the goal posts:

To me, that makes it look like a made field goal. The reaction from the students around this guy confirm that line of thinking. It looks good to me. It looked good to them.

Not all angles help Va. Tech, though. Others make the refs look like they got it right, which is hard to do given refs are generally terrible.

Like this one from behind the kicker, and off to the right:

You see? Now THAT one looks like he missed it. No good! Wide left. Game over. The zebras actually got a call right. Shocking!

But wait, there's more!

Like I said, we live in the social media age. Do you think anyone was watching that final kick without recording it? Of course not. We can't do anything without our phones nowadays. They own us.

This angle, from the other end of the field, swings me again:

See? Now I think it's good again! What a rush.

There's also that pesky NCAA rulebook, which provides even more context to the whole situation.

For those of you who wanted the play reviewed ... you can't.

On reviewable plays:

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Field goal attempts if and only if the ball is ruled (a) below or above the crossbar or (b) inside or outside the uprights when it is lower than the top of the uprights. If the ball is higher than the top of the uprights as it crosses the end line, the play may not be reviewed.

This one was not reviewable, based on that rule. It went above the uprights.

It's also important to note that the NFL and NCAA differ just a bit in their language regarding made field attempts. The college rulebook states the ball must cross "over the crossbar between the uprights of the receiving team’s goal."

The NFL rulebook specifically mentions what we saw last night:

The entire ball must pass through the vertical plane of the goal, which is the area above the crossbar and between the uprights or, if above the uprights, between their outside edges.

The NCAA rulebook doesn't say anything about the ball going above the uprights. Just "between" the uprights. Not saying that's the rule, just saying the rulebook leaves it out. Context is important.

OK, that's enough yapping out of me. What do you guys think?

Let me have it! Zach.Dean@OutKick.com.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/outkick-sports/virginia-tech-controversial-missed-field-goal-sparks-fiery-debate-different-angles-tell-different-story

posts.title: Court sentences woman to six months in prison for abusing minor in Imo
posts.excerpt: A Magistrate Court sitting in Imo State, has sentenced one Rose Okon to six months in prison for maltreating 14 year old niece in her care and inflicting multiple injuries on her. The Court, presided
posts.content:
A Magistrate Court sitting in Imo State, has sentenced one Rose Okon to six months in prison for maltreating 14 year old niece in her care and inflicting multiple injuries on her.

The Court, presided over by C.J Nkwoada, added that in lieu of the six months prison term, the convict can pay N50, 000 as fine.

Mrs Okon pleaded guilty when arraigned by the Police in the state on a one count charge bordering on assault.

The charge sheet read, “that you Rose Okon, on the 19th of September at 1800 hrs at Umuneke, Ngor Okpala in the Ngor Okpala Magisterial district did assault one Favour Emmanuel, 14 years by pouring on her hot water on her head and body which caused her grievous harm and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 355 of the criminal code Cap C38 laws of the Federation of Nigeria 2004 as applicable in Imo State of Nigeria.”

The prosecuting counsel, Sampson Obodo, showed the court photographs of the injuries the convict inflicted on the minor, and tendered the statements made at the police by the convict and the victim and that of a human rights organization.

Before the judgement, the culprit asked the court to have mercy on her, through her Counsel, Innocent Onyekwere, who asked the Court to be lenient while pronouncing the judgement.

The culprit was arrested following a petition by a human rights organization, Stand For Humanity Foundation.

The president of the foundation, Chidiebube Okeoma, who led over 20 members of the Organization to the Court, told Journalists that the organization initiated the arrest of the woman to remind people that child abuse is a punishable offence in law.

He said that the conviction and sentencing of the woman would serve as a lesson to all abusers of children.

Okeoma added that his foundation would continue to clampdown on all abusers of children.

He recalled that the foundation had on several occasions organised awareness campaigns against child abuse, following series of reports of abuse received by his office daily.

Court sentences woman to six months in prison for abusing minor in Imo

posts.title: Troost-Ekong calls for proper structure to help Super Eagles excel
posts.excerpt: Former Super Eagles captain William Troost-Ekong insisted that the right structure must be put in place for the team to strive on the international stage. The West Africans have failed to qualify for
posts.content:
Former Super Eagles captain William Troost-Ekong insisted that the right structure must be put in place for the team to strive on the international stage.

The West Africans have failed to qualify for the last two editions of the FIFA World Cup.

Nigeria have also started the qualifiers for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations on a shaky note.

The three-time African champions laboured to a 2-1 home win victory over Madagascar’s Barea, before they were thrashed 3-0 by the Wild Dogs of Guinea-Bissau in the second game.

Troost-Ekong said their must be level of consistency from the players, coaches and the Nigeria Football Federation, NFF.

“We are at a point where we need to see some consistency I think from the top down. From federation to coach to this group of players,” Troost-Ekong beIN SPORTS

“I think the talent is there in abundance. What we see now is still some uncertainty about how things are prepared for the team.

“Appointing Eric Chelle for the long term has been a great thing to do. He’s also in charge of the Olympic team. He understands the young players coming through.”

Troost-Ekong also believed a strong foundation must be built around the players if Nigeria is to compete consistently at the highest level.

“That consistency is number one. But I do think the team needs the structure and the backbone, and we can’t just rely on talent alone,” Troost-Ekong added.

“I think we’ve managed to cover a lot of gaps over the years. But now, over time, those things will get exposed. They need to have the right structure around it.”

Troost-Ekong calls for proper structure to help Super Eagles excel

posts.title: Tinubu avoided Nigeria’s insecurity crisis in Independence Day speech – Atiku’s aide
posts.excerpt: Paul Ibe, media aide to the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Atiku Abubakar, has criticised President Bola Tinubu over his Independence Day address, accusing him of fail
posts.content:
Paul Ibe, media aide to the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Atiku Abubakar, has criticised President Bola Tinubu over his Independence Day address, accusing him of failing to adequately address Nigeria’s worsening insecurity.

Ibe made the remarks in a post on X on Saturday while reacting to Tinubu’s Independence Day speech.

He said the President’s address was notable not only for what he said but also for what he allegedly avoided saying about insecurity in the country.

According to him, Tinubu made brief references to insecurity and thanked the security forces but failed to provide a detailed assessment of the killings, kidnappings, mass abductions and attacks on communities across the country.

Ibe said: “President Bola Tinubu’s Independence Day address was remarkable not only for what he said, but for what he carefully avoided saying.

“Yes, he made fleeting references to ‘insecurity’ and thanked the security forces. But on the pervasive insecurity confronting Nigerians today—the killings, kidnappings, mass abductions and communities living in fear—there was no serious accounting, no assessment of the crisis and no clear explanation of what his government intends to do differently.”

The former Atiku aide said the situation had made insecurity an “uncomfortable subject” for the administration.

Ibe argued that the government could not meaningfully discuss economic prosperity while insecurity continued to affect farmers, businesses, travellers and communities.

“You cannot talk seriously about prosperity while avoiding security. A farmer who cannot safely reach his farm cannot contribute to food security. A businessman afraid to travel cannot grow his business. Children who fear abduction cannot learn in peace,” he said.

He added that Nigerians deserved clear answers from Tinubu, as Commander-in-Chief, on why insecurity persisted, what had gone wrong, the progress recorded and what measures would be changed.

“Playing the ostrich cannot make the crisis disappear,” Ibe said.

He maintained that the protection of lives and property remained the primary responsibility of government and that Nigerians deserved more than a passing reference to insecurity in an Independence Day address.

“Insecurity cannot be wished away. It must be confronted, accounted for and defeated,” he added.

Tinubu avoided Nigeria’s insecurity crisis in Independence Day speech – Atiku’s aide

posts.title: Latest Ranking: 10 best universities in Africa
posts.excerpt: The University of Cape Town (UCT) has emerged as Africa’s highest-ranked university in the 2027 Times Higher Education World University Rankings, with the continent showing broader representation in t
posts.content:
The University of Cape Town (UCT) has emerged as Africa’s highest-ranked university in the 2027 Times Higher Education World University Rankings, with the continent showing broader representation in the latest global assessment.

UCT placed joint 147th in the world, improving from its joint 164th position in the previous edition, as universities across Africa continued to gain visibility in international higher education.

The latest ranking features 69 universities from sub-Saharan Africa, compared with 55 in the previous edition.

South Africa dominated the African list, accounting for most of the continent’s highest-ranked institutions. Universities from Morocco and Egypt also secured places among Africa’s leading institutions.

For the 2027 edition, Times Higher Education evaluated 2,297 universities in 118 countries and territories, making it the largest ranking exercise conducted by the organisation.

The ranking considers a range of measures, including teaching, research, research quality, industry engagement and international outlook.

Below are the 10 best-ranked universities in Africa in the 2027 Times Higher Education World University Rankings.

1. University of Cape Town — South Africa

The University of Cape Town retained the top position in Africa, ranking joint 147th globally with an overall score of 62.4.

Founded in 1829, UCT is based in Cape Town and is among the oldest universities on the continent.

Its academic structure comprises six faculties: Commerce, Engineering and the Built Environment, Health Sciences, Humanities, Law and Science.

UCT has 20,318 students, with women accounting for 57% and men 43%. International students make up 13% of the university’s total student population.

2. University of the Witwatersrand — South Africa

The University of the Witwatersrand, widely known as Wits, occupies the 301–325 bracket globally, recording an overall score between 53.4 and 54.8.

The institution traces its origins to the South African School of Mines, founded in Kimberley in 1896. It relocated to Johannesburg in 1904 before attaining full university status in 1922.

Wits has 26,766 students, comprising 61% women and 39% men. International students represent 5% of the population, while its student-to-staff ratio stands at 21.6:1.

3. Stellenbosch University — South Africa

Stellenbosch University ranks between 326th and 350th globally, with an overall score ranging from 52.3 to 53.3.

The institution began in 1918 with four faculties — Arts, Science, Education and Agriculture — and had 503 students and 40 lecturers at the time.

It has since expanded into a major institution operating across five campuses and 10 faculties.

The university has 27,676 students, with women representing 57% and men 43%. International students account for 7% of the student body.

4. University of Johannesburg — South Africa

The University of Johannesburg is placed in the 351–375 global range, posting an overall score of between 51.6 and 52.2.

The public university was established in 2005 following the merger of Rand Afrikaans University, Technikon Witwatersrand and parts of Vista University.

Since its creation, the institution has developed a strong profile in research, innovation and international partnerships.

The University of Johannesburg has 33,530 students, of whom 57% are women and 43% are men. International students constitute 13% of the student population.

5. Mohammed VI Polytechnic University — Morocco

Morocco’s Mohammed VI Polytechnic University is ranked 376–400 globally, with a score ranging from 50.5 to 51.5.

Established in 2016, the university forms part of the Green City project initiated by King Mohammed VI in 2009, with an emphasis on sustainable development, research and education.

6. University of Pretoria — South Africa

The South African university has nine faculties and a business school and places considerable emphasis on research and its wider impact.

It is also described as producing the largest number of graduates annually in South Africa.

The university has 31,305 students, with women accounting for 69% and men 31%. International students represent 9% of the student population, while the student-to-staff ratio is 17.6:1.

7. University of KwaZulu-Natal — South Africa

The University of KwaZulu-Natal occupies the 501–550 position range globally, with an overall score of 46.0–47.3.

The institution operates across five campuses and maintains links with more than 250 universities and other institutions around the world.

Its academic activities span a wide range of programmes, with research and international collaboration forming important parts of its profile.

UKZN has 34,947 students, comprising 62% women and 38% men. International students account for 1% of the student population, while the student-to-staff ratio is 31.9:1.

8. American University in Cairo — Egypt

American University in Cairo The American University in Cairo is ranked within the 701–800 bracket globally, with an overall score of 40.2–42.3.

Established in 1919, the Egyptian institution has 5,953 students. Women make up 58% of the student population, while men account for 42%.

International students represent 8% of its student body, and the university has a student-to-staff ratio of 10.8:1.

9. University of the Western Cape — South Africa

The University of the Western Cape shares the 701–800 global ranking bracket, with an overall score of 40.2–42.3.

Founded in 1959, the university has seven faculties, including its Faculty of Dentistry, which is recognised as one of South Africa’s leading dental schools.

The institution has 25,094 students, with women accounting for 64% and men 36%. International students make up 4% of the student population, while the student-to-staff ratio stands at 35.7:1.

10. Al-Azhar University — Egypt

Al-Azhar University completes the top 10 African universities, ranking between 801st and 1,000th globally with an overall score of 36.4–40.1.

Based in Cairo, the institution traces its origins to 970 AD and is widely regarded as one of the oldest universities in the world.

Although it formally became a university in 1961, its history spans more than 1,000 years.

Al-Azhar has a student population of 296,734, with women making up 61% and men 39%. International students account for 14% of the student body, while its student-to-staff ratio is 22.5:1.
