posts.title: INEC warns Nigerians against fake voter registration website
posts.excerpt: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has warned Nigerians against a fake website claiming that the online voter registration exercise is currently ongoing. The post INEC warns Nigerian
posts.content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has warned Nigerians against a fake website claiming that the online voter registration exercise is currently ongoing.

The commission, in a public notice on Saturday, said the website, pvc-inecnigeria-org.blogspot.com, falsely announced a nationwide registration window from September 28 to October 27, 2026.

INEC said the platform has no affiliation with the commission and urged Nigerians not to click on the link or provide personal information on the website.

“Members of the public are strongly advised not to click on the link or submit any personal information on the website, as doing so may expose them to the risk of having their sensitive personal data harvested or misused,” the notice posted on X reads.

“The Commission further wishes to clarify that the voter registration exercise closed on 26th July 2026. Any information suggesting that a new nationwide online voter registration exercise is currently ongoing through the above mentioned website is false.

“INEC urges the public to remain vigilant and to verify all electoral information through the Commission’s official communication channels.”

The website claims to offer a “Final Phase of Nationwide Online Voter Card Registration”, including services to update voter registration details, transfer registration to another polling unit, and replace damaged or lost permanent voter cards (PVCs), adding that voter registration and PVC delivery are free.

INEC urged Nigerians to remain vigilant and verify electoral information through the commission’s official communication channels.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/inec-warns-nigerians-against-fake-voter-registration-website/

posts.title: Russia warns diplomats, foreigners to leave Kyiv
posts.excerpt: Russia on Saturday issued a new call for diplomats and foreigners to leave Kyiv, warning the Ukrainian capital of new "massive" strikes The post Russia warns diplomats, foreigners to leave Kyiv appear
posts.content:
Russia on Saturday issued a new call for diplomats and foreigners to leave Kyiv, warning the Ukrainian capital of new “massive” strikes, in a statement by its foreign ministry.

Moscow has been pummelling Ukraine with drone and missile barrages throughout its offensive and in the past weeks has stepped up the strikes against Kyiv, targeting key infrastructure.

In a statement on Saturday, the Russian foreign ministry said it “had previously urged foreign nationals and diplomats in Kyiv to leave the city and refrain from visiting Ukraine.”

“We note with concern that not everyone has heeded these warnings, and that individuals are knowingly exposing themselves to mortal danger,” the ministry said.

“The Armed Forces of the Russian Federation will continue to deliver massive retaliatory strikes,” it warned.

It also stated that “responsibility for any potential negative consequences rests entirely with those who ignore this warning.”

On Friday, Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko said the city should now be on a war footing as the enemy was “tearing Kyiv apart” with strikes on bridges and energy infrastructure.

President Volodymyr Zelensky accused his Russian counterpart, Vladimir Putin, of ripping up the rulebook of armed conflict by sanctioning massive attacks on civilian areas, an accusation the Kremlin has rejected.

Former Minister of Transportation, Rotimi Amaechi, has blamed policies of President Bola Tinubu’s administration for contributing to the death of his mother, saying the rising cost of medicines made it difficult for his family to care for her.

Amaechi, who is the African Democratic Congress (ADC) vice-presidential candidate, made the claim during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today aired on Friday.

He said his mother had been healthy before Tinubu assumed office but became increasingly difficult to care for as the cost of drugs rose.

“Because policies are killing people. I’ve lost my mother,” he said.

posts.title: Over 57, 000 Women To Benefit As Shettima Launches Economic Fund In Katsina
posts.excerpt: The intervention, which will initially benefit women across Daura and Funtua Local Government Areas, is designed to expand economic opportunities, strengthen livelihoods and reduce poverty among poor
posts.content:
Vice President Kashim Shettima is set to launch the Nigeria for Women Programme Scale-Up (NFWP-SU) in Katsina State on Sunday, marking a major milestone in efforts to empower women economically, with 57,432 women expected to receive direct financial support under the Community Investment Fund (CIF).

The intervention, which will initially benefit women across Daura and Funtua Local Government Areas, is designed to expand economic opportunities, strengthen livelihoods and reduce poverty among poor and vulnerable households.

Addressing journalists in Katsina ahead of the launch, the State Commissioner for Women Affairs, Aisha Aminu Malumfashi, described the initiative as a transformative programme that will deepen women’s participation in economic activities through direct financial assistance and community-based support structures.

Under the programme, beneficiaries will be organised into Women Affinity Groups (WAGs), where they will build savings, access financial and non-financial services, strengthen their businesses and connect to wider markets.

World Bank Senior Social Development Specialist and Task Team Leader for the Nigeria for Women Programme, Michael Ilesanmi, and the State Commissioner for Women Affairs, Aisha Malumfashi, while addressing journalists in Katsina Ahead Of The Launch.

World Bank Senior Social Development Specialist and Task Team Leader for the Nigeria for Women Programme, Michael Ilesanmi, said the initiative is deliberately inclusive, stressing that every eligible woman aged 18 years and above, including persons with disabilities, can participate.

He explained that the programme will equip women with financial literacy, enterprise development skills and improved access to finance, markets and productive opportunities while helping them overcome social barriers that limit economic participation.

According to him, the project will also strengthen the resilience of women to climate change by supporting sustainable livelihood activities capable of generating income and improving household welfare.

Ilesanmi commended the Katsina State Government for expanding the programme from an initial six Local Government Areas to all 34 LGAs, revealing that the state has committed over ₦8.5 billion in counterpart funding over the past two years, with additional funding already earmarked in the next budget.

He disclosed that the expanded programme is expected to reach nearly 800,000 women across Katsina State, making it one of the largest women-focused economic empowerment initiatives in the country.

Implemented through a partnership involving the Federal Government, Katsina State Government, the World Bank, financial institutions, communities, women’s groups and other development partners, the programme is expected to usher in a new era of financial inclusion, enterprise development and economic empowerment for women across the state.

The official launch will bring together Federal and State Government officials, development partners, women’s organisations and other stakeholders to formally commence the next phase of the programme.

Source: https://www.channelstv.com/2026/10/03/over-57-000-women-to-benefit-as-shettima-launches-economic-fund-in-katsina/

posts.title: The 9.3 Million Nobody Owns
posts.excerpt: While Nigeria's politicians have been busy counting themselves, millions of young Nigerians have quietly acquired the power to count them. The post The 9.3 Million Nobody Owns appeared first on Channe
posts.content:
THE SIGNAL

Nigeria’s politicians have spent much of the past year counting.

Governors. Senators. Defectors. Endorsements. States they claim to control and political structures they insist they can “deliver.” But while the politicians were counting one another, 9.3 million young Nigerians quietly joined the voters’ register. That may prove to be the more important number.

INEC says 9,324,349 young Nigerians were newly registered during the 2026 Continuous Voter Registration exercise. Nine-point-three million. Not a rally crowd. Not social-media followers.

Not an opinion poll. But Potential voters. And with the presidential election approaching, they represent something every campaign desperately wants, but none can yet claim: an enormous pool of political possibility.

The temptation, of course, will be to colour them immediately. Obi? Atiku? Tinubu? Makinde?

Not so fast. Young Nigerians are not a political party. A 23-year-old graduate searching for work in Lagos does not necessarily see Nigeria through the same political lens as a young farmer outside Katsina, an apprentice in Aba, a trader in Kano or a first-time voter in Makurdi. They may share frustration. They may share ambition. They may even share anger. But shared emotion does not automatically produce a shared ballot. That is why 9.3 million registrations are not yet 9.3 million votes. And that may be the first lesson of this week’s Political Signals: The youth have entered the room. Nobody should presume to know where they will sit.

TINUBU’S BRIDGE: FROM REFORM TO PROSPERITY

President Bola Tinubu chose Independence Day to tell Nigerians that the painful surgery is ending.

His message, stripped to its political essentials, was simple: We have repaired the foundations. Now prosperity must follow.

“The emergency treatment is over,” the President declared, presenting an economy that is growing above four per cent, with moderating inflation, stronger reserves, a steadier foreign-exchange market and rising non-oil exports.

On a spreadsheet, the argument is becoming easier to make. At the kitchen table, it remains harder.

And elections are not decided on spreadsheets. They are decided in homes where the price of rice matters more than the level of foreign reserves; in markets where traders measure economic recovery by what customers can afford; and among young graduates for whom GDP growth means little if the next job application produces another silence. That is the bridge Tinubu must cross before January: from macroeconomics to the marketplace.

The CBN’s recent reset gives the government more ammunition. The benchmark interest rate has fallen from 26.5 per cent to 23 per cent. Inflation has moderated. GDP growth has strengthened.

The numbers are beginning to tell one story. But are Nigerians’ pockets telling the same story?

That is where economics becomes politics.

ATIKU: LOOK BEYOND THE NUMBERS

Atiku Abubakar is effectively asking voters to look away from the dashboard and through the windscreen. His Independence Day response focused on poverty, insecurity, purchasing power and the cost of living. And so the economic argument ahead of 2027 is becoming sharper.

Tinubu’s case is increasingly: The reforms are beginning to work. The opposition’s answer is: Then why can’t Nigerians feel them?

That may become one of the defining arguments of this election. Because governments campaign with statistics. Voters often vote with experience. And somewhere between those two lies January 16.

THE YOUTH METER STARTS TICKING

This is where those 9.3 million registrations become politically fascinating. Imagine the campaign through the eyes of a 25-year-old Nigerian. He hears that GDP is growing. But can he find work? She hears that inflation is falling. But has the food bill fallen? They hear that the naira is more stable. But can they start a business, pay rent, travel safely, obtain affordable credit, or imagine a future that does not begin with a visa application?

These are not abstract policy questions anymore. They are campaign questions. And no amount of dancing at youth rallies will answer them. The candidate who wants young voters will have to do more than appear young at heart. He will have to make the future believable.

THEN THERE IS THE GROUND GAME

There is another number worth remembering. Four out of five. That is the APC’s score from the recent legislative by-elections across Gombe, Kano, Bauchi and Delta. Five constituencies cannot forecast Nigeria. But elections leave footprints before they arrive. And these footprints tell us that organisation still matters. Social media can create momentum. Crowds can create spectacle. Opinion polls can create headlines. But Nigerian elections are eventually won and lost in less glamorous places: polling units, wards, local governments, collation centres. This is where enthusiasm must become organisation. Where supporters must become voters. Where popularity must acquire agents, logistics, lawyers, transport, data and discipline. The APC possesses a formidable political machine. The opposition’s challenge is not simply to demonstrate that Nigerians are unhappy. It must prove that unhappiness can be organised. Because anger that stays at home on election day is politically invisible.

WELCOME TO THE WIKE EXPERIMENT

And then there is Nyesom Wike. Nigeria’s political laboratory rarely lacks an experiment, and the FCT Minister may now be conducting one of the most interesting. Wike has publicly staked his political reputation on delivering Rivers State and the FCT for Tinubu. But his emerging cross-party “Rainbow Coalition” raises a larger question. Can you tell voters: Tinubu for President — but someone else further down the ballot? In other words, can political loyalty be sliced? Can a governor, minister, or godfather still “deliver” voters wholesale? Or has the Nigerian voter become increasingly comfortable shopping à la carte? President from Party A. Governor from Party B. Senator from Party C. If ticket-splitting grows, one of Nigerian politics’ oldest assumptions may need rewriting: that politicians own electoral territories. Rivers and the FCT could tell us a great deal about whether that assumption still holds.

With January approaching, five needles on the Political Signals dashboard deserve watching.

The Youth Meter. Registration has surged. Turnout is the next test.

The Pocketbook Meter. If inflation continues falling, when does statistical relief become household relief?

The Ground-Game Meter. Can opposition enthusiasm build an electoral machine capable of matching the APC ward for ward?

The Wike Meter. Can political influence still be transferred from politician to voter on command?

The Trust Meter. As INEC preparations accelerate, confidence in the electoral process itself will become increasingly important.

Those five indicators may tell us more about January than another photograph of politicians changing party scarves.

For months, Nigeria’s political class has behaved as though the 2027 election were a giant chessboard. Move a governor here. Capture a senator there. Flip a state. Build a coalition.

Break another coalition. Count the pieces.

But elections have an inconvenient habit of reminding politicians that voters are not chess pieces.

They move themselves. And 9.3 million newly registered young Nigerians have just moved onto the board. Nobody owns them. Not Tinubu. Not Atiku. Not Obi. Not Makinde. Not a governor. Not a godfather. They will have to be persuaded. They will have to believe that voting is worth their time.

And then they will actually have to turn up.

So perhaps the most important political question this Friday is not which politician has acquired another governor. It is much simpler. Who is acquiring voters? Because while Nigeria’s politicians have been busy counting themselves, millions of young Nigerians have quietly acquired the power to count them.

That is the Signal.

EDITORIAL NOTE

Political Signals is an independent weekly political analysis produced for Channels Television. It examines political developments, personalities and electoral trends without endorsement of any political party or candidate. Its assessments are based on publicly available evidence and may change as events and evidence develop.

Source: https://www.channelstv.com/2026/10/03/the-9-3-million-nobody-owns/

posts.title: You Failed As Speaker, Governor And Minister For 24 Years, Wike Fires Amaechi
posts.excerpt: The Minister declared that unlike past leaders who used their elevation to pull down others and monopolise power, his political philosophy centers on human capacity development, divine gratitude, and
posts.content:
Former Governor of Rivers State and Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has challenged the people of Evo Kingdom to point to any tangible development or political empowerment attracted to their land by his predecessor, Rotimi Amaechi, despite holding top political offices as Speaker, Governor, and Minister for 24 years.

​Speaking during an interactive session with leaders and stakeholders of Evo Kingdom in Obio-Akpor Local Government Area, Wike declared that unlike past leaders who used their elevation to pull down others and monopolise power, his political philosophy centers on human capacity development, divine gratitude, and uplifting his people.

​Wike questioned the moral right of those who spent decades in high offices without leaving behind a legacy of leadership or infrastructure in the area, warning against selfish politics that crumbles once the leader passes on.

​”Because how will I answer before God if these people could take that kind of risk, and opportunity came up for you to help, for you to uplift them? But because of your greed, because of your selfishness, you don’t want anybody to reach the level you are,” Wike said.

He said, “You don’t want anybody in Obio-Akpor to be governor again because you have become governor. God will not be happy with me”.

Wike speaking during an interactive session with leaders and stakeholders of Evo Kingdom in Obio-Akpor Local Government Area, in Rivers State.

​Taking direct aim at Amaechi’s 24-year tenure across various arms of government, Wike challenged the kingdom to present evidence of what was attracted to the land under his rival’s reign.

​”Someone was Speaker of the House of Assembly for eight years, Governor for eight years, and Minister for eight years—that is 24 years in top leadership positions! What can anybody point to that he attracted to Evo Kingdom or Rivers State in all those 24 years? Nothing! Not one single thing!

​”I was a Minister of State for Education, and as I sit here, I can count the projects I brought to Rivers State and my people. But somebody was Speaker, Governor, and headed a very lucrative ministry as a full Minister for eight years, yet brought nothing back home! How can someone who spent 24 years in power without empowering his people or raising new leaders now turn around to tell you he loves you?” Wike queried.

Wike during an interactive session with leaders and stakeholders of Evo Kingdom in Obio-Akpor Local Government Area, in Rivers State.

​Highlighting his political trajectory and contentment with his achievements under the administration of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, the FCT Minister stressed that he has no further personal political ambitions other than serving as a vessel for his people.

​”After all, what do I want that God has not given to me? Nothing! Nothing! Nothing! The only thing I ask from God today is to continue to give me long life,” he said.

“I can’t be a governor again. I’ve been a minister two times. I cannot be chairman of council again. So I am happy. I don’t have anything to lose”.

​He continued: “What leadership, as you are leaving, what’s the leadership you have kept behind to continue with where you have stopped? Because our problem here is that you just want only yourself. When you die, everything crumbles. That is not our own case.”

​Addressing political uncertainties and betrayal, the Minister reiterated his firm trust in God rather than human promises.

​”As a politician, I know that the only person who will not disappoint is God,” Wike declared.

“So, don’t ever believe that a human being will not disappoint you. No matter the love you have, do the best you can do. If the person disappoints you, don’t kill yourself. God will right the wrong”, he said.

Wike exchanging pleasantries during an interactive session with leaders and stakeholders of Evo Kingdom in Obio-Akpor Local Government Area, in Rivers State.

​Wike also recounted how his administration restructured the chieftaincy institution to give Evo Kingdom adequate representation in the Rivers State Council of Traditional Rulers, dismissing claims that traditional politics or native charms could intimidate him.

Political leaders and traditional rulers like Eze Temple Ejekwu and Elder Peter Chinwo, President of Evo Assembly, assured the FCT Minister of victory for the President and other candidates endorsed by the Rainbow Coalition.

Source: https://www.channelstv.com/2026/10/03/you-failed-as-speaker-governor-and-minister-for-24-years-wike-fires-amaechi/

posts.title: What CIPM’s 58th International Conference Revealed About Nigeria’s Changing Workplace
posts.excerpt: A job description written three years ago may already be struggling to describe the job being done today. The post What CIPM’s 58th International Conference Revealed About Nigeria’s Changing Workplace
posts.content:
From AI and productivity to leadership, skills and organisational culture, nearly 5,000 delegates gathered in Abuja for CIPM ICE 2026, regarded as Africa’s largest HR event. But beyond the numbers was a bigger question: how must organisations and the people who power them, reposition for what comes next?

A job description written three years ago may already be struggling to describe the job being done today.

Artificial intelligence is finding its way into everyday work. Employees are asking different questions of their employers. Leaders are under pressure to do more with less. Skills are becoming obsolete faster, and organisations are discovering that having talented people does not automatically translate into having a high-performing organisation.

Work has changed.

The more interesting question is whether the way we manage people has changed enough with it.

That question followed many of the conversations at the 58th International Conference and Exhibition of the Chartered Institute of Personnel Management of Nigeria (CIPM), held in Abuja from September 21–24, 2026, under the theme “Repositioning for Value and Impact.”

On paper, it sounds like the sort of phrase one might expect at a professional conference. But across four days of conversations among business leaders, policymakers, HR professionals, academics and other workplace thinkers, it became something far more practical: What exactly is HR doing that makes an organisation better?

It is a question worth asking.

The days of counting activities are disappearing

For years, much of HR’s success could be communicated in activities.

How many people were recruited? How many employees were trained? How many engagement programmes were organised? How quickly were vacancies filled?

Those things still matter but increasingly, organisations want to know what happened

because of them.

Did productivity improve? Are we retaining the people we cannot afford to lose? Are our managers becoming better leaders? Do we have the skills the business will need tomorrow? Is our culture helping or quietly frustrating our strategy?

Perhaps most importantly: can HR connect its work to results that matter to the

organisation?

That was one of the clearest threads running through the conversations in Abuja.

CIPM President and Chairman of the Governing Council, Mallam Ahmed Ladan Gobir, FCIPM,

fnli, put the challenge to delegates plainly: the real value of the conference would not be

determined by what happened inside the venue, but by what people did differently when they

returned to their organisations.

It is an important distinction.

A conference can fill notebooks. Impact has to show up somewhere else – in a better decision,

a stronger manager, a redesigned process, a more productive team, a problem solved or

perhaps even a difficult conversation an organisation has postponed for too long.

Then there is AI

It is almost impossible to have a serious conversation about the future of work today without

artificial intelligence entering the room.

The temptation is to reduce that conversation to one dramatic question: Will AI take people’s

jobs?

But the more useful questions are less dramatic and far more urgent.

Which parts of jobs will change? Which skills will become more valuable? What happens to roles that can now be partially automated? Who decides where AI should and should not be used? How do organisations protect judgement, accountability and trust while pursuing efficiency? and who prepares people for all of this?

That last question puts HR right in the middle of the conversation.

Technology decisions can no longer sit entirely with technology teams. If AI changes how work is performed, it changes jobs. If it changes jobs, it changes skills. And if it changes skills, it changes recruitment, learning, performance, workforce planning and leadership.

Suddenly, AI becomes a people issue too.

The challenge for HR is not to become the IT department. It is to understand technology well enough to ask better questions about its impact on people and the organisation.

Buying technology is relatively easy but building an organisation capable of using it well is harder.

Perhaps we have been talking about HR too narrowly

One of the more interesting things about a gathering of this nature is that the conversation eventually becomes bigger than the profession that convened it.

Talk about people for long enough and one inevitably begins to talk about productivity.

Talk about productivity and one arrives at competitiveness.

Talk about competitiveness in Nigeria and, sooner or later, there is a conversation about national development.

That is why what happens inside HR departments matters far beyond HR departments.

A factory with poorly trained people will feel it in its output. A bank with weak leadership will eventually feel it in performance. A government institution with the wrong culture will make citizens experience the consequences. A company that cannot retain critical talent will eventually discover the cost on its balance sheet.

People management, therefore, is not merely about keeping employees happy.

At its best, it is about creating the conditions in which people can do work that produces value. That is a much bigger responsibility and it explains why a CIPM conference increasingly brings together voices beyond traditional HR circles.

Nearly 5,000 people gathered for its conference but the number isn’t the story

The 58th International Conference and Exhibition attracted 4,905 delegates – 4,020 physically

and 885 virtually – drawn from public and private sector organisations.

For any professional gathering, those are significant numbers but attendance alone is an easy

metric.

The more consequential question is what happens when nearly 5,000 people return to thousands of different desks, teams, organisations and spheres of influence.

Does anything change?

That may be a better measure of the conference than the number of people who walked through its doors.

Because the danger with professional conferences is familiar.

People arrive enthusiastic, notes are taken, photographs are shared, business cards are

exchanged and LinkedIn fills with reflections.

Then Monday comes.

The inbox is waiting and the notebook joins several others on a shelf.

“Repositioning for Value and Impact” asks for something harder which is to Take something

back, change something and measure what happened.

HR itself is being asked to reposition

There is an irony in asking organisations to change if the profession responsible for much of that change remains the same.

Today’s HR professional needs a considerably broader toolkit.

Understanding people remains fundamental. But increasingly, so do data, technology, business models, finance, workforce planning, change, risk and commercial judgement.

The HR leader sitting with a CEO cannot speak only about HR. He or she must understand the business of the business.

What makes money? What destroys value? Where is the organisation going? What capabilities will it need to get there? What people risks could prevent it? What evidence supports the recommendation being made?

That shift from administrator to adviser, from activity to outcome, from intuition alone to evidence, is part of the repositioning taking place within the profession itself.

This is perhaps where CIPM’s role becomes most consequential.

As the statutory body responsible for regulating Human Resource Management practice in Nigeria, CIPM sits at an interesting intersection: between today’s HR profession and the one Nigeria will need tomorrow.

That means setting standards and developing professionals, certainly.

But it also means creating spaces where uncomfortable questions about the profession can be asked.

A conference in its 58th edition that only celebrates what HR already knows would have limited usefulness.

One that asks what HR needs to unlearn, relearn and become is a different proposition.

The real conference starts afterwards

By the time the final sessions ended in Abuja, delegates had heard a great deal about transformation, technology, leadership, capability, productivity and impact. But eventually, every conference badge comes off.

The stages are dismantled, exhibition stands disappear, delegates catch their flights and photographs move down social-media timelines.

What remains is what people do with what they heard.

For an HR professional, that might mean finally measuring the business effect of a programme instead of merely reporting that it happened.

For a CEO, it could mean bringing the people conversation into strategy earlier.

For a public-sector leader, it might mean asking whether existing systems make excellent performance easier or harder and; For an organisation experimenting with AI, it could mean spending as much time thinking about people and work redesign as it does thinking about software.

There will be another conference.

There will be another theme.

But the question left behind by CIPM’s 58th International Conference and Exhibition is worth carrying beyond Abuja:

What are we doing differently because the world of work is different?

For HR, that question is becoming increasingly difficult to avoid and that is precisely the point.

Repositioning begins when the old position is no longer enough.

Source: https://www.channelstv.com/2026/10/02/what-cipms-58th-international-conference-revealed-about-nigerias-changing-workplace/

posts.title: Referee selected for next Italy match against Turkey on October 5
posts.excerpt: Polish referee Szymon Marciniak has been selected as the referee for the upcoming Nations League...
posts.content:
Polish referee Szymon Marciniak has been selected as the referee for the upcoming Nations League match between Italy and Turkey on Monday, October 5.

Marciniak to referee Italy vs. Turkey

Italy will host Turkey at the Dall’Ara in Bologna on Monday evening for their fourth and final Nations League match of the extra-long September-October international break.

BURSA, TURKEY – SEPTEMBER 28: Michael Kayode of Italy crosses the ball under pressure from Eren Elmal of Turkiye during the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Türkiye and Italy at Atatürk Spor Kompleksi Matli Stadyumu on September 28, 2026 in Bursa, Turkey. (Photo by Ahmad Mora/Getty Images)Roberto Mancini and Vincenzo Montella’s sides have already met once this break, in Bursa last week, which the Azzurri won 4-1 thanks to goals from Alessandro Bastoni, Davide Frattesi, Michael Kayode and Pio Esposito.

Italy have since drawn 1-1 away against France on Friday evening and were beaten 2-0 by Belgium just before their 4-1 victory away against Turkey.

The match officials for the next game against Turkey have now been confirmed: It will be a Polish officiating team led by Marciniak and assistants Tomasz Listkiewicz and Adam Kupsik and fourth official Karol Arys. Piotr Lasyk will be the video assistant referee and Swizz Lukas Faehndrich will be his assistant.

ISTANBUL, TURKEY – JUNE 10: Kevin De Bruyne of Manchester City looks on as Matteo Darmian of FC Internazionale interacts with Referee Szymon Marciniak during the UEFA Champions League 2022/23 final match between FC Internazionale and Manchester City FC at Ataturk Olympic Stadium on June 10, 2023 in Istanbul, Turkey. (Photo by Shaun Botterill/Getty Images)This is a slightly worrying omen for Italy, as they have not won any of their previous four matches that have been refereed by Marciniak.

Marciniak was also the man with the whistle for Italy’s 3-3 draw with Germany in the second leg of their Nations League quarter-final back in 2025. He also took charge of Italy’s 2-0 loss against Switzerland in the EURO 2024 round of 16, a 0-0 draw against England in the Nations League in 2022 and a 3-1 friendly defeat against Belgium all the way back in 2015.

Marciniak was also the referee for the 2023 Champions League final when Inter were defeated 1-0 by Manchester City in Istanbul. He has also refereed a World Cup final, between victors Argentina and runners-up France in Qatar in 2022.

Source: https://football-italia.net/referee-selected-for-next-italy-match-turkey/

posts.title: Italy beat 10-year statistic in first-half performance in 1-1 draw away against France
posts.excerpt: Italy picked up an encouraging 1-1 draw away against France on Friday evening, and in...
posts.content:
Italy picked up an encouraging 1-1 draw away against France on Friday evening, and in doing so, had more first-half shots against Les Bleues on their home patch than any national team since the semi-finals of EURO 2016.

No side has had more first-half shots away against France than Italy over the last 10 years

Roberto Mancini’s second spell in charge of the Azzurri has started with a 2-0 defeat at home against Belgium, but he has since bounced back with two impressive away results against Turkey (1-4) and France (1-1) this week.

Sandro Tonali of Italy salutes coach Roberto Mancini after his substitution against France in the Nations League MD3 (@azzurri)Given Italy’s recent failure to qualify for the 2026 World Cup and France’s status as semi-finalists in 2026, finalists in 2022 and winners in 2018, a draw at the Stade de France was seen as a positive outcome by many across the peninsula, even if Mancini seemed disappointed to have to settle for a point at full-time.

Even if reports in France claim that the home side dominated and that the visitors were fortunate to have a goalkeeper as strong as Gianluigi Donnarumma, there is an encouraging first-half statistic that shows Italy did try to take the game to Zinedine Zidane’s side.

Italy ended the first 45 minutes in Paris with eight shots attempted, which is more than any other nation playing away against France since the semi-final of EURO 2016: Germany registered 11 on their way to a 2-0 defeat in Marseille that evening.

Source: https://football-italia.net/italy-beat-10-year-stat-away-against-france/

posts.title: Mancini’s full-time reaction shows Italy weren’t happy to settle for a draw vs. France
posts.excerpt: Italy supporters have taken positively to Roberto Mancini’s frustrated full-time reaction after Friday night’s 1-1...
posts.content:
Italy supporters have taken positively to Roberto Mancini’s frustrated full-time reaction after Friday night’s 1-1 draw away against France, as they feel that it shows the Azzurri were not satisfied with settling for a point away against one of the strongest nations in the world.

Mancini wasn’t happy to settle for a draw in France 1-1 Italy

Italy came from behind to secure a 1-1 draw away against France in the Nations League on Friday evening with second-half goals from Michael Olise and Alessandro Bastoni at the Stade de France.

Alessandro Bastoni celebrates scoring the equaliser against France in the Nations League MD3 (@azzurri)Mancini’s second spell as head coach of the Italy national team has brought four points from three matches following a 2-0 defeat at home against Belgium, a 4-1 win away against Turkey and Friday’s 1-1 draw away against France.

Given that 2026 had been a year of disappointment for the Azzurri prior to the September-October international break, a draw away against World Cup semi-finalists and 2018 champions France was seen as a positive outcome by most.

However, Mancini’s frustrated reaction when the full-time whistle blew, when Italy were in possession in the France half, shows that the CT wasn’t happy to just settle for a point, but that he thought the Azzurri could go on and win it in the closing stages.

FIN DU MATCH : FRANCE 1-1 ITALIE

La réaction de Roberto Mancini au coup de sifflet final, alors que l’Italie avait la possession…

[@MattheoTrn]#FranciaItalia #NationsLeague#Nazionale #Azzurri #VivoAzzurro pic.twitter.com/orbR3VkzwJ

— Team Serie A (@teamserieafr) October 2, 2026

posts.title: Spence plays first 50 minutes for Inter in 2-0 training ground friendly victory
posts.excerpt: England international Djed Spence picked up his first minutes in an Inter shirt on Saturday...
posts.content:
England international Djed Spence picked up his first minutes in an Inter shirt on Saturday afternoon as the Nerazzurri players who remained in Milan for the international break beat Lumezzane 2-0 in a training ground friendly on Saturday.

Inter took on Serie C side Lumezzane in a 70-minute friendly at the club’s training ground on Saturday, claiming a 2-0 victory thanks to goals from Henrikh Mkhitaryan and 20-year-old Richi Agbonifo.

Cristian Chivu was able to name a relatively competitive side featuring the likes of Marcus Thuram, Curtis Jones, Federico Dimarco, Yann Bisseck and Spence, who were either not selected by their nations or have already returned from international duty.

MADRID, SPAIN – SEPTEMBER 08: Cristian Chivu, Manager of Internazionale, looks on before the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD1 match between Real Madrid C.F. and FC Internazionale Milano at Estadio Santiago Bernabeu on September 08, 2026 in Madrid, Spain. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)Dimarco had withdrawn from the Italy national team squad at the beginning of the September-October break, but was fit enough to play all 70 minutes in Saturday’s friendly.

Spence, who is yet to make his first appearance for Inter after completing his €35m transfer from Tottenham over the summer, played the first 35-minute half plus 15 minutes of the second half in what was his first Nerazzurri outing.

Djed Spence is welcomed to Serie A champions Inter in the trophy room after his move from Tottenham Hotspur (inter.it)The Nerazzurri were without Italy internationals Alessandro Bastoni, Nicolo Barella and Pio Esposito, plus Lautaro Martinez, Ange-Yoan Bonny, Petar Sucic, Andy Diouf, Piotr Zielinski, Josep Martinez, Manuel Akanji and Aleksandar Stankovic, who are all still away with their national teams.

posts.title: MAGA mom's dire warning over tech guardrails as Trump puts pedal to the metal on race with China
posts.excerpt: Amy Kremer's Humans First organization demands AI guardrails to protect children from chatbot dangers and prevent mass displacement of American workers.
posts.content:
A conservative political activist who has been deeply entrenched in right-wing politics for decades is calling on the government to implement safety guardrails on artificial intelligence (AI), especially when it comes to protecting children and ensuring that the booming technology doesn't displace American workers en masse.

"If something happens with one of these companies, whether it's a child taking their own life due to suicide by manipulation with a chatbot, these companies are not required to report it to the federal government," Amy Kremer told Fox News Digital.

Kremer is the chairwoman of Humans First, a gorup that advocates for government safeguards on the technology and says it gives the American people a voice in the AI conversation, rather than leaving all the power in the hands of what it calls "Big AI globalists" who have little concern for ordinary Americans.

MIKE JOHNSON REJECTS AI MORATORIUM OVER CHINA THREAT AS CONSERVATIVE ACTIVIST DEMANDS GUARDRAILS

"We are a grassroots organization focused on putting guardrails and safety mechanisms in place around AI technology in order to protect the American people, our children, jobs and so forth, and also to put those guardrails in place to to make sure that the people have a seat at the table and a voice in the conversation about what goes into their community," Kremer said.

Kremer, who is known by the political right for her time as a Tea Party advocate and ferocious fighter for President Donald Trump's MAGA movement, mentioned the 2025 mass shooting at Florida State University, which claimed the lives of two people and injured six others, as an instance of AI gone wrong.

Court documents in that case claim that the alleged shooter, Phoenix Ikner, used ChatGPT to plan aspects of the shooting. The company was sued by the wife of one of the deceased victims, and the state of Florida took the rare step of opening a criminal investigation into the company.

"If a chatbot is used in planning a school shooting like what happened at Florida State University in April of 2025, they're not required to report that to the federal government," said Kremer. "The only reason we know about a number of these things that have happened is because of lawsuits that have been filed by the victims and/or their families."

She argued that as a former flight attendant, she had to report every issue on an airliner to the government. And just as hospitals, pharmaceutical companies and hordes of other industries are regulated under the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), Kremer believes that AI companies should face similar scrutiny.

FOX NEWS POLL: VOTERS QUESTION WHETHER AI’S PROMISE OUTWEIGHS ITS RISKS

AI is a hotly-contested issue ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, with some Democrats looking to reign in the technology while the Trump administration hoping to keep competition and innovation flowing in the effort to win the AI race with China.

But Kremer is far from a Democrat, and she wants also wants the United States to crush China in the race for technological dominance.

"I want America to win this AI race, I absolutely I do. I'm America first, always have been, and we've led the world on innovation and ingenuity," she said. "But again ... I go back to, you don't have to forego safety to have innovation and ingenuity."

"I'm not siding with the Democrats," Kremer said. "I am not a tech person. I'm not anti-AI. I'm not anti-technology. I'm not anti-data center."

"I am a mom with common sense and I'm a conservative, and it only makes sense that guardrails are put in place," she added.

After all, Kremer said, AI companies aren't partisan actors.

TRUMP'S AI RACE WITH CHINA COULD BECOME THE BIGGEST MISTAKE OF OUR TIME

"They don't care about Republicans, they don't care about Democrats, they don't care about Americans. At the end of the day, I think they care about their own companies and their technology, and that's what, what drives them," she said. "And so, everything with these guys I think is contractual, you know, it's not, 'these are my friends, these are the people, I have the same ideology.' It's contractual, it's what benefits them and I think that's why they've cozied up to President Trump and Republicans in this administration and Congress."

In a high-stakes summit in Washington, D.C., last week, AI was a hot topic of discussing between Chinese President Xi Jinping and Trump, though what exactly was discussed remains under wraps.

"The Trump administration’s priority is to ensure there is a booming economy so that workers have many opportunities and experience limited volatility from any short-term disruptions," a White House official told Fox News Digital. "The goal is for workers to continue to have access to high paying jobs and that workers can easily adapt to new technologies and processes."

OBAMA CRITICIZES TRUMP ON APPROACH TO AI, ESCALATES WARNING FOR STRONGER REGULATION

As for children's safety, the official pointed Fox News Digital to its National Policy Framework on Artificial Intelligence.

That framework calls on Congress to implement a number of AI child safety measures, including empowering parents with tools to control their children's content exposure, privacy settings, content exposure and account controls.

It also asks the lawmaking body to "establish commercially reasonable, privacy protective, age assurance requirements (such as parental attestation) for AI platforms and services likely to be accessed by minors," and ensure that AI platforms implement safeguards against child sexual exploitation and self-harm.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/politics/maga-mom-dire-warning-tech-guardrails-trump-pedal-metal-race-china

posts.title: One group of married Americans is having more sex — and happier marriages
posts.excerpt: Institute for Family Studies research finds regular churchgoers report more frequent sex and greater sexual satisfaction than nonreligious spouses.
posts.content:
Married couples who regularly attend church report having more frequent sex and greater sexual satisfaction than those who attend less often or not at all, according to a new report from the Institute for Family Studies (IFS) in Charlottesville, Virginia.

Researchers analyzed findings from multiple datasets, including the 2026 IFS Religion and Family Survey of 3,125 married adults ages 18–54, the long-running nationally representative General Social Survey, and a separate survey of 1,219 alumni of FOCUS, a Catholic campus ministry.

Regular churchgoers reported having more frequent sex than less religious or non-religious married adults, with regularly attending Catholics reporting some of the highest levels of sexual frequency. The association remained even after accounting for demographic differences.

COMMON MARRIAGE HABIT COULD QUIETLY KILL YOUR SEX LIFE, EXPERT WARNS

Among married adults ages 20 to 54, 62% of regular churchgoers reported having sex at least once a week, compared with 48% of nonreligious spouses, according to the report.

In addition to frequency, sexual satisfaction was also higher among church attendants. Catholics and Protestants who regularly attended religious services were more likely to rate their sex lives positively than those who attended less often or had no religious affiliation.

Daily prayer was linked to greater sexual satisfaction among married Catholics and Protestants, though it was not associated with more frequent sex.

Among churchgoers, 55% of Catholics and 45% of Protestants rated their sex lives as "excellent" or "very good," compared with 45% of nominal Catholics, 35% of nominal Protestants and 40% of religiously unaffiliated respondents.

‘QUIET QUITTING’ IN MARRIAGE: THE SUBTLE SIGNS A SPOUSE HAS EMOTIONALLY CHECKED OUT

Those who viewed marriage as a permanent commitment were more likely to report both frequent and satisfying sex. That belief, along with shared values, was also strongly associated with overall marital quality.

Because the analysis was observational, it cannot determine whether religious practice directly causes better marital or sexual outcomes, the authors acknowledged.

Additionally, the marital outcomes were self-reported, and other unmeasured differences between religious and non-religious respondents could have influenced the results.

Differences in factors such as age and length of marriage could also make it challenging to strike comparisons with the broader population.

The study was funded by FOCUS, the Fellowship of Catholic University Students.

Jessica Steinman, a licensed marriage and family therapist and certified sex addiction therapist in Los Angeles, spoke with Fox News Digital about the potential relationship between religious activity and the quality of a couple’s sex life.

"When we think of people who are really involved in religion … we might think they're not having a lot of sex or that they're having very constricted views on their sex lives," she said. "And this article and research show that's changing."

WHY COUPLES SHOULD FLIRT WITH EACH OTHER EVERY DAY — PLUS THE ‘RED FLAG’ TO AVOID

People who actively participate in a shared spiritual or religious life may also feel more connected to one another as partners, according to Steinman, who is also the chief clinical officer for No Matter What Recovery in Los Angeles, Chicago and Austin.

"If they're showing up and looking at things outside themselves — things that are spiritual, things that are religious, things are having them look inward, things that are having them look into larger morals and values within their marriages and partnerships — I think they're going to possibly have happier marriages and partnerships," the therapist said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

They may also be more vulnerable and open with one another, which could contribute to a more active sex life, she added.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

The rituals and shared practices associated with religious life likely play a role in strengthening that connection, the expert suggested.

"Certain religious settings are really focused on rituals and traditions," Steinman said. "And if you're looking at partnership and marriage … engaging in sexual connection and sexual intimacy can really become a ritual itself."

The research highlighted what has been described as an ongoing "sex recession," where people are not engaging in sexual intimacy as much as they once did.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Regardless of religious affiliation, Steinman encourages people to find ways to connect with their partners.

"Get off the phones, get off of the internet, turn the TV off and start really connecting with your partner," she advised.

Steinman suggested that partners engage with one another and build connections that go deeper than simply asking, "How was your day?"

That can include building emotional openness and discussing how partners want to connect sexually, she said.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/health/group-married-americans-having-more-sex-happier-marriages

posts.title: JACK CARR: The lesson from FlyDubai is simple. Be ready to save yourself
posts.excerpt: The FlyDubai Flight 1073 knife attack over Saudi Arabia exposes critical gaps in pilot screening and cockpit security that demand new reforms.
posts.content:
The events on FlyDubai Flight 1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv on 30 September 2026 reads like something out of one of my thrillers. But what occurred in the skies over Saudi Arabia was not fiction, it was real world and highlights an adage I learned long ago and has been repeated in various incarnations across social channels with differing attributions over the years — hope is not a course of action, in most cases, no one is coming to save you, you will need to be your own cavalry.

That means be prepared.

I am actually surprised that this or something like this has not happened previously — an unhinged pilot or co-pilot killing the other, perhaps suicidal, perhaps in search of martyrdom, as what some terrorist organizations call an istishhadi or "martyrdom seeker."

FORMER ISRAELI PM HAILS ‘HEROISM’ AFTER PASSENGERS HELP THWART ALLEGED COCKPIT ATTACK

With prior planning it is possible for pilots to work together in a "martyrdom operation" that would be much harder to thwart. Or a single pilot or co-pilot could work with other "muscle" sitting in first class to prevent passengers from doing what they did on September 30, giving the terrorist in the cockpit time to kill them all or once again turn an airliner into a weapon focused on a specific target.

I think about scenarios like this every time I fly.

I look at and evaluate the passengers, the flight attendants, and I always look in on the pilots as I enter the aircraft, searching for anything that does not look or feel right, remembering something a Vietnam-era Project Delta Army Special Forces soldier told me decades ago: "if it doesn’t look right, it’s probably not."

Trust your instincts — you have them for a reason.

I am also identifying assets and liabilities among those groups. Who is a potential asset if things go south? I’m noting shoes, belts, shirts, watches, hats, bags, sunglasses, tattoos, cauliflower ear, and filing away what that tells me about each person. Which of them are likely to help — and which of them may hinder in the event of an incident.

On September 30, the skies over Saudi Arabia were full of miracles. The pilot, Captain Smit Machchhar, was not immediately incapacitated in the initial knife attack and managed to open the cockpit door before collapsing. Passengers with the instinct to act, fight, and prevail were sitting near the front of the plane, one of the passengers had the wherewithal to pull back on the controls — something he remembered from watching a television show.

HERO FLYDUBAI PILOT SAYS HE WAS 'FIGHTING FOR MY LIFE' AS PLANE PLUNGED AFTER COPILOT ATTACK

And there happened to be a pilot or pilots onboard who were able land the plane. Incredible.

If any one of those things had not happened, we would be talking about a very different incident, one in which every single person on that flight is dead.

I weave a lot of history and the history of terrorism into my thrillers, and I also have a series of non-fiction books on terrorism, the second of which is on Pan Am 103, a plane that exploded over Lockerbie, Scotland, on December 21, 1988, killing 259 passengers and crew and 11 residents on the ground. In that attack, there was no warning — a bomb detonated in the cargo hold at 31,000 feet.

The destruction of Pan Am 103 horrified the world — and led to important changes in airline security, thanks in large part to pressure from victims’ families who pushed lawmakers to pass the Aviation Security Improvement Act of 1990. That legislation heightened the focus on domestic and international security, including placing federal security managers at major airports and requiring background checks on all air carrier workers. The law demanded the FAA work in tandem with the FBI, expanded scrutiny of overseas airports, and improved the flow of terrorist threat information.

AMERICA BUILT A FORTRESS AFTER 9/11. THEN THE THREAT STARTED HIDING IN PLAIN SIGHT

The recent FlyDubai event should lead to changes as well, namely enhanced pilot screenings. It is not just about qualifications and your ability to fly a plane — it’s about your background, associations, and your mental stability.

If, for example, a background check finds that instead of funding your 401(k) each month, you are diverting funds to Hezbollah or a charity funding terrorist organizations — an obvious red flag — you should not be a pilot and certainly should not be flying a plane full of Israelis into Tel Aviv.

This is common sense to most, but common sense seems to be in limited supply these days.

The model for hijackings and the use of terror focused on airlines was different before September 11, 2001. Typically, in the 1970s and 1980s, planes were hijacked and the passengers were exchanged for prisoners or ransomed — sometimes a passenger or passengers were killed to make a point.

SEN MCCORMICK: THE HEROIC PASSENGERS OF FLIGHT 93 SHOWED AMERICA HOW TO STAND UNITED

From a tactical security standpoint that meant that you would want a window seat so you were not in the aisle where you could be struck and injured or grabbed by a terrorist — you wanted to be able to survey the situation, bide your time, and act when appropriate.

On September 11, 2001, that paradigm shifted — planes and passengers were not being hijacked to bring about a political end or for a ransom, they were being turned into weapons. That adaptation by terrorists meant protectors needed to act quickly in the event of a hijacking. They moved from window seats to aisle seats to be in an advantageous position to recognize the threat and take immediate decisive action. And by "protectors" I do not mean military or law enforcement, I mean citizens. I am referring to those who have not suppressed the will to fight and have not outsourced their protection to a government or outside entity who is not coming to save them.

Protecting those who cannot protect themselves is our responsibility as citizens, as husbands, as fathers. The FlyDubai incident is an example of that duty and of the warrior mindset — from the pilot to the passengers who all acted heroically to save the day.

Col. John Boyd developed something called the OODA Loop — Observe, Orient, Decide, Act. In combat, in most cases, whoever does that faster than their opponent — or who can disrupt their enemy in the middle of their loop — will be victorious. That is what the pilot and passengers did on the FlyDubai flight. They stepped up and tapped into that primal urge to live and to protect that is in all of our DNA — and they prevailed.

The enemy will learn and adapt to September 30, 2026.

Next time it might be both pilots or it might be one incapacitating the other, working in conjunction with a passenger or passengers who will block access to the cockpit. We must adapt as well to ensure those with mental disorders or associations with terrorist organizations or those who fund them are kept from the ranks of the aviators we all trust with our lives.

As John Steinbeck writes in The Acts of King Arthur and his Noble Knights, "‘Now — I will lay down the law, and you will learn it word by word, and every word must be edged with fire. This is the law. The purpose of fighting is to win. There is no possible victory in defense. The sword is more important than the shield, and skill is more important than either. The final weapon is the brain, all else is supplementary.’"

Remember — hope is not a course of action.

In most cases, no one is coming to save you. Your mind is the ultimate weapon, and you will need it, coupled with the will to fight, to save yourself and your loved ones, and in this case, an entire plane full of innocent people.

Be prepared.

posts.title: 'Digger' Review: Tom Cruise destroys the planet in Alejandro Iñárritu's grandiose, messy political satire
posts.excerpt: Fox News Digital reviews Warner Bros. Pictures' "Digger" starring Tom Cruise, John Goodman, Riz Ahmed, Sandra Hüller and Jesse Plemons. Directed by Alejandro Iñárritu.
posts.content:
A great satire must be two things: innovative and funny. Unfortunately for Tom Cruise and Oscar-winning director Alejandro G. Iñárritu, "Digger" is neither of those things.

Cruise is nearly unrecognizable, buried under layers upon layers of prosthetics transforming himself into Digger Rockwell, an eccentric oil tycoon who has affection for his wealth and his chronically ill robotic-like cat Maggie.

Digger doesn't like to take no for an answer, even as he's repeatedly warned that a crack at his oil drilling site in Greenland could lead to catastrophe.

‘PRIMETIME’ REVIEW: ROBERT PATTINSON CHANNELS CHRIS HANSEN IN RIVETING DRAMATIZATION OF ‘TO CATCH A PREDATOR’

Well, catastrophe quickly takes shape — what started as a small crack turned into an explosion seemingly in the blink of an eye, causing a massive ice shelf to break off and head straight to Europe. The worst fears of a tsunami and mass flooding impacting tens of millions of Europeans may become a reality.

The international dilemma puts Digger in the crosshairs — with President Compson (John Goodman) and his evangelical cabinet rushing to his remote taxidermy-filled estate to do damage control.

‘RESIDENT EVIL’ REVIEW: DIRECTOR ZACH CREGGER DELIVERS INFECTIOUS REBOOT TO GORY VIDEO GAME FRANCHISE

What's frustrating about "Digger" is that it has all the pieces of a great film. As much as there is to admire Cruise as an actor, his performance here feels like a mishmash of his past performances (see Les Grossman in "Tropic Thunder," or Frank T.J. Mackey in "Magnolia"). This has been positioned as the role that could finally earn him a competitive Oscar, but he and the rest of the top-tier cast give one-note performances, most of which involve yelling hysterically.

'THE DOG STARS' REVIEW: JACOB ELORDI FIGHTS FOR SURVIVAL IN RIDLEY SCOTT'S DULL POST-APOCALYPTIC WESTERN

Goodman's Compson clearly borrows elements from Donald Trump, but love or hate Trump, at least he's a nuanced man. Oscar-nominated German actress Sandra Hüller ("Anatomy of a Fall," "Project Hail Mary") is utterly wasted playing Digger's half sister Emma, spending all her screen time complaining how Digger's global disaster will negatively impact her environmental non-profit (which he funds anyway). The only cast member who remotely gives a compelling performance is Riz Ahmed, who plays the soft-spoken scientist who has been sounding the alarm about the consequences of Rockwell Corp's costly drilling.

Iñárritu, who directed and co-wrote 2014's Best Picture winner "Birdman or (The Unexpected Virtue of Ignorance)" — an actual great satire about showbiz — attempts to swing big here but ultimately strikes out. Unlike "Birdman," the laughs here are few and far between. Iñárritu takes bold narrative risks with plot twists that are commendable, yet there isn't enough for an audience to engage with.

"Digger" clearly tries to emulate Stanley Kubrick's 1964 Oscar-nominated classic "Dr. Strangelove or: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb," which is regarded as one of the greatest movie satires of all time. Instead, it's more like 2021's "Don't Look Up," the insufferable satire from Adam McKay that's a giant metaphor for climate change (of course, the Academy gave it a Best Picture nod). Both sacrifice humor for over-the-top preachiness.

The most redeeming aspect of "Digger" is that it was still incredibly well-crafted between the stunning visuals from Oscar-winning cinematographer Emmanuel Lubezki and the whimsical score from Cosmo Sheldrake.

BOX OFFICE COMEBACK: HOW SUMMER 2026 OFFERS A GLIMMER OF HOPE FOR HOLLYWOOD IN THE POST-COVID ERA

CLICK HERE FOR THE LATEST MEDIA AND CULTURE NEWS

Despite Cruise and Iñárritu's best efforts, "Digger" is truly a mess of a film that's unworthy of the work we're used to seeing from the two of them. You're better off revisiting "Dr. Strangelove," "Birdman" or any Cruise classic. It's easily the biggest misfire of awards season.

"Digger" is rated R for pervasive language. Running time: 2 hours, 9 minutes. In theaters now.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/opinion/digger-review-tom-cruise-destroys-planet-alejandro-inarritus-grandiose-messy-political-satire

posts.title: Virginia Tech's controversial missed field goal sparks fiery debate as different angles tell a different story
posts.excerpt: Fan video from around the stadium captures Virginia Tech Hokies kicker John Love's razor-thin field goal attempt in the 35-33 loss to Pittsburgh.
posts.content:
The Virginia Tech Hokies dropped their first game of the season Friday night, losing to Pittsburgh, 35-33, in an absolute thriller.

The Hokies led early. Pittsburgh stormed back. Both teams traded blows in the second half. Ultimately, the Hokies missed what would've been a game-winning kick wide to the left in the waning seconds.

And by "wide to the left," I mean ... well, I'm not sure.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The ball appeared to slip just inside the left upright by the slimmest of margins. I'm talking razor thin. I'm talking Florida-in-the-2000-election thin.

The fans, as you'll see, thought Va. Tech kicker John Love made the kick, thus sending the Hokies to the program's first 5-0 start in years. Love himself thought he made it, too.

The refs, though, threw a wet blanket on the whole thing.

Take a look:

Thoughts? First impressions?

Initially, I thought it was good. I was watching this game live, and couldn't figure out why the ESPN announcers weren't saying anything about it. They completely glossed over the entire thing. There was barely even a replay. It was insane.

I was screaming at my TV. I was sure it went in. I might still be?

MICHIGAN-WESTERN MICHIGAN CLOCK CONTROVERSY LEAVES PLAYERS, FANS AND A RULES ANALYST PUZZLED

Obviously, because we live in the social media era, other angles have emerged of the kick. Some help Virginia Tech's case, like this was taken from a fan directly behind the goal posts:

To me, that makes it look like a made field goal. The reaction from the students around this guy confirm that line of thinking. It looks good to me. It looked good to them.

Not all angles help Va. Tech, though. Others make the refs look like they got it right, which is hard to do given refs are generally terrible.

Like this one from behind the kicker, and off to the right:

You see? Now THAT one looks like he missed it. No good! Wide left. Game over. The zebras actually got a call right. Shocking!

But wait, there's more!

Like I said, we live in the social media age. Do you think anyone was watching that final kick without recording it? Of course not. We can't do anything without our phones nowadays. They own us.

This angle, from the other end of the field, swings me again:

See? Now I think it's good again! What a rush.

There's also that pesky NCAA rulebook, which provides even more context to the whole situation.

For those of you who wanted the play reviewed ... you can't.

On reviewable plays:

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Field goal attempts if and only if the ball is ruled (a) below or above the crossbar or (b) inside or outside the uprights when it is lower than the top of the uprights. If the ball is higher than the top of the uprights as it crosses the end line, the play may not be reviewed.

This one was not reviewable, based on that rule. It went above the uprights.

It's also important to note that the NFL and NCAA differ just a bit in their language regarding made field attempts. The college rulebook states the ball must cross "over the crossbar between the uprights of the receiving team’s goal."

The NFL rulebook specifically mentions what we saw last night:

The entire ball must pass through the vertical plane of the goal, which is the area above the crossbar and between the uprights or, if above the uprights, between their outside edges.

The NCAA rulebook doesn't say anything about the ball going above the uprights. Just "between" the uprights. Not saying that's the rule, just saying the rulebook leaves it out. Context is important.

OK, that's enough yapping out of me. What do you guys think?

Let me have it! Zach.Dean@OutKick.com.

posts.title: Phil Collins gets frank on marriage failures and life regrets: 'I regret my marriages falling apart'
posts.excerpt: Phil Collins told Piers Morgan his Genesis touring schedule destroyed his first marriage and revealed deep regrets about all three marriages falling apart.
posts.content:
Phil Collins is opening up about his biggest regret throughout the course of his career.

During a recent interview on "Piers Morgan Uncensored," the 75-year-old musician reflected on the toll his career took on his relationships with his children and how it affected his three marriages.

"To some extent, I have to say I regret my marriages falling apart," he explained. "Sometimes I jumped. Well, one time I jumped, two times I was pushed. But I wouldn't have written it like that. But on the other hand, I've got five fantastic kids that I wouldn't have if that hadn't happened. So I have to balance it."

The famous drummer was married to his first wife, Andrea Bertorelli, from 1975 to 1980. Collins adopted Bertorelli's daughter, Joely, and the couple welcomed son Simon.

PHIL COLLINS' BRUSH WITH DEATH LEFT HIS CHILDREN PREPARING FOR THE UNTHINKABLE

He also shares daughter Lily with his second wife, Jill Tavelman, whom he was married to from 1984 to 1996, and sons Nicholas and Mathew with his third wife, Orianne Cevey, whom he was married to from 1999 to 2006.

When looking back on his first marriage, Collins admitted it broke down because he wasn't around, as he was touring with his band, Genesis, and couldn't be home.

"Genesis did, in one year, I think, three American tours, two European tours, and a tour of Japan. And when I ended up getting separated from my first wife, the guys in the band said, ‘Well, why didn’t you tell us? We’d have stopped it.’ But that’s easy to say in retrospect," he said. "I was gone, and we grew apart."

Despite his failure to make his relationships with his wives work, Collins said he "always tried to be there for the kids," and that he never planned on getting married three times, noting, "You don't go into life thinking that."

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

His daughter Lily, who stars in the hit Netflix series, "Emily in Paris," wrote about her relationship with her father in her 2017 memoir, "Unfiltered: No Shame, No Regrets, Just Me."

"I'm learning how to accept your actions and vocalize how they made me feel," she wrote in an excerpt read by Morgan. "I accept and honor the sadness and anger I felt toward the things you did or didn't do, did or didn't give me. I forgive you for not always being there when I needed it, for not being the dad I expected. I forgive the mistakes you made. And although it may seem like it's too late, it's not. There's still so much time to move forward."

The father-daughter duo has managed to put the past behind them, as she shared photos of them celebrating his 75th birthday together in January, writing "Love you to the moon and back again…"

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

In a birthday message to her father, she expressed feeling "grateful" to be able to celebrate the milestone birthday with him, saying she considers herself "lucky to have hugged you, laughed with you, and reminisced with you on such a monumental day."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

She also shared a Father's Day tribute to him on her Instagram stories for Father's Day, writing that she is "endlessly grateful for your unconditional love, guidance and support."

Now as a parent, I have a newly found understanding and deeper appreciation for everything you’ve done and continue to do," she wrote. "Tove is lucky to call you Grandpa P."

Lily welcomed her first child, Tove, with her husband, Charlie McDowell, via surrogate in January 2025.

posts.title: Minnesota quarterback gets kicked in the crotch by teammate en route to upset win over Michigan
posts.excerpt: Minnesota's Bennett Warren accidentally kicked QB Drake Lindsey in the groin during a celebration in the Gophers' upset win over Michigan football.
posts.content:
All sports have unwritten rules, and one of the biggest in football is never kick your own quarterback in the crotch.

It doesn’t matter whether it’s intentional or accidental during the throes of celebration: You just don’t do it.

The Minnesota Golden Gophers did not abide by this, but still managed to take a huge win over Michigan on Saturday afternoon.

CRAZIEST UPSET OF THE COLLEGE FOOTBALL SEASON HAPPENED ON FRIDAY NIGHT WHILE EVERYONE WAS ASLEEP

Last week, Minnesota beat Washington 27-24, a win that led to a euphoric PJ Fleck smearing a player's blood on his own face, and this week they welcomed the Wolverines to Huntington Bank Stadium.

However, during the game, things got a little rough for QB Drake Lindsey.

The Gophers had just secured a first down, and offensive lineman Bennett Warren was fired up about it.

Understandable, but the issue was that he didn't make sure the airspace was clear before performing a celebratory kick.

A kick that landed straight to Lindsey's groin.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Between this and the aforementioned blood-smearing incident, the Gophers may need to take a look in the mirror when it comes to celebrations.

These are getting out of hand.

I didn't think there was anywhere to go after the blood-smearing, but then here they go, kicking their QB in the nards, and now I have no clue where this goes.

At this rate, they could end up going all Texas on everyone and just let 'er rip.

Fortunately, they did stick the dismount on their last celebration of the afternoon, when they stormed the field to celebrate the Gophers' 20-14 win after coming into the game as 8.5-point underdogs.

Next weekend, the 4-1 Gophers will head to West Lafayette to take on the Purdue Boilermakers.

If they win? Well, buckle up.

And perhaps wear a cup.

posts.title: Cornell president says university 'must do better' on handling of sexual assault allegations
posts.excerpt: Cornell University President Michael Kotlikoff said the university "must do better" after questions arose over its handling of fraternity sexual assault claims.
posts.content:
Cornell University President Michael Kotlikoff said Saturday that the institution "must do better" as it faces questions over its response to sexual assault allegations involving seven former fraternity brothers.

"What happened to Jane Doe in 2024 is deeply disturbing and will weigh heavily on our community for years to come. My heart aches when I think of what she experienced," Kotlikoff said in a video statement to the Cornell community.

Kotlikoff said the case raises questions about sexual assault, campus party culture, alcohol and drug abuse on the Ithaca, New York, campus, as well as the investigation conducted after the allegations were reported.

"I want to acknowledge something that can be difficult for an institution to say we don't have all the answers, but we are committed to investigating and finding the answers our community deserves. I believe we as an administration, and we as a community must do better," Kotlikoff said.

INSIDE EXPLOSIVE CORNELL RAPE ALLEGATIONS: 7 MEN ACCUSED, CONFLICTING ACCOUNTS AND A POLITICAL FIRESTORM

Kotlikoff welcomed an independent review by an outside law firm into Cornell's handling of the case and said the university supports Gov. Kathy Hochul's decision to turn the criminal investigation over to New York Attorney General Letitia James.

He said Cornell would not wait for those reviews to conclude before making changes to prevention and education, student support, mental health and substance use resources and investigative processes.

"We will act," Kotlikoff said.

Jane Doe alleges in a lawsuit that seven former Chi Phi fraternity brothers drugged and sexually assaulted her during an October 2024 night at the fraternity house. Doe was a 20-year-old Cornell undergraduate at the time.

CORNELL RAPE ALLEGATIONS PROMPT NY ATTORNEY GENERAL LETITIA JAMES TO OPEN ‘ACTIVE CRIMINAL INVESTIGATION’

The men have denied wrongdoing, with some maintaining the sexual activity was consensual and others denying they participated. No criminal charges have been filed against the seven men.

Doe filed a 101-page lawsuit last month accusing the former fraternity members of sexual assault and rape and naming Cornell and other entities.

The case came under renewed scrutiny after Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten said his office had not received the full transcript of Doe's November 2024 interview with Cornell University Police before prosecutors initially declined to pursue charges.

Van Houten reopened the investigation before Hochul appointed the Office of the Attorney General as special prosecutor. James said Friday that her office was conducting an "active criminal investigation."

CORNELL SEXUAL ASSAULT CASE REVIVES SCRUTINY OF A LITTLE-KNOWN NEW YORK LAW ON INTOXICATED VICTIMS

Kotlikoff also addressed frustration over Cornell's communication about its response to the allegations and said the university would make a greater effort to be transparent.

"There are real legal and privacy limits on what we can say, but we will make a greater effort to explain what we can to provide context about the actions Cornell has taken and to be more transparent," Kotlikoff said.

Kotlikoff said Cornell would also reexamine the role of fraternities and sororities on campus and support efforts to change New York's sexual assault laws.

"You have my commitment that this will not be a moment that passes," Kotlikoff said.

Fox News Digital's Michael Dorgan contributed to this report.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/us/cornell-president-says-university-must-do-better-handling-sexual-assault-allegations

posts.title: Pete Hegseth handles Air Force-Navy coin toss after showing off basketball skills at Academy

posts.content:
United States Secretary of War Pete Hegseth was in Colorado Springs to take in the Air Force Falcons and Navy Midshipmen football game, but he also took time to show off some pretty impressive athletic skills.

TRUMP SAYS HE WILL ATTEND ALABAMA VS GEORGIA COLLEGE FOOTBALL GAME AT BRYANT-DENNY STADIUM

He must be an absolute menace in Pop-A-Shot down at Dave & Buster's.

Imagine if international disputes were settled with three-point shooting competitions or games of Horse?

Every other nation would think twice when dealing with us, knowing that Sec. Hegseth can uncork a Caitlin Clark-like shot from the logo if he has to.

While he missed one, Sec. Hegseth clearly found a groove and was on autopilot through most of that impressive performance.

Of course, Hegseth was not there to show off his skills when it comes to shooting from range; he was at the Air Force Academy to speak to cadets ahead of the Falcons-Midshipmen game on Saturday afternoon.

Just before kickoff, the Secretary of War was down on the field for the coin toss.

AIR FORCE ATHLETES CHASING OLYMPIC DREAMS IN BETWEEN SERVING THE NATION IN A CRITICAL TIME

Air Force wound up winning this one 14-9 to go 3-1 on the season.

They'll visit Northern Illinois next weekend while the Midshipmen — who dropped to 1-3 — will head home to host Tulsa.
