posts.title: More Gen Z college freshmen are quitting school early and moving back home with mom and dad
posts.excerpt: Just weeks into the fall semester, some Gen Z college freshmen have left campus and headed back home to take online classes — creating viral debates about the reasons.
posts.content:
Some Gen Z freshmen have already decided — just weeks into the fall semester — to abandon their college campuses, head back home and take classes online.

Others are quitting school entirely very early on.

In a recent "Outnumbered" segment, the Fox News co-hosts discussed the trend of young college students bailing out of campus life and returning home — saying the degree is what they’re after, not the "college experience."

Online reactions to the controversial and trending decision are running the gamut.

‘SHUT UP’ AND LISTEN: TRACE GALLAGHER SHARES WISDOM LEARNED FROM BEING A ‘GIRL DAD’

"To be fair, college is not for everyone," one Facebook user commented.

Another blurted, "Time for the school of HARD KNOCKS!"

A viral TikTok posted by a 17-year-old indicated that the student left campus at Southern University in Louisiana just two weeks into her first semester to go back home to Las Vegas, according to reports.

Some students today seem to be strangers with discomfort and struggle — as one user advised, "Y'all have to learn how to be uncomfortable."

Another was more understanding, posting, "It's OK to be uncomfortable, anxious and stressed during your first year of college."

"Outnumbered" co-host Kaleigh McEnany said she remembered her own college days, when she would struggle to return to school after spending time at home.

"I would cry in the airport, and my mom was like, 'You've gotta get on the plane, you've gotta go back …' And it was tough, but I'm so glad she pushed me," she said.

In her viral TikTok, the teenager shared a disclaimer in the caption of her video, noting that she didn’t drop out — she switched to the school’s online program instead.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Various factors affect the decisions of students to leave campus and take classes at home — with some online posters on various forums weighing in with their own experiences and beliefs.

Writing on Reddit recently, one parent said a son in the family's household "is quitting college quickly, and I feel like a loser."

The parent went on, "He was one of the top students in his high school class. Had anxiety, but worked through all issues eventually. I have anxiety issues as well, so I've always done my best to help him through it. Dished out so much money to get him a car, a laptop, paid for bus passes, etc., only to have him drop out after one week."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The person continued, "Won't even consider just sticking with it for a semester or two. He even had a scholarship to cover his entire first year! I mean, I took 19 years to finish my bachelor's degree, but I was always employed, so what can I really say?"

In response, another person on Reddit wrote, "What are his reasons? How much ability do you have to force him to stay? Is it a done deal already? I would absolutely try to get to the bottom of it and figure out how to work around whatever his concerns are."

Another parent weighed in with this experience: "My daughter has a lot of social anxiety and just got through her second week of college. She is particularly anxious about public speaking. So much so she would miss days of high school almost any time it was required. I have been very nervous about her ability to adapt."

Added the parent, "So far it is going well, but not without some struggle. One of her classes required discussion from everyone, each time."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Still another individual shared a very different perspective.

"I feel that college is a huge maturity checkpoint and most young adults aren't ready for it right out of high school," the person wrote.

"I am a big proponent of not pushing them toward it until they feel it's something they want to do. That doesn't mean there aren't expectations — but maybe there is an option to choose to work full time, and pay some bills instead."

Others chimed in on that same theme.

"There is NO reason he has to attend college right now. He can work and see whether he is able to earn enough to support himself that way. He may need a break from academics. There are many paths; don't stress!"

Students and online commenters have pointed out that financial concerns, mental health struggles or the desire to simply focus on academics can make on-campus life more difficult for some young people.

The "Outnumbered" segment also noted that many members of Gen Z completed high school largely from home — taking online classes in their living room or kitchen, with parents not far away, during the COVID pandemic.

A recent Psychology Today piece on the topic noted that kids who leave college early — for whatever reason — need clear guidance once they get back home.

"Set clear boundaries regarding work, household responsibilities, health and wellness, and daily routines," a mental health counselor advised parents.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/lifestyle/more-gen-z-college-freshmen-quitting-school-early-moving-back-mom-dad

posts.title: Dems hand GOP fresh midterm weapon by opposing widely used voter ID
posts.excerpt: Senate Democrats blocked a voter ID and insider trading ban bill as Republicans like Chuck Schumer's caucus face accusations of denying Trump a win.
posts.content:
Senate Democrats’ recent rejection of voter ID is giving Republicans fresh ammunition in the midterm fight, putting them on the opposite side of a practice that is common across the country and broadly popular with voters in both parties.

Republicans have developed a cynical view of why Democrats won’t play ball with voter ID, arguing that Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., and his caucus don’t want to give the GOP a win heading into the midterm elections.

"Democrats are gonna vote against it because they don't want to give the president a win," Sen. Jim Banks, R-Ind., told Fox News Digital. "They don’t want to give Republicans a win. They'll screw the country and stuff."

DOZENS OF HOUSE DEMOCRATS REJECT BILL FUSING CONGRESSIONAL STOCK BAN WITH FEDERAL VOTER ID

Republicans' latest attempt to pass a federal voter ID law, which was paired with another popular issue to ban insider trading in Congress, comes months after initially launching their push to pass the SAVE America Act, a high priority for President Donald Trump that Schumer and Democrats have time and again rejected.

Earlier this year, Democrats argued that voter ID isn’t so bad, it’s just how Republicans were approaching it that they disagreed with — Schumer dubbed the SAVE America Act "Jim Crow 2.0" and contended it would disenfranchise Black and Brown voters.

"Democrats support voter ID," Schumer said on a press call earlier this year. "In fact, we included it, and it is included, in our Freedom to Vote legislation several years ago."

INSIDE THE SENATE'S CHAOTIC ALL-NIGHTER THAT LEFT TRUMP'S SAVE AMERICA ACT ON THE SHELF

But as the months have dragged on, an issue that voters overwhelmingly support has become a place for Democrats to dig their heels into the dirt against.

Requiring identification to vote is already a practice in 36 states. Of those, 23 require photo ID, while 13 accept another form of identification, such as a bank statement. Nine of those states have Democratic senators.

"We already have it," Sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., told Fox News Digital. "I mean, Virginia has a voter ID law that our citizens really like."

"Virtually every state has a voter ID law," he continued. "So, what, there has to be a one size fits all federal thing for states [that[ are already doing this?"

SCHUMER, DEMOCRATS SAY THEY SUPPORT VOTER ID, THEN BLOCK GOP AMENDMENT TO REQUIRE IT

Republicans say that the Democratic resistance has a more nefarious intent. Requiring voter ID would allegedly nuke some of their voter base, illegal immigrants, and therefore lower their chances of winning in federal elections.

"Well, it's evident Democrats want to make it easier to cheat," Senate Majority Whip John Barrasso, R-Wyo., told Fox News Digital. " Republicans want to make it easier to vote, make sure nobody's cheating. And that's where we are on this voter ID, an 80/20 issue or not even more."

Barrasso argued that identification is required in several mundane instances of life, from boarding a plane to buying a beer — and even to get into some rallies held by Democratic candidates during this election cycle.

"They’re complete hypocrites on this," Barrasso said. "But [what] we need to do is elect more Republicans to be able to win these elections and make sure we have people here that see what the American people see, which is, you have to have a photo ID to vote."

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/politics/dems-hand-gop-fresh-midterm-weapon-opposing-widely-used-voter-id

posts.title: Robert Blake’s son returns to restaurant tied to family tragedy for new murder mystery
posts.excerpt: Noah Blake opens "A Killer Night in Studio City" at Vitello's, confronting decades of pain tied to his father Robert Blake's infamous trial.
posts.content:
Twenty-five years after Vitello's became part of a painful chapter in his family's history, Noah Blake has returned to the restaurant to direct and star in a fictional murder mystery, describing the production as part of his healing journey.

The "Teen Witch" alum's "A Killer Night in Studio City," a noir-inspired immersive theater production set in 1958, opened at the famed Italian restaurant on Sept. 15.

"When I was first approached about this, of course, there was this little bit of ... and then I was like, 'Wait, what am I doing? Of course, I should do this,'" Blake told Fox News Digital. "This is a chance for me to, not rewrite history, but to create a new page and to create a new connection and a new relationship for me with this place, for my name with this place, for my family with this place."

ROBERT BLAKE DEAD AT 89

"I've got a four-year-old son," Blake said. "I want him to be able to go there and enjoy Vitello's as he's grown up, God willing, as long as Vitello's is there. And I don't want him to ever feel funny. I want him to think about, 'Oh, Vitello's, that's the place where daddy did that fun show.' Not this other stuff. I'm not trying to minimize that tragedy, but it wasn't my tragedy, and it was a cross that I've had to bear and still will probably for the rest of my life."

Blake said Vitello's was a regular gathering place for his family while he was growing up, but he stayed away for decades. He eventually returned and agreed to stage the production there, saying he wanted to reclaim positive memories of a place he had loved.

"I want to go and do something in this space that is creative, that is fun, that is exciting, where people come and laugh and gasp and have a great time," he explained. "Some people may not even know [what happened] and the people who do might be curious and go, 'Oh, that has nothing to do with anything, and I had a great time.'"

WATCH: NOAH BLAKE SAYS RETURN TO SITE TIED TO FAMILY TRAGEDY IS ‘FULL CIRCLE’

The history Blake is trying to move beyond dates back to 2001, when his father Robert Blake's wife, Bonny Lee Bakley, was killed after the couple had dinner at Vitello's.

The actor was acquitted of murder in 2005 in connection with Bakley's killing. Bakley was shot and killed while sitting in Robert's car near the restaurant. A civil jury later found him liable for her death and ordered him to pay Bakley's family $30 million, prompting him to file for bankruptcy, according to The Associated Press.

An appeals court later reduced the award to $15 million, after which the parties reached a confidential settlement. Robert died in 2023 at 89.

Rose Lenore, Bakley's daughter with Robert, feels differently about the production. She told Fox News Digital that Vitello's remains too painful for her and others who loved her mother.

"I think him doing it at Vitello's is upsetting for me and anyone who loved Bonny," she said. "And there were quite a few people who did. She left behind three children, plus me. She also left behind a sister, my aunt, who misses her dearly. And so, to have Robert Blake's son do any show at Vitello's, let alone a murder mystery show, I find that to be insensitive and upsetting."

"I don't even care what the show is about," Lenore said. "I'm also not here to invalidate anyone's healing journey, if that's what this is for him. But I also think it's my moral obligation to stand up for what I believe in. I would still be upset if he was doing anything else. And for Noah to be doing a happy, fun show — I think it's in poor taste."

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

"I'm not wishing any harm on Noah," Lenore continued. "I wish him well in his life and career. But it would be hard for me to stay silent on something like this. It would be hard for me to stay silent about my mother."

Responding to Lenore's criticism, Blake wrote in a statement to Fox News Digital, "I have my own deeply personal reasons for doing this play. Vitello's was a place that I loved my entire life. Over time, that place became the physical embodiment for me of a much larger and devastating chapter of my life — one thing that I had nothing to do with, but whose consequences I have had to endure for years."

"Choosing to walk back into that space now and create something uniquely mine — something lighthearted and entertaining that people are enjoying — is part of my own healing journey," he wrote. "It's about taking a place that had come to represent something painfully dark in my life and allowing it to represent something else. I'm not erasing history or rewriting it. I'm simply adding a new page to it, and I don't ask or expect anyone else to sign off on what I need to do to heal."

"Rose is absolutely entitled to her feelings," Blake continued. "I've been there for her many times over the years, and I care for her. She chose to express her feelings about this publicly, which certainly wouldn't have been my choice and still isn't. I would much rather have had a private conversation with her. I've reached out and asked her to call me so that we could talk about this, and that conversation has yet to happen. But that door remains open for her."

Blake said returning to Vitello's has also forced him to revisit his complicated relationship with his late father.

"I don't think people really realize when something like that happens, how many lives are impacted in such a profound way," he explained. "I had to wrestle with who my father really was for everything I thought he was or knew or saw him as. Did he do this thing? Was he really capable of this? Was he that far gone? Was my father this monster?"

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"It's tough because it makes you question a lot. 'What is my genetic makeup?' It was years of intense scrutiny, and it was impossible to live my life, and for other people as well. It's not cool to know that this guy's son had a nervous breakdown and couldn't leave his house for six months and was having panic attacks and night sweats and was incapable of functioning."

"There were moments my father could be a very loving, kind, decent, generous human being," he said. "And there were times when he could just be an absolute f---ing monster and just the worst kind of selfish and menacing and threatening."

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

Before his death, Robert fiercely denied murdering Bakley.

For Blake, returning to the restaurant carries a meaning beyond the fictional story he says he wants to tell. While he recognizes the connection others may make to his family's past, Blake stressed he does not want that history to define him.

"... I live my life as me," he said.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/entertainment/robert-blake-son-returns-restaurant-tied-family-tragedy-new-murder-mystery

posts.title: DR MARC SIEGEL: The angels behind Alcoholics Anonymous still inspire hope
posts.excerpt: Middle-aged adults are drinking more and dying at alarming rates from alcohol use disorder, but a faith-based cure from the 1930s still works.
posts.content:
Alcohol is still something to be worried about. Granted, national data shows a decline coming out of the pandemic, but the overall numbers are still higher than they were in 2018. Not only that, but though Gen Zers and millennials are drinking less, middle-aged adults are drinking more, with an increase in heavy drinking since 2018.

Some of this is because middle-aged adults face increased pressures as they try to manage both aging parents and children who are in adolescence or early adulthood and are just finding themselves. But though drinking may temporarily ease stress, the long-term health risks are significant. A recent study from Colorado determined that older adults are more likely to drink alone, which carries with it additional health risks, including cognitive decline.

There are an estimated 28 million Americans who suffer from alcohol use disorder, with a substantial portion of them being middle-aged. Not only that, but about 50% of the deaths due to alcohol in the U.S. occur among middle-aged adults.

HEAVY DRINKING SURGES AMONG AMERICANS IN ONE AGE GROUP AS OTHER GENERATIONS CUT BACK

Faith-based cures remain highly effective for alcoholism, with none more effective than Alcoholics Anonymous, which was developed in the 1930s by Bill Wilson and Dr. Bob Smith after a chance meeting, the kind that the famed psychiatrist Carl Jung called synchronicity, or meaningful coincidence.

They became messengers of God for each other and ultimately, for millions of other alcoholics with their 12-step program based largely on making a spiritual connection.

In my new book, "The Angels Among Us," I devote a chapter to the miracle recovery of Bill Wilson and his consequential friendship with Dr. Bob. Bill is admitted to Towns Hospital in New York City in 1934 for the fourth time because of alcohol intoxication followed by withdrawal. He is in the depths of despair and is not sure if he will survive. And then he experiences the central miracle of his life as he demands that God show Himself.

CAN FAITH HELP PATIENTS HEAL? VETERAN DOCTOR REVEALS WHAT HE'S WITNESSED FIRSTHAND

"The room lights up with a blinding glare of light. Wilson is seized by an ecstasy he has never known. He stands on a mountaintop with a great wind blowing. He thinks to himself, 'This is not a wind of air. This is spirit. This is the God of the preachers.'

"Bill feels that a great, clean strength is blowing through him, that he is now free."

Bill Wilson tells about his experience to his medical angel, Dr. Silkworth, who is tending to him there in the hospital, who decides he is not crazy, but that a great psychic event has occurred. This changes Bill's life, as the doctor/"angel" advises him to hang on to this experience and to share it.

By meeting other alcoholics where they live, and not speaking down to them, by not preaching, Wilson and later Dr. Bob spread faith, goodwill, and ultimately sobriety.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

In today's world, this lesson remains crucial. It is the in-person exchange of peer-to-peer kindness and caring that gives us all the chance to heal. It doesn't work the same way on social media, and self-destructive behavior (including alcohol addiction) is much more likely to occur in isolation.

There is still a lesson to be learned from Bill Wilson's experience. Doctors can be angels of healing, just as fellow sufferers can.

CLICK HERE TO READ MORE FROM DR. MARC SIEGEL

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/opinion/dr-marc-siegel-angels-behind-alcoholics-anonymous-inspire-hope

posts.title: 10-minute fitness habit can help adults over 40 maintain muscle and stay strong
posts.excerpt: CEO Carl Daikeler compares metabolism to a furnace: Muscle is the coal and cardio stokes it, urging a balance of strength training and cardiovascular work.
posts.content:
Adults over 40 may not need to spend hours in the gym to maintain muscle, preserve mobility and stay strong.

According to Los Angeles fitness entrepreneur Carl Daikeler, just 10 minutes of targeted resistance exercise each day can help preserve muscle, mobility and long-term function.

Daikeler, 63, who has spent 28 years leading BODi, the fitness brand formerly known as Beachbody, says his approach to exercise stems from a practical desire to stay healthy without having to be a dedicated fitness enthusiast.

4 SIMPLE HABITS CAN HELP SLOW MUSCLE LOSS AS YOU AGE, FITNESS EXPERT SAYS

"I don't like to eat healthy, I don't like to work out," Daikeler told Fox News Digital at the Strong New York conference in September. "I'm just constantly trying to figure out how I can hack my way without having to overturn my life to become one of these diehard health and fitness people, because I'm never going to become that."

For adults looking to stay healthy in midlife, Daikeler recommends what he considers a "minimum effective dose" — short, targeted resistance workouts at home instead of lengthy gym sessions.

"Ten minutes a day, and you can establish and build and maintain muscle," he said.

WANT TO AGE BETTER? RESEARCHERS SAY 4-MINUTE ROUTINE MAY HELP PREVENT DANGEROUS FALLS

Federal physical activity guidelines say that adults should perform muscle-strengthening activities involving all major muscle groups at least two days per week, in addition to regular aerobic activity.

Rather than doing a full-body workout every day, Daikeler recommends rotating muscle groups — focusing on the chest one day, upper body the next, then legs and glutes — to build consistency without requiring lengthy gym sessions.

"Do that consistently, and you're going to find your strength return, your muscles return, your joints will start to respond appropriately," he said.

The 10-minute approach can be especially valuable for people taking GLP-1 medications, who may be trying to preserve muscle mass and bone density while losing weight but may feel intimidated by traditional gyms, Daikeler said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

For individuals seeking more significant weight loss, he recommends extending daily activity to 20 or 30 minutes, incorporating a balance of strength training and cardiovascular exercise.

Daikeler cautioned against focusing exclusively on either cardio or resistance training, noting that different exercise types serve distinct functions in the body.

"Your body's like a furnace," Daikeler said. "The coal in that furnace is muscle. So you want to build muscle. But then you want to stoke that coal, and that's cardio. So, you need a balance of both things."

While resistance training builds muscle and strengthens bones and connective tissue, cardiovascular exercise challenges the heart and lungs, helping to maintain overall fitness, he said.

As adults age, Daikeler says the primary motivation for maintaining physical activity should shift away from aesthetic goals and toward functional mobility and independence.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Reflecting on his personal experience visiting his father in an assisted living facility, Daikeler observed how residents struggled with basic movement and balance.

Many residents relied on walkers and canes, and often stopped walking before talking to one another because they feared tripping over cracks in the pavement, he recalled.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"This is no longer about my abs," Daikeler added. "I need to work out in order to be able to walk and talk at the same time into my 90s ... It's no longer about aesthetics and vanity. It's really about mobility."

Maintaining healthy physical habits means accepting daily short-term discomfort to protect long-term independence, Daikeler noted.

"If I do 20 minutes of discomfort, the rest of the day is awesome," he said, adding that the goal is to consistently incorporate resistance training, cardio and flexibility work into a daily routine.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/health/10-minute-fitness-habit-help-adults-over-40-maintain-muscle-stay-strong

posts.content:
The former Zonal Women Leader of the All Progressives Congress, APC, in Bauchi South, Mrs Jamima J. Dutse, has been killed by unknown assailants at her residence in Bauchi State.

Dutse was reportedly attacked at her home before the assailants fled the area.

Reacting to the incident, the Take-It-Back, TIB, Movement, Bauchi State chapter, condemned the killing, describing it as a “senseless” act of violence and an attack on the peace and security of the state.

In a statement issued on Sunday and signed by the movement’s Bauchi State Coordinator, Nazif Bashi, TIB expressed condolences to Dutse’s family, friends and associates, while calling on security agencies to urgently investigate the circumstances surrounding her death.

The group urged the Bauchi State Police Command, the Department of State Services, DSS, and other relevant security agencies to identify and arrest those responsible for the killing.

It also demanded transparent communication from the security agencies, including regular updates to the victim’s family and the public on the progress of the investigation.

“Justice must not only be done; it must be seen to be done,” the group said, insisting that those responsible for the murder must be prosecuted and made to face the full wrath of the law.

TIB further called on the Bauchi State Government and security authorities to strengthen security measures, surveillance and intelligence gathering across Bauchi metropolis and neighbouring local government areas.

posts.excerpt: Former Real Madrid manager and present France national team head coach Zinedine Zidane has sent a message to Portugal over the Cristiano Ronaldo’s situation. He said that the players’ accomplishments
posts.content:
Former Real Madrid manager and present France national team head coach Zinedine Zidane has sent a message to Portugal over the Cristiano Ronaldo’s situation.

He said that the players’ accomplishments in football warrants appropriate recognition and celebration.

Ronaldo found himself at the centre of controversy following his departure from the Portugal national team’s training facility over an alleged disagreement with head coach Jorge Jesus.

The Portuguese veteran chose to exit the camp following remarks made by Jesus during a press conference preceding their UEFA Nations League victory against Denmark.

Zidane represents one of numerous coaches who achieved considerable success with Cristiano Ronaldo as a key member of their squad.

The French tactician secured one LaLiga championship and three consecutive UEFA Champions League titles during his tenure with the accomplished forward in his line-up.

During a press conference preceding France’s Nations League encounter with Belgium, Zidane commended the 41-year-old striker for the significant influence he has exerted on his managerial career and emphasised that Ronaldo’s professional legacy merits appropriate acknowledgment. His statement (via Madrid Zone on X) read as follows:

“Cristiano Ronaldo made me win incredible trophies. Hats off to you, Cris. We must salute his great career the right way. I was lucky to have him with me. I have a lot of respect for all my players and especially for Cristiano.”

Ronaldo’s withdrawal from the national squad results in his absence from their concluding Nations League match against Norway scheduled for later today.

UNL: Zidane sends message to Portugal over Cristiano Ronaldo

posts.title: Choose dialogue over violence – Peter Obi tells Umuoba-Anam, Aguleri communities
posts.excerpt: The presidential candidate of the Nigerian Democratic Congress, NDC, Peter Obi, has appealed to residents of Umuoba-Anam and Aguleri communities in Anambra East Local Government Area of Anambra State
posts.content:
The presidential candidate of the Nigerian Democratic Congress, NDC, Peter Obi, has appealed to residents of Umuoba-Anam and Aguleri communities in Anambra East Local Government Area of Anambra State to end hostilities and embrace peace.

​

Obi made the appeal in a statement posted on his official X handle, expressing sadness over reports of clashes between the two communities.

He warned that continued hostilities would only lead to destruction, noting that many Nigerians were already struggling with economic hardship.

His statement reads, “I am deeply pained by the reports of hostilities between the good people of Umuoba-Anam and Aguleri in Anambra East LGA of Anambra State.

“Hostilities of the kind we are witnessing between the two communities achieve nothing but destruction. At a time when people are already finding it increasingly difficult to survive, adding the devastation of conflict is like adding fuel to the fire.

“I appeal to both communities to immediately cease hostilities and embrace peace. No grievance, however serious, is worth the loss of lives, the destruction of homes and livelihoods, or the pain inflicted on families.

“Let us choose dialogue over violence, reconciliation over revenge, and peace over destruction. There is always a better way to resolve our differences.

“May God grant wisdom to our leaders and peace to Umuoba-Anam and Aguleri.”

Choose dialogue over violence – Peter Obi tells Umuoba-Anam, Aguleri communities

posts.title: US Marine arrested in Japan on suspicion of murder
posts.excerpt: A US Marine stationed on Japan's southern island of Okinawa was arrested on suspicion of the murder of a Japanese woman, police said on Sunday. The post US Marine arrested in Japan on suspicion of mur
posts.content:
A US Marine stationed on Japan’s southern island of Okinawa was arrested on suspicion of the murder of a Japanese woman, police said on Sunday.

The suspect “killed the 39-year-old woman at a hotel in Naha and stole her wallet on Saturday”, a local police spokesman told AFP.

Crimes including rapes, assaults, hit-and-run and drunk-driving accidents by US personnel have long sparked protests on Okinawa, which bears a disproportionate burden of hosting about 70 percent of US military facilities in Japan.

US Ambassador George Glass posted on social media that he had spoken with Japan’s foreign ministry and Okinawa’s governor, offering “our sincere condolences and pledging full cooperation as the investigation continues”.

Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said Japan had lodged a protest with US authorities and called the crime “exceptionally brutal and vicious”.

The government has urged the US “to provide maximum cooperation with the investigation, enforce stricter discipline among US military personnel, and take thorough measures to prevent the recurrence of similar crimes,” Takaichi said.

Public broadcaster NHK and other Japanese media outlets, citing investigation sources, reported that CCTV footage from near the scene showed a foreign man entering a room with a woman and later leaving with her belongings.

Police then found a 20-year-old man who matched the description of the suspect seen in the footage, and asked him to accompany them voluntarily to a local police station where he was arrested, NHK reported.

He reportedly denied the charges.

“We have lost a family member and are deeply saddened. My parents, in particular, are utterly devastated at the loss of their daughter,” the woman’s brother said through local police, according to the Asahi Shimbun daily newspaper.

The United States has around 54,000 military personnel stationed in Japan, mostly on Okinawa.

Crimes committed by US personnel have been a thorn in relations between the close security allies.

“Incidents and accidents involving US military personnel cause great anxiety among the local community and must not be allowed to happen,” Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi said.

Last year, a Japanese court sentenced a US Marine accused of choking and attempting to rape a woman in her 20s to seven years in prison.

In 2017, a former US Marine and civilian military base worker was sentenced to life in prison for the rape and murder of a local woman in Okinawa.

The same year, US Forces Japan banned all personnel from consuming alcohol after an intoxicated US Marine crashed his vehicle into a mini-truck, killing its 61-year-old local driver.

According to the Yomiuri Shimbun newspaper, around 6,000 US military personnel have been arrested since Okinawa was returned to Japan from the US in 1972, after World War II.

In 2024, the number of arrests hit 80, the highest in 20 years.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/us-marine-arrested-in-japan-on-suspicion-of-murder/

posts.title: ‘This govt doesn’t engage’ —  Ajaero accuses Tinubu’s admin of disconnect from NLC
posts.excerpt: He said the congress had made several attempts to open discussions with the Federal Government but received no response to its correspondence to Tinubu between May and December 2025. The post ‘This go
posts.content:
The President of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), Joe Ajaero, has accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of failing to engage with organised labour, describing the government as aloof and disconnected from the congress.

Ajaero made the allegation on Saturday during the latest episode of the Mic On Podcast, while recounting the events that led to the NLC’s planned nationwide protest in December 2025.

He said the congress had made several attempts to open discussions with the Federal Government but received no response to its correspondence to Tinubu between May and December 2025.

“For the past two to three years, it’s not government that is engaging. This government doesn’t engage,” Ajaero said.

The NLC president said the government only responded when labour unions took steps to express their grievances publicly, adding that the administration had become detached from the congress.

“It’s only when people engage; they now say A, B, C, D. So they are aloof,” he said.

Ajaero said the congress eventually fixed December 17, 2025, for a street protest after its efforts to reach the president failed.

He, however, disclosed that some state governors intervened following the planned demonstration, leading to a meeting between the labour leaders and the governors.

According to him, the intervention resulted in an interface with the government, but engagements since then have been limited.

“And after that, some governors intervened, and we had an interface. So some governors met with us, and since that time, we have talked once or twice,” he said.

Ajaero alleged that the government had since continued with its activities without addressing the issues raised by organised labour.

“And those issues, from December last year to now, they are just doing their business. Everybody is their enemy,” he added.

His comments come amid renewed labour tensions following a three-day warning strike by public servants under the Joint National Public Service Negotiating Council (JNPSNC).

The council had threatened industrial action if the Federal Government failed to reduce petrol prices to N500 per litre and approve a new wage award for workers.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/this-govt-doesnt-engage-ajaero-accuses-tinubus-admin-of-disconnect-from-nlc/

posts.title: 2027: ADC urges Zamfara govt to review campaign permit fees
posts.excerpt: According to him, the ADC leadership is seriously concerned about the scale and nature of the stated permit fees, particularly where such charges could create an unnecessary financial barrier to lawfu
posts.content:
The Zamfara chapter of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) has called on the state government to review what it described as exorbitant political campaign permit fees.

The state ADC Chairman, Kabiru Garba, stated this in a statement issued in Gusau on Saturday.

Garba called for an immediate review of the process to ensure transparency.

“The state ADC leadership has noted the letter dated Sept. 25, issued by the Zamfara Urban and Regional Planning Board (ZUREPB), containing the approved rules and permit fees for political campaign activities in Zamfara for the 2027 general elections.”

“The ADC recognises the legitimate responsibility of government to regulate the use of public spaces, protect public infrastructure, maintain environmental sanitation, manage traffic and ensure that political activities are conducted peacefully and orderly,” he said.

According to him, the ADC leadership is seriously concerned about the scale and nature of the stated permit fees, particularly where such charges could create an unnecessary financial barrier to lawful political participation and democratic engagement.

“We consider these provisions deserving of urgent review, clarification and consultation with political parties and other stakeholders.

“The ADC therefore respectfully appeals to the Zamfara Government to consider our call for immediate review of the campaign permit fees in order to ensure justice and fairness,” the chairman added.

He noted that the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) had issued the official framework for the 2027 electoral process, including provisions governing political party activities and campaigns.

“The INEC’s current regulations also contain specific provisions on the procedure, audience, period, venue and conduct of political campaigns.

“Political parties are essential institutions of democracy; they provide platforms through which citizens organise, present candidates, communicate policies and seek the mandate of the people.

“We recognise the need to regulate posters and billboards, rallies and processions, road shows, use of public spaces, traffic management, environmental protection and protection of public infrastructure,” he explained.

He, however, observed that such regulation should be lawful, proportionate, transparent, affordable and applied equally to all political parties and candidates.

“We therefore call on the authorities concerned to review the fees with a view to establishing reasonable, proportionate and affordable charges where legitimate regulation is required,” he pleaded.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/2027-adc-urges-zamfara-govt-to-review-campaign-permit-fees/

posts.title: 2027: Yayi targets 2m Ogun votes for Tinubu as CityBoy opens secretariat
posts.excerpt: Yayi praised Tinubu for projects and federal support to Ogun State, saying the president’s administration had delivered significant benefits to the state. The post 2027: Yayi targets 2m Ogun votes for
posts.content:
The Ogun State governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress, Senator Adeola Olamilekan, has said the state should deliver at least two million votes for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general election.

Olamilekan, popularly known as Yayi, spoke on Saturday at the inauguration of the Ogun State executives of the CityBoy Movement and the commissioning of the group’s state secretariat in Abeokuta.

The movement, a grassroots support group for Tinubu, is mobilising support for the president’s re-election bid ahead of the 2027 poll.

“Ogun State has over three million registered voters, and with this number, I believe we should give President Tinubu at least two million votes in 2027,” Olamilekan said.

He praised Tinubu for projects and federal support to Ogun State, saying the president’s administration had delivered significant benefits to the state.

Among the projects he highlighted were the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, the Sokoto-Badagry Expressway, the establishment of the Federal University of Medicine and Medical Sciences in Abeokuta and the upgrade of Tai Solarin University of Education to a federal institution.

The event was attended by Minister of State for Health, Ishaq Salako; Special Adviser to the President on Public Communication and Orientation, Sunday Dare; and the President’s Personal Assistant on Special Duties, Alhaji Kamorudeen Yusuf.

Governor Dapo Abiodun was represented by his deputy, Noimot Salako-Oyedele.

In his address, the Ogun State Director-General of the CityBoy Movement, Dr Abdulateef Sulaimon, said the group was committed to engaging young people and encouraging participation in the democratic process.

He disclosed that the movement had registered more than 150,000 active members in the state within a month of commencing its membership drive, adding that it aimed to build a verifiable grassroots network of over 500,000 members before January 2027.

The movement’s National Director-General, Francis Oluwatosin Shoga, charged the newly inaugurated executives to extend the group’s activities to all 20 local government areas of Ogun State and build a disciplined grassroots structure ahead of the election.

Shoga urged the executives to regard their appointments as a call to service and commended Yusuf for his leadership and commitment to the movement in the state.

posts.title: 10 footballers who served in military before football fame
posts.excerpt: Football has produced some of the world's biggest sporting stars, but several prominent players also have military backgrounds. The post 10 footballers who served in military before football fame appe
posts.content:
Football has produced some of the world’s biggest sporting stars, but several prominent footballers also have military backgrounds.

From mandatory national service to active military duty, these footballers served in the armed forces before or during their professional careers.

Here are 10 notable footballers who were former military personnel.

1. Son Heung-min

South Korea captain Son Heung-min completed his mandatory military service with the Republic of Korea Marine Corps in 2020.

His service was shortened to about three weeks after he helped South Korea win the gold medal at the 2018 Asian Games, which earned the squad an exemption from the country’s standard lengthy military service requirement.

2. Eric Cantona

Former Manchester United and France forward Eric Cantona completed two years of compulsory military service in the French Army.

Cantona later established himself as one of the most influential players in Manchester United’s history.

3. Sir Bobby Charlton

England and Manchester United legend Sir Bobby Charlton served in the Royal Army Ordnance Corps during his national service.

He also represented the British Army football team before going on to win the 1966 World Cup with England.

4. Duncan Edwards

Manchester United great Duncan Edwards also served in the Royal Army Ordnance Corps.

The midfielder completed his military service while beginning his professional football career and went on to become one of the most highly regarded players of his generation.

5. Paolo Maldini

Italy and AC Milan legend Paolo Maldini completed compulsory military service in the Italian Army.

Maldini subsequently enjoyed a career spanning more than two decades with AC Milan and the Italy national team.

6. Fabio Cannavaro

Former Italy captain Fabio Cannavaro served in the Italian military between 1995 and 1996.

The defender later captained Italy to victory at the 2006 FIFA World Cup and won the Ballon d’Or that same year.

7. Gary Holt

Former Scotland international Gary Holt served in the Army Catering Corps and played for the British Army football team.

He later built a professional career that included spells with Norwich City and Kilmarnock.

8. Teemu Tainio

Former Tottenham Hotspur midfielder Teemu Tainio completed military service in the Finnish Defence Forces.

The Finland international later played in France and England, including for Tottenham and Sunderland.

9. Bruce Grobbelaar

Former Liverpool goalkeeper Bruce Grobbelaar was conscripted into the Rhodesian Army in 1975.

He served during the Rhodesian Bush War before establishing himself as Liverpool’s first-choice goalkeeper and helping the club win several major trophies.

10. Gordon Astall

Former England international Gordon Astall served in the Royal Marines during World War II.

After his military service, he continued his football career and represented England at international level.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/10-footballers-who-served-in-military-before-football-fame/

posts.title: Death Toll From Plateau Road Crash Rises To 21
posts.excerpt: Road accidents continue to claim lives and leave many others injured on Nigeria’s roads, with multiple-vehicle collisions recorded on major highways and inter-state routes. The post Death Toll From Pl
posts.content:
The death toll from the multiple road crashes along the Hawan Kibo Road in Riyom Local Government Area of Plateau State has risen to 21.

The Sector Commander of the Federal Road Safety Corps in the state, Corps Commander Adelaja Ogungbemi, who visited the scene alongside the Zonal Commanding Officer, Assistant Corps Marshal, Joseph Udoabba, disclosed the latest figure after assessing the crash site on Saturday.

The officials inspected the scene and the extent of damage caused by the accident, which occurred on Friday evening when a truck reportedly suffered brake failure and rammed into other vehicles travelling towards Jos.

The crash involved a truck, a Hummer bus and a motorcycle.

The Hummer bus caught fire following the impact, while several victims were trapped in the vehicle.

Speaking after the assessment, the FRSC officials urged motorists to exercise greater caution while driving and ensure that their vehicles are properly maintained.

They urged vehicle owners to carry out regular checks of critical vehicle components, particularly braking systems, as these are essential to preventing avoidable road crashes and loss of life.

The FRSC has also continued efforts to manage traffic around the scene and facilitate the removal of the affected vehicles and recovery of the victims.

Road accidents continue to claim lives and leave many others injured on Nigeria’s roads, with multiple-vehicle collisions recorded on major highways and inter-state routes.

Last month, six people were confirmed killed in a fatal motor accident that occurred along Girei Road in Adamawa State.

Months earlier, a multiple-vehicle accident on the Ibadan end of the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway claimed at least five lives, while eight people sustained varying degrees of injuries.

In April, the Ogun State Sector Command of the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) confirmed three deaths in another multiple-vehicle crash at the Onipepeye axis of the Abeokuta–Sagamu Road in Obafemi Owode Local Government Area of the state. Seven other people were injured in the accident.

Source: https://www.channelstv.com/2026/10/03/death-toll-from-plateau-road-crash-rises-to-21/

posts.title: ‘We Were Very Authentic,’ Stella Damasus Recalls Nollywood Memories
posts.excerpt: The veteran actress, whose career has spanned decades across stage and screen, said she and her contemporaries stood out because they remained true to themselves. The post ‘We Were Very Authentic,’ St
posts.content:
Nollywood veteran, author, coach, and singer Stella Damasus has identified authenticity as a defining quality that set her generation of leading female actors apart during the early era of Nollywood.

The veteran actress, whose career has spanned decades across stage and screen, said she and her contemporaries stood out because they remained true to themselves rather than trying to imitate others.

“We were very authentic,” Damasus said on the Pulse Old vs New show. “We were not trying to be like other people. We’re not trying to copy other people or be who we’re not. Everything was authentic.”

Damasus, who authored the book Mama It’s a Girl, further added that she, like other big actresses, Genevieve Nnaji and Omotola Jalade Ekehinde, in the early days of Nollywood, had no idea how far and how big they would later become from doing what they passionately enjoyed doing.

“I’m going to assure you, we were not doing it because of the fame or the money. There was no social media to tell us how big we could get. We did not know,” the veteran said.

“After you see yourself on a poster, that’s about it. People will recognise you here and there and all of that at that time. It wasn’t about the fame. It wasn’t about the money. How much were they paying us?”

“We just loved the job. It was more about passion.”

This screengrab shows Stella Damasus as a guest on Pulse Old vs New (Photo: YouTube/Pulse Nigeria)

The prominent screen actor recalled how tough and daring it was for any female to be seen as an actor.

“At that time, it wasn’t easy for females at that age to be allowed by parents and families to enter the industry,” she said. “So those of us who could were bold.”

Damasus admitted that the movie ‘The Widow’ from 2005, where she played the role of a grieving wife subjected to intense emotional and physical degradation by her husband’s relatives following his sudden death, was one of her most challenging roles, one of the biggest because it changed her career overnight, both at home and abroad.

“But I’m grateful for the role because I saw what could happen, and then it did happen,” she added.

Source: https://www.channelstv.com/2026/10/03/we-were-very-authentic-stella-damasus-recalls-nollywood-memories/

posts.title: Chidera Okonji on Why Women Need to Be Intentional About Rest
posts.excerpt: Is there an art to rest? Can someone be inactive and still not truly rest? These are questions Chidera Okonji, better known as Odera Collins, hopes to explore at her
posts.content:
Is there an art to rest? Can someone be inactive and still not truly rest? These are questions Chidera Okonji, better known as Odera Collins, hopes to explore at her upcoming Bloom & Brunch event, themed ‘The Art of Rest.’

A media professional, event host and creative producer with experience spanning radio, television and large-scale productions, Okonji understands how demanding work environments can affect one’s wellbeing. Having experienced firsthand the physical and mental toll of constantly being in motion, she has also observed how often women put themselves last. These experiences inspired her to create Bloom & Brunch as a space where women can pause, connect, reflect, have a good time and simply be.

In this interview with Vanessa Obioha, she explains the idea behind ‘The Art of Rest.’

Ordinarily, one sees rest as just taking a break from work, but the theme of your event suggests otherwise. Does rest really require an art?

Yes, there is. Sadly, due to the current state of the economy, coupled with living in a capitalist world, we have been tasked with a life where we have to keep working/running different streams of income in a bid to measure up to the demands of our society. So what you see is people, in this case women, burying themselves in their business/work. Now, behind this are high-stress conditions, bad eating habits, toxic relationships, etc., which greatly affect the overall balance of women’s lives and health.

I have also seen this personally. I spent over 10 years working in a very demanding environment, and I barely took days off or even a leave. I eventually realised the effect that lifestyle was having on my mental and physical health. That experience, alongside seeing women constantly self-sacrifice and later carry resentment from years of putting themselves last, made me start thinking about how I could contribute differently.

That is part of what inspired Bloom & Brunch. An avenue and a space where women can actually pause, reconnect, talk about the things they are experiencing and learn better ways to prioritise themselves, while having a good time.

Would you say that our culture of constant work and “hustle” has changed our understanding of rest, particularly in a place like Lagos where many people cannot easily step away from their responsibilities?

Oh, definitely. In a way, we have demonised rest. I mean, you hear people say things like, “If you sleep beyond 4/5 a.m., then you are unserious with your life,” and unfortunately, people have become slaves to these types of ideologies.

Speaking about Lagos, we can also see the weight that basic living expenses have put on people, so for some, it’s almost impossible to consider themselves deserving of rest when there is always another bill, responsibility or goal to meet. We have normalised being constantly busy to the point where slowing down can almost feel like failure.

I think that is why we need to start having more honest conversations around rest, and also intentionally curating spaces that allow us to do so. This is more about learning how to create healthier rhythms within the realities of the lives we are living.

What makes rest different from doing nothing? Can someone be physically inactive and still not be truly resting?

You have to be intentional about rest. It’s more mental, in my experience, than it is physical. I mean, you could be physically inactive but have a thousand tabs open in your head. That is not rest. It is in the intentional acts of boundaries, prioritisation, hobbies, etc.

It was something I realised in my last job, which was a high-stress one with tight deadlines, heavy work and intense emotional demands. I mentioned I had spent over 10 years working in demanding environments, so I know what it feels like to be physically present but mentally exhausted.

That is also why, with Bloom & Brunch, we want to create an environment where women can actually pause. We want them to talk, laugh, engage in sensory activities, dress up nice, enjoy good food, connect with other women and simply be present without feeling the need to be productive.

Why do you think rest has to be something people feel they need to justify, earn or even be productive about?

Because of how we have been socialised to think that slowing down is a bad thing, so we go about our lives thinking that taking a break is an abominable thing; meanwhile, an optimised life is one where balance exists.

I think women especially have been conditioned to constantly pour into other people, their work, their families and their responsibilities, while putting themselves last. So even when they finally have an opportunity to rest, there can be this feeling that they should be doing something more productive with that time.

For me, part of the conversation around the Art of Rest is helping women understand that they do not have to wait until they are completely exhausted before they give themselves permission to pause. Rest can be intentional, and it can exist alongside ambition, responsibility and everything else that matters to us.

What makes rest genuinely restorative?

Proper rest helps us recalibrate and moves our nervous system out of that fight-or-flight mode, allowing for better emotional regulation. Doctors have spoken about how it helps with cellular repair and immune system function. In my experience, my health became better when I started resting intentionally. From skin, physical health, to work output, I saw immense improvement.

Bloom & Brunch practically exists to reach more women and show them that intentional living is possible. For this edition, we are creating a curated experience themed ‘Arabian Luxe’ where women can come together, relate to each other’s experiences and hear from experts about the importance of self-prioritisation, rest and the best ways to practise it in the world we currently live in.

Beyond the conversation, we are also curating activities that allow women to engage their senses through wellness activities, laugh, play and reconnect with themselves.

If rest is an art, what are the skills involved in learning it, recognising when we need it, creating the space for it, and resisting the guilt that can come with it?

I think the first skill is self-awareness, being able to recognise when your body and mind are asking you to slow down. Then comes intentionality, setting boundaries, prioritising what truly matters and creating the space to rest without waiting until you are completely burnt out.

You also have to learn to detach your sense of worth from how much you are able to accomplish. Rest is not something you have to earn. It is part of living a balanced life, and learning to rest without guilt involves unlearning the idea that being constantly busy is the same as being productive.

Sometimes, it also means giving yourself permission to simply be. To laugh, enjoy yourself, reconnect with yourself and do things that have no other purpose than making you feel present and alive. I think that is an important part of the art of rest too.

Source: https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/04/chidera-okonji-on-why-women-need-to-be-intentional-about-rest/

posts.title: Pjanic reveals Juventus ‘tricked’ Cristiano Ronaldo into leaving crucial free kick
posts.excerpt: Miralem Pjanic revealed an extraordinary ‘trick’ Max Allegri played at Juventus to prevent Cristiano Ronaldo...
posts.content:
Miralem Pjanic revealed an extraordinary ‘trick’ Max Allegri played at Juventus to prevent Cristiano Ronaldo taking a decisive free kick. ‘It was the only way I could get the ball!’

The debate rages on in Portugal after Cristiano Ronaldo stormed out of their Nations League training camp in a row with coach Jorge Jesus, but keeping this ego in check has long been a problem for tacticians.

Some took slightly more subtle approaches to nudging him aside in order to make room for others, as revealed by former teammate Pjanic during the Festival dello Sport panel in Trento.

Pjanic and Allegri tricked Cristiano Ronaldo

TURIN, ITALY – AUGUST 07: Juventus players talk amongst themselves during the UEFA Champions League round of 16 second leg match between Juventus and Olympique Lyon at Allianz Stadium on August 07, 2020 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)“I do have an anecdote about this,” revealed Pjanic.

“We were playing at Napoli, I scored with a free kick, strangely with Cristiano Ronaldo in the team.”

When asked if CR7 was distracted and didn’t notice, the Bosnian confessed to some help from the touchline in the March 2019 match.

Juventus forward Cristiano Ronaldo (R) talks to Juventus goalkeeper Wojciech Szczesny prior to Rome shooting a penalty kick during the Italian Serie A football match AS Roma vs Juventus on January 12, 2020 at the Olympic stadium in Rome. (Photo by Tiziana FABI / AFP) (Photo by TIZIANA FABI/AFP via Getty Images)“Cristiano Ronaldo won the free kick, I think Meret got sent off for it. Max Allegri saw Cris on the ground touching his knee and immediately sent the physios on for treatment.

“This is because the free kick was so enticing, he got Cristiano off and let me take the free kick. And I scored from it! This was the only way I could get the ball, so thank you, Max!”

NAPLES, ITALY – MARCH 03: Miralem Pjanic of Juventus scores the 0-1 goal during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and Juventus at Stadio San Paolo on March 3, 2019 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images)The statistics show this is no idle boast from Pjanic, who was along with another teammate Paulo Dybala one of the most consistent players in Serie A from set plays.

On the other hand, Cristiano Ronaldo took 98 Serie A free kicks in the Juventus jersey, and he scored from just one.

Pjanic sul trucco di Allegri per non far calciare le punizioni a CR7

Della Valle – Morici

#gazzetta #ilfestivaldellosport https://t.co/StO4IaOn55

— La Gazzetta dello Sport (@Gazzetta_it) October 4, 2026

Ayari attracting Serie A interest

SOLNA, SWEDEN – SEPTEMBER 28: Yasin Ayari of Sweden celebrates after scoring 2-1 with teammate Sebastian Nanasi during the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Sweden and Poland at Strawberry Arena on September 28, 2026 in Solna, Sweden. He is seen as a potential heir to Luka Modric in the Milan midfield, with Ardon Jashari still struggling to make his mark.

MANCHESTER, ENGLAND – SEPTEMBER 16: Yasin Ayari of Brighton & Hove Albion looks on during the warm up before the Carabao Cup Third Round match between Manchester United and Brighton & Hove Albion at Old Trafford on September 16, 2026 in Manchester, England. posts.title: Spalletti: ‘Kenan Yildiz like Kvaratskhelia, Vlahovic causes his own trouble’
posts.excerpt: Luciano Spalletti compares Kenan Yildiz to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, ‘helped’ get the best out of Mohamed...
posts.content:
Luciano Spalletti compares Kenan Yildiz to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, ‘helped’ get the best out of Mohamed Salah, but identifies Dusan Vlahovic’s problem. ‘He causes his own trouble.’

The Juventus coach sat down for a lengthy interview with Tuttosport, and you can read some more of his comments here.

Spalletti has worked with so many talents in his career, including Kvaratskhelia before he became the Ballon d’Or contender at Paris Saint-Germain, or Salah at Roma on his way to becoming a Liverpool legend.

Spalletti record with top talent

TURIN, ITALY – FEBRUARY 22: Juventus FC head coach Luciano Spalletti looks on during the Serie A match between Juventus FC and Como 1907 at on February 21, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)“A coach must create a sense of ease, but what counts is getting the players together thinking the same way,” he told Tuttosport.

“We mustn’t just make a crude combination of individuals, but to pull something extra out of each of them. I feel like some of the players I made a real impact on were David Pizarro at Udinese, Stanislav Lobotka and Kvara at Napoli, Salah at Roma, and Joao Cancelo at Inter.

NAPLES, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 13: Stanislav Lobotka of SSC Napoli celebrates after scoring his side first goal during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and Bologna FC at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on September 13, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images)“Kvaratskhelia was coming from a different style of football and we helped him adapt. Salah, I should be clear, hands a Ballon d’Or to anyone who has the good fortune to coach him.

“I was convinced that Pizarro would have far more impact playing in front of the defence than his usual role as a trequartista, because you get 300 per cent more touches there. He could create spaces in a crowd and this is how David got to show his talent.

“When I arrived at Napoli, Lobotka had been practically forgotten, and I think he too had forgotten how good he was. Sometimes you just need to reassure a player that you have chosen him, to give him that confidence.”

NAPLES, ITALY – MARCH 03: Khvicha Kvaratskhelia of SSC Napoli celebrates scoring his team’s first goal during the Serie A TIM match between SSC Napoli and Juventus at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on March 03, 2024 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images)Now the player under Spalletti’s guidance at Juventus who needs to be nurtured is Kenan Yildiz, even if the Turkiye international is currently out injured following knee surgery.

“Yildiz puts the chrome on top of football, he makes it shine,” continued the coach.

“His every move is ingenious and breaks the system, so when he starts, even he doesn’t necessarily have a plan of what he’ll do next. Sometimes in training I see the defender predict his movement, and still can’t stop him. He has the madness of invention.”

PERTH, AUSTRALIA – AUGUST 11: Kenan Yildiz of Juventus controls the ball during the match between Juventus and Palermo at HBF Park on August 11, 2026 in Perth, Australia. (Photo by Janelle St Pierre/Getty Images)When it comes to players Spalletti has worked with before, Yildiz earns only the highest praise.

“For me, he is comparable to Kvaratskhelia. He needs to play a bit more, but I see similarities in the unpredictability, the way he stays outside of the rules and timing you expect in football. He’s a lovely guy, the boy next door type, but also a leader, one that doesn’t need to talk much.”

With all these players Spalletti was able to influence and develop, who does he feel regret that he didn’t fully understand?

“Adam Ounas at Napoli, without a doubt. As for Vlahovic, he still needs to find that personal balance within himself, because he causes his own trouble. Giving it too much gas is just as bad as not giving enough. It’s a question of balance, finding the right emotional temperature.”

Source: https://football-italia.net/spalletti-kenan-yildiz-kvaratskhelia-vlahovic/

posts.title: Njie confession: ‘Crystal Palace tried to hijack move, but I wanted Fiorentina’
posts.excerpt: Alieu Njie confessed his move from Torino was hijacked by Crystal Palace over the summer,...
posts.content:
Alieu Njie confessed his move from Torino was hijacked by Crystal Palace over the summer, but ‘it was too late, I told them it’s Fiorentina or nothing.’

Currently on international duty with the Sweden Under-21 side, the winger has been in Italy since coming to the Torino youth academy in 2021.

When the time came to move on from the Granata, he had several big offers, including from the Premier League, but had his heart set on the Stadio Artemio Franchi.

Njie rejected Crystal Palace for Fiorentina

Alieu Njie joins Fiorentina from Torino (via https://www.acffiorentina.com)“It was a difficult decision, because I was ready to leave Italy, but then I realised that Fiorentina made a really good offer, so I couldn’t refuse,” Njie told Expressen in Sweden.

It proved to be in the balance right to the final moment before he signed on the dotted line on August 30.

“There were moments when the move to Crystal Palace really did seem to be on the verge of conclusion, but Torino always rejected their proposals.

“While I was on my way to Florence for the medical tests, Crystal Palace tried to intervene at the last moment to ruin that move. I was clear straight away, it was Fiorentina or nothing.

“They wanted one last attempt, but I had already made my decision, so it was too late. Fiorentina represented the best option for me, and I am truly happy.”

Crystal Palace weren’t the only club interested, as RB Salzburg also targeted him.

VERONA, ITALY – JANUARY 04: Alieu Eybi Njie of Torino celebrates scoring his team’s third goal during the Serie A match between Hellas Verona FC and Torino FC at Stadio Marcantonio Bentegodi on January 04, 2026 in Verona, Italy. (Photo by Alessandro Sabattini/Getty Images)Part of the decision was fuelled by the fact Njie had already worked with Viola coach Paolo Vanoli at Torino, and he was recalled to Florence after Fabio Grosso’s early season dismissal.

“This was one of the main reasons why I chose Fiorentina. The project proposed to me was exciting, a young team with enormous potential, but Vanoli’s presence counted for a lot too.

“This represents the ideal step for my growth process. Vanoli gave me my Serie A debut, he was the coach when I scored my first top flight goal with Torino. It’s a young squad, we’re all around 21 to 23 years old.”

FLORENCE, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 20: David de Gea goalkeeper of ACF Fiorentina reacts during the Serie A match between ACF Fiorentina and SSC Napoli at Stadio Artemio Franchi on September 20, 2026 in Florence, Italy. (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images)Everyone with the notable exception of veteran former Manchester United goalkeeper David De Gea.

“Exactly, he’s like a big brother who takes care of us,” smiled Njie.

The transfer to Fiorentina was a loan for €4m with obligation to buy for a further €12m, plus add-ons up to €4m and a 10 per cent cut of the future sale fee.

Source: https://football-italia.net/njie-crystal-palace-hijack-move-fiorentina/

posts.title: Bove reveals precious Calafiori advice for an Italian in London
posts.excerpt: Watford’s Edoardo Bove reveals he is neighbours with Arsenal defender Riccardo Calafiori, who gave him...
posts.content:
Watford’s Edoardo Bove reveals he is neighbours with Arsenal defender Riccardo Calafiori, who gave him some precious advice on living in London as an Italian.

The pair grew up together as part of the Roma youth academy, and remained good friends over many years, including on international duty with Italy at youth level.

Calafiori moved to England for Arsenal in the summer of 2024, and Bove followed to Watford in January after a cardiac implant made it impossible for him to continue his career in Serie A.

Bove boosted by Calafiori presence

Edoardo Bove (l) and Riccardo Calafiori (r) during their Roma youth team days (picture @richycala via Instagram story)“It’s incredible considering that London is an immense city, but destiny saw us become neighbours,” Bove told the crowd at the Festival dello Sport event in Trento.

“Having a friend so close and present in my life really helped me to settle in. I was always fond of London, but he gave me such a big hand in getting to know the city.”

LONDON, ENGLAND – AUGUST 21: Kai Havertz of Arsenal celebrates scoring his team’s first goal with teammate Riccardo Calafiori during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Arsenal FC and Coventry City at Emirates Stadium on August 21, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images)Did Calafiori give Bove any particular advice about navigating life in London?

“Yes, don’t eat Italian food!” laughed the Watford man.

“Apart from very few trusted places, it’s all fake!”

BURSA, TURKEY – SEPTEMBER 28: Riccardo Calafiori of Italy looks on as he sits on the bench before the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Türkiye and Italy at Atatürk Spor Kompleksi Matli Stadyumu on September 28, 2026 in Bursa, Turkey. (Photo by Ahmad Mora/Getty Images)Bove has made seven appearances so far this season in the Watford jersey between the Championship and the Carabao Cup.

Calafiori is fresh from winning the Premier League for Arsenal and is currently part of the senior Italy squad preparing for tomorrow’s Nations League match against Turkiye.
