posts.title: Christmas comes early for Ondo community as LG Electronics donates 21st solar-powered borehole
posts.excerpt: What began as a commitment to bring clean water closer to underserved communities has reached a significant milestone for LG Electronics with the commissioning of its 21st solar-powered borehole at Os
posts.content:
What began as a commitment to bring clean water closer to underserved communities

has reached a significant milestone for LG Electronics with the commissioning of its 21st solar-powered borehole at Osan Agba, Oke Oka Akoko, Ondo State.

In Oke Oka Akoko, however, the significance of the intervention is not simply in the number, rather it’s in what reliable access to water means in everyday life: less time spent searching for water, greater convenience for households, improved hygiene and a dependable resource that can serve the wider community.

The new facility extends LG Electronics’ community water initiative into another part of Nigeria, combining access to clean water with renewable energy infrastructure designed to operate independently of the national electricity grid. It also reflects the evolution of the company’s approach to corporate citizenship – from individual interventions to a growing footprint of sustainable community infrastructure built around identified local needs.

At the commissioning, the Akoko South West Local Government Chairman, Hon. Ayọ Ajana, said the intervention demonstrates the value of collaboration between the private sector and communities in addressing practical development needs. “Water is fundamental to the well-being of every community, and this is the kind of intervention whose impact people can feel every day. What LG Electronics has done in Oke Oka Akoko complements the work of

government and shows what responsible private-sector participation in community development can achieve. We welcome this investment, and our responsibility is to ensure that the community takes ownership of it and protects it for the generations that will come after us,” Ajana said.

Hon. Ologunbaba Ruben (Ṣóyọ), the Adedibu of Osan Àgbà Oka, described the facility as an intervention whose value would extend well beyond the commissioning ceremony. “For us, this is more than the commissioning of a borehole. It is about meeting a need that touches our people every day. Families will use this water, our children will benefit from it, and the entire community has a responsibility to preserve what has been provided. We appreciate LG Electronics for looking beyond the major cities and recognising that communities such as ours also matter,” he said.

Chief Darusa Adedibu, Olugbedere of Igbedere, Osan Àgbà Oka, said the project underscores the importance of bringing development closer to the people. “Development becomes meaningful when it reaches people where they live. Clean water touches health, hygiene, our homes and the general well-being of the community. We appreciate LG

Electronics for bringing this project here. Our responsibility now is to protect it and ensure that it continues to serve everyone,” Adedibu said.

Hon. Ajulo Tayo, Chairman of Udẹ̀ Osan Àgbà Oka, also emphasised the everyday relevance of the project and the need for collective stewardship. “There are projects people hear about, and there are projects they experience in their daily lives. Water belongs in the second category. This borehole will serve our people every day, and that makes it deeply relevant to this community. Our appreciation to LG Electronics must therefore be matched by our commitment to look after the facility and ensure that its benefits are shared responsibly,” Tayo said.

FROM ONE COMMUNITY TO TWENTY-ONE

The Oke-Oka Akoko commissioning represents the 21st solar-powered borehole delivered by LG Electronics across communities in Nigeria, following the company’s 20th installation in Nariya Rigasa, Kaduna State. The growing programme reflects a deliberate effort to use sustainable technology to address a basic human need while reducing dependence on grid electricity.

For Mr. Hyoung Sub Ji, Managing Director, LG Electronics Nigeria, represented by Mr. Choongbae Seok, General Manager, Media Entertainment Solutions, TV Department, LG Electronics, Nigeria, the milestone is significant because of the lives and communities represented by the number. “Twenty-one communities is an important milestone

for us, but the real story is not the number. It is the people behind those twenty-one communities and what reliable access to water can mean to their everyday lives. At LG, we believe innovation has its greatest value when people can feel its impact. Sometimes that is through the technology in their homes; at other times, it means applying technology

and our resources to a fundamental need such as clean water,” Seok said.

He added: “The solar-powered model is particularly important because sustainability has been considered from the outset. We are not interested in infrastructure that works only on commissioning day. The objective is to create something relevant, practical and capable of continuing to serve the community. Oke Oka Akoko is another important

chapter in that journey.”

By powering the facility with solar energy, LG brings together two dimensions of sustainable development: addressing a basic social need and using renewable energy to support long-term functionality. Just as importantly, the initiative places emphasis on community participation and stewardship, recognising that infrastructure delivers lasting value when the people it serves have a stake in sustaining it.

A borehole can be commissioned in a day. Its real value is measured in the years that follow. From its earlier interventions to Oke Oka Akoko, LG Electronics’ expanding clean-water footprint is turning individual CSR projects into a broader model of community investment where technology, sustainability and local participation meet.

For the people of Osan Agba, the measure is simpler: clean water is now closer to home.

ABOUT LG ELECTRONICS

LG Electronics is a global innovator in technology and consumer electronics, with a longstanding presence in Nigeria. Through its products, partnerships and community-focused initiatives, the company continues to pursue its commitment to improving everyday life while supporting more sustainable communities.

Christmas comes early for Ondo community as LG Electronics donates 21st solar-powered borehole

posts.title: 10 things to know about the viral Lagos Life game
posts.excerpt: Lagos Life game, a Nigerian-made browser game that turns everyday Lagos experiences into a virtual life simulation, has gone viral just days after its launch, attracting more than one million players
posts.content:
Lagos Life game, a Nigerian-made browser game that turns everyday Lagos experiences into a virtual life simulation, has gone viral just days after its launch, attracting more than one million players and sparking conversations across social media.

Called Lagos Life, the game allows users to create characters, find jobs, earn virtual naira, rent homes, socialise, visit familiar Lagos locations and compete with other players in a shared virtual city.

Here are 10 things to know about the game.

1. Lagos Life is basically “The Sims” set in Lagos

Lagos Life is a life-simulation game that takes the concept popularised by The Sims and places it in a Nigerian setting.

Instead of living in a fictional suburb, players navigate a virtual Lagos where they can work, earn money, pay rent, socialise, go out and build their virtual lives.

The developer says the game is inspired by different aspects of Nigerian life, including employment, finance, property, transportation, entertainment, relationships, government and social activities.

2. It was created by Nigerian developer Shalom Rayhamen

The game was created by Nigerian software developer Shalom Rayhamen, who operates under the name Eliy.

Rayhamen has said the idea was influenced by her experience playing The Sims 3 and wondering what the game would look like if it reflected the environment and culture she knew.

The viral Lagos Run danfo-driving game also helped inspire the project.

3. It launched on October 1, 2026

Lagos Life went live on October 1, Nigeria’s Independence Day, and its growth was almost immediate.

Techpoint Africa reported that the game’s dashboard showed more than 1.2 million total players and over 71,000 people online by October 5, alongside more than 9.6 million all-time visits.

The developer had also reported a peak of more than 109,000 players online at once.

The figures come primarily from the game’s own dashboard, so they have not been independently audited.

4. You don’t need to download an app

One of Lagos Life’s biggest advantages is its accessibility.

It is played directly through a web browser, meaning users do not need to download a large game or install an application before playing.

The game can be accessed from phones and computers, making it considerably easier for people to try compared with games that require consoles, gaming PCs or large mobile downloads.

5. Players have to make a living

The game isn’t simply about walking around a virtual Lagos.

Players have to manage their virtual lives by working jobs, earning money, spending money and paying rent.

There are multiple career paths, with jobs ranging from banking and technology to entertainment and other professions. Players can progress through different levels of their careers as they develop their characters.

In other words, the game turns familiar Lagos struggles — getting a job, making money and paying the landlord — into gameplay.

6. The game has recognisable Lagos locations

Lagos Life deliberately uses locations and experiences that Nigerians can recognise.

Players can visit places including Amala Shitta and Quilox, while other aspects of the game draw from Lagos transport, nightlife, food and popular culture.

That local detail is an important part of its appeal because the game isn’t simply a generic life simulator with Nigerian names added to it. Its gameplay is built around experiences that are familiar to its target audience.

7. The virtual money is not real money

One of the biggest misconceptions surrounding Lagos Life is that players can make money they can eventually withdraw.

They cannot.

The game’s terms state that its in-game naira, properties, items and jobs have no real-world value and cannot be cashed out or transferred outside the game.

Players can purchase in-game naira using real money, but the virtual currency itself cannot be withdrawn as cash.

So, despite the game’s focus on jobs and money, it should not be treated as an investment or money-making platform.

8. Businesses can advertise inside the virtual Lagos

Lagos Life is not relying entirely on players to generate revenue.

The developer has created a form of virtual real estate where businesses can pay to advertise inside the game.

According to Techpoint Africa, companies can rent virtual billboards and plots in the game, with some businesses already using the space to promote their brands.

This means Lagos Life is effectively turning its virtual city into an advertising platform as its audience grows.

9. It is designed for adults

Despite its cartoon-like appearance, Lagos Life is officially an 18+ game.

Its terms of service state that users must be at least 18 years old to create an account.

The requirement is particularly relevant because the game involves interaction between real players, including chat and social activities. The developer’s rules prohibit harassment, threats, hate speech, sexual content, scams and the sharing of private information.

10. Its success could be bigger than just a viral game

Perhaps the most interesting thing about Lagos Life is what its sudden popularity says about Nigerian digital entertainment.

The game has demonstrated how quickly a locally relevant product can attract an audience when it combines familiar culture, humour, accessibility and social interaction.

Its rise also follows the viral success of Lagos Run, another Nigerian browser game in which players drive a yellow danfo through Lagos traffic. That game was released only days before Lagos Life and helped trigger a wave of interest in Nigerian-themed browser games.

Source: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/10-things-to-know-about-the-viral-lagos-life-game/

posts.content:
Novak Djokovic won the China Open on Tuesday after his opponent Alex de Minaur retired from the final, extending an astonishing unbeaten streak in Beijing and winning the 102nd title of his career.

The 39-year-old Serbian won the first set in the tie-break 7-6 (7/3) and was down a game in the second set when the Australian ended the match early.

“I always want to visualise myself with the trophy, particularly here in Beijing,” Djokovic said during the trophy ceremony.

“But I was also quite aware that reality is a little bit different these days,” he said, adding that it had been a challenging year with “physical and health issues”.

“I was just trying to find the good feeling on the court,” he said.

The first set was a physical battle that lasted more than one hour, and both men needed medical timeouts before the second.

De Minaur, the world number nine, won the first game of the second set before retiring.

It was not immediately clear why de Minaur left the match, but he walked back onto the court after his medical timeout with a white wrap around his left thigh.

“I don’t feel great,” de Minaur told the crowd afterwards.

“I want to say sorry to the amazing fans that came to watch… I didn’t want to finish like this,” the 27-year-old added.

De Minaur advanced to the final after his opponent Hubert Hurkacz retired injured from their semi-final on Monday, while Djokovic moved through when Daniil Medvedev was disqualified for hitting a fan with a ball.

With the win, Djokovic extended a perfect record to 34 wins in as many matches for his seventh title in the Chinese capital — his first since 2015.

He put on a valiant show to lift the trophy, ousting top seed Alexander Zverev in the quarter-final and coming back to defeat home hopeful Bu Yunchaokete in a demanding three sets.

Djokovic, a 24-time Grand Slam champion, will finish the season with a title for the 21st consecutive year.

– ‘Really grateful’ –

In the women’s draw, Karolina Muchova beat former world number one Naomi Osaka on her ninth match point to reach the quarter-finals, triumphant in a tense tie-break.

Muchova, the seventh seed, overcame 50 unforced errors across the two-hour-and-52-minute match to beat Osaka 7-5, 1-6, 7-6 (9/7).

Osaka, who represents Japan, saved eight match points but could not get past Muchova’s match-winning volley.

“I was shaking. I’m happy I made the last volley… Naomi could be standing here. It’s me, and I’m really grateful for it,” the 30-year-old Czech player told the crowd.

She next faces compatriot Nikola Bartunkova.

Earlier, Russia’s Mirra Andreeva beat Ukraine’s Daria Snigur 6-2, 6-2 to book her quarter-final spot against fellow Russian Ekaterina Alexandrova.

Alexandrova, ranked 28th, upset Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova 6-2, 6-2, ending the Czech player’s bid to return to the Beijing final that she reached last year.

AFP

posts.title: 2027: We need our full budget to ensure seamless polls, INEC cries out
posts.excerpt: "We expect the prompt release of the remaining budget to ensure seamless execution of the remaining activities," Amupitan said. The post 2027: We need our full budget to ensure seamless polls, INEC cr
posts.content:
…We’ve no candidates in Nigeria’s elections – EU

…Explains how it will use AI during election

…To deploy 1,414,768 ad hoc staff

By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja

The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has asked the Federal Government to promptly release the remaining part of its budget, saying it is needed to deliver the 2027 General Election seamlessly.

INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash O. Amupitan SAN, made the appeal on Tuesday at a World Press Conference and National Stakeholders’ Meeting in Abuja, held to mark 100 days to the first ballot.

“We expect the prompt release of the remaining budget to ensure seamless execution of the remaining activities,” Amupitan said.

He, however, acknowledged that “the Federal Government has maintained its commitment to democratic governance through the timely release of statutory budgetary allocations to the Commission.”

According to him, the funds have enabled INEC to “meet international vendor obligations, finance the production of critical election technology, upgrade physical infrastructure, and sustain multi-stakeholder operational deployments nationwide.”

‘EU has no candidate’

The Ambassador of the European Union EU to Nigeria and the Economic Community of West African States ECOWAS, Mr Gautier Mignot, backed the call, urging all actors “to facilitate as much as possible the work of INEC, not least from a budgetary point of view.”

“This is a Herculean task,” Mignot said.

He also made clear where the EU stands. “Ours is a friendly partnership, respectful of Nigerian sovereignty. We don’t impose any view or orientation. And needless to say, we don’t support specific candidates or parties,” he said.

Mignot said the EU would deploy an electoral mission of experts to follow the run-up to the election, the conduct of the ballot and its aftermath, and “come back in due time with recommendations.”

AI integration

On technology, Amupitan disclosed that INEC has set up a dedicated Artificial Intelligence AI Division within its Information and Communication Technology ICT Department.

He said, “Automated AI auditing tools are being integrated into our results verification process under a five-pillar AI Governance Framework, operating under mandatory human oversight. ” A governance policy, he added, “is being finalised by the Commission.”

The chairman said INEC is also integrating “AI-driven anomaly detection tools to monitor database traffic and shield our public portals against cyber intrusions or unauthorised alterations.”

Amupitan warned that generative AI, voice cloning and deepfake videos “now make it cheap to fabricate the voices of election officials, doctored result sheets and fake letterheads, and to spread them faster than they can be verified.”

He urged the media to set up fact-checking desks and verify with INEC before publishing. “In national elections, it is far more important to be right than to be first,” he said.

1.4m ad hoc staff

On manpower, the chairman said INEC will need 707,384 ad hoc personnel for the Presidential and National Assembly elections on January 16 and the same number for the Governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections on February 6.

“That is a total of 1,414,768 engagements across 176,846 polling units, compared with about 1.2 million in 2023,” he said.

The bulk of the workforce will again come from the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC).

Amupitan recalled that in 2023, “more than 70 per cent of our ad hoc staff, nearly 850,000 people, were corps members and student volunteers.” He said the INEC Portal for Recruitment of Election Staff opened on September 18 and closes at midnight on November 18.

The chairman said the National Register of Voters now stands at 103 million, following the registration of 10,772,421 new voters in three phases of the Continuous Voter Registration. The register will be displayed for public scrutiny from October 9 to 15, while distribution of Phase 1 Permanent Voter Cards PVCs to local government centres begins on Friday, October 9.

He added that 18 of the 22 registered political parties submitted candidates for the presidential election.

Amupitan disclosed that INEC received the certified true copy of the Supreme Court judgment in INEC v. Zenith Labour Party only on Tuesday morning and is reviewing it.

The Chairman of the House of Representatives Committee on Electoral Matters, Hon. Adebayo Balogun, said the committee had written INEC “to enforce the judgment of the Supreme Court on the Section 74 of the Electoral Act.”

“Just like the governors who decide or shy away from signing death warrants, which is their right and duty, INEC too is also mandated to take action where necessary,” Balogun said.

The Chairman of the Senate Committee on Electoral Matters, Sen. Simon Lalong, said “the credibility of an election is the responsibility” of political parties, candidates, security agencies, the media, civil society and voters.

Assistant Inspector-General of Police (AIG) Francis Idu of the Police Mobile Force, who represented the Inspector-General of Police, Mr Olatunji Disu, said clearance operations were ongoing in Kogi, Niger, Benue and Taraba states “to quell the various crisis points and ensure there is social harmony for the election.”

The National Chairman of the Inter-Party Advisory Council IPAC, Yusuf Mamman Dantalle, commended INEC over the Osun State governorship election but warned its officials “not to take sides with any political party or any candidate.”

He asked INEC to “engage more before election with the political parties” and told stakeholders, “This election will come and go, but Nigeria will remain.”

posts.title: Trump rallies New York crowd for Republican Bruce Blakeman's bid to replace Gov. Kathy Hochul
posts.excerpt: President Donald Trump rallied Syracuse supporters behind Bruce Blakeman's bid to unseat Gov. Kathy Hochul, promising tax cuts and cheaper energy for New York families.
posts.content:
President Donald Trump returned to his home state of New York on Friday night, showcasing America's "New Golden Age" and promising to help Republican gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman flip the Empire State red as the GOP makes its final push toward November's midterm elections.

Trump rallied supporters in Syracuse with a sweeping celebration of his administration's economic and immigration agenda, pledging to help New Yorkers secure lower taxes, cheaper energy and safer streets by electing Republicans up and down the ballot.

"We're in the Golden Age of America," Trump told the crowd, urging supporters to deliver the same enthusiasm that powered his presidential campaigns.

TRUMP CAMPAIGN INSIDER REVEALS STRATEGY BEHIND MIDTERM BLITZ THAT WHITE HOUSE HOPES PAYS OFF BIG

"Please pretend I'm on the freaking ballot," Trump urged. "And in a really, in a certain way, I am on the ballot because they can take away everything that we, that we got."

The president took Blakeman's challenge to Democrat Gov. Kathy Hochul as the centerpiece of the rally, promising direct support from Washington if elected.

"[Blakeman will] save this state. He'll turn the state around and I'll help him from the White House," Trump said. "I'll be helping him for governor."

Trump blasted Hochul over New York's taxes, utility bills and public safety, arguing that Blakeman could unleash the state's economic potential by embracing domestic energy production and cutting costs for families.

DEBRA MESSING SAYS COST OF LIVING, SUBWAY VIOLENCE PUSHED HER TO BACK TRUMP-ENDORSED REPUBLICAN

The president also hailed his administration's economic agenda as proof of what Trump described as a remarkable national turnaround.

He singled out Micron's planned $100 billion semiconductor complex in central New York, a project the company says is expected to generate 50,000 jobs across the state, including 9,000 directly with Micron.

"This will soon be the home to the largest semiconductor manufacturing facility ever built in the Western Hemisphere," Trump said.

Blakeman joined Trump onstage and echoed the president's message of a Republican resurgence, promising to cut taxes and utility bills, focus on public safety and make New York more attractive to both businesses and families.

"We have to create good jobs, good benefits to keep our young people here," Blakeman said. "We gotta look at business not as the enemy, but as a partner."

Trump also threw his support behind Republican congressional candidates Kailee Buller, who is challenging Democrat Rep. John Mannion in New York's 22nd District, and Anthony Constantino, who is running for the state's open 21st District seat, pledging to help Republicans compete for both seats.

The rally also notably featured a brief but memorable on-stage appearance by legendary former heavyweight boxing champion Mike Tyson, whom Trump invited up before the crowd.

"I'm just happy to be up here with my president, President Trump," Tyson said. "And, there's no way in the world I would ever be here if it wasn't for a president like Donald Trump. Thank you. Thank you very much."

Trump responded with a laugh, recalling Tyson's notorious reputation.

"I don't want to fight him," Trump joked, before complimenting the former champion. "You look good. Mike. What the h— are you doing?"

With Election Day approaching, the president returned to his core message that Republicans need Trump supporters to make a roaring showing at the ballot box.

"We're going to elect a Republican House and Republican Senate," Trump said.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/politics/trump-rallies-new-york-crowd-republican-bruce-blakemans-bid-replace-gov-kathy-hochul

posts.title: Gov Kathy Hochul signs New York onto Trump's school choice program despite teachers union opposition
posts.excerpt: New York Gov. Kathy Hochul joined President Donald Trump's Education Freedom Tax Credit despite fierce opposition from teachers unions and a petition to reject it.
posts.content:
New York Gov. Kathy Hochul on Friday signed on to join President Donald Trump’s school choice program despite opposition from teachers unions.

"Every parent wants their child to have a great education and the best possible chance to succeed. That’s what guides my decisions as governor," Hochul announced Friday.

"New York’s public schools are the backbone of communities across this state," she added. "That’s why I’ve made historic investments in public education, increasing school funding by more than $10 billion and fully funding Foundation Aid for the first time."

GOV HOCHUL'S PLAN TO OPT NEW YORK INTO FEDERAL SCHOOL CHOICE PROGRAM DRAWS UNION OPPOSITION

Despite Hochul's stated intention to participate, major labor groups and teachers unions remain staunchly opposed. A coalition of teachers unions and other public school advocates launched a petition demanding that Hochul reject the program.

"Gov. Hochul plans to opt New York in starting in 2027. But most New Yorkers haven’t even heard of this program or know how it will affect New York," the petition states. "Tax dollars would help pay private tuition for families who never used public schools."

Sydney Altfield, Scholarships for All founder and Teach Coalition CEO, told Fox News Digital, "This is a tremendous day for New Yorkers. Millions of children across our state will now have access to scholarships that can help pay for tutoring, after-school programs and other educational needs.

"Gov. Hochul has kept her promise to New York families, helping put money back into the pockets of hardworking parents while expanding educational opportunities for children across the state."

PRO-TRUMP GROUP LEADS NEW COALITION TO UNDERCUT TEACHERS UNIONS

Hochul’s announcement came after the Department of the Treasury and the IRS issued proposed regulations Oct. 1 to implement the Federal Scholarship Tax Credit (FSTC) program, paving the way for America's first nationwide school choice framework.

The initiative, also referred to as the Education Freedom Tax Credit, allows individual taxpayers to receive up to a $1,700 dollar-for-dollar federal tax credit for donations made to non-profit scholarship-granting organizations (SGOs). However, state governors must formally opt into the program for their residents and local educational organizations to participate and receive the funds.

The IRS recently reported that more than half of U.S. states have already signed up to participate. Burke noted that "competitive pressure" will ultimately force blue states to capture the influx of private donations.

Education Secretary Linda McMahon previously noted that some Democratic leaders have resisted the federal scholarship program simply because "it’s a Trump measure."

Democratic governors who have traditionally opposed school choice initiatives will face mounting competitive pressure to join Trump's program as states weigh whether to participate and Hochul moves to formally opt in, a top Department of Education official told Fox News Digital.

Kentucky has since formally joined the federal program after the state legislature overrode Gov. Andy Beshear's veto of opt-in legislation.

Unlike traditional voucher programs that draw directly from municipal or state public education funds, tax credit scholarships allow taxpayers to redirect a portion of their federal tax liability toward non-profit funding for student scholarships. The federal framework leaves the opt-in decision to state governors, enabling local families to access federally incentivized scholarship dollars.

"I’ve been clear from the start that New York would participate in the federal scholarship tax credit program if, and only if, all schools and students, including those in our public schools, could benefit," Hochul said.

"After a careful review of the federal regulations, we believe this program has the potential to bring millions of additional dollars to New York students and families without taking a single dollar from public schools or our state or local budgets.

"I’m not going to leave money on the table when it could help our kids," she added. "That’s why I have also been directly engaging with business leaders who have committed to use this program to support public school students and their academic needs.

"I look forward to working with education leaders across the state to make sure these resources reach students in every community. My commitment to public education has not changed, and it never will."

MORE THAN 400K NEW YORK CITY CHILDREN ENROLLED IN FAILING PUBLIC SCHOOLS: REPORT

For decades, school choice initiatives have remained a third-rail issue for many Democrats, who contend that choice models weaken public school systems and undermine labor unions.

However, growing parent demand for alternative education options — including charter schools, private schooling and homeschooling after the COVID-19 pandemic — has pushed several prominent Democrats to reevaluate their positions.

Trump's landmark school choice program comes as major blue city school districts struggle to retain students since the coronavirus pandemic.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/media/gov-kathy-hochul-signs-new-york-trump-school-choice-program-despite-teachers-union-opposition

posts.title: Lions head coach pays tribute to Mike Ditka after learning of his death from a press conference question
posts.excerpt: Dan Campbell shared an unforgettable pre-draft story about sitting alone with Mike Ditka in a room full of cigar smoke ahead of the 1999 NFL Draft.
posts.content:
Reactions are pouring in after news broke of the death of legendary NFL coach Mike Ditka, and one of the best came from Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell.

The Lions coach was in the midst of a news conference when a reporter asked if he had heard the news of Ditka's passing at the age of 86.

He hadn't, and that led to Campbell telling the story of his experience with Ditka ahead of the 1999 NFL Draft.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Campbell was a tight end out of Texas A&M heading into the draft, and like any prospect, he did some interviews with teams.

One of those teams was the New Orleans Saints, who were coached at the time by Ditka, who was also a tight end in his playing days.

"[Ditka] was someone I loved, man. Growing up, Ditka was it," Campbell said. "[I'm a] huge fan."

He said that the Saints, and specifically Ditka, wanted to meet with him.

While Campbell knew the legendary coach would be in the room, he thought others would be in there too.

Nope.

Just him, Ditka, and a room full of cigar smoke.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"It was one of the best times of my life and most intimidating times of my life sitting across from Mike Ditka," Campbell said. "It was awesome, man. Him asking questions about where you grew up, how you think, how you're wired, the game, what you see, it was awesome.

"Thoughts and prayers go out to his family. He's a legend."

What a classy tribute, and to pull that story out of his hat in the moment shows just how much the late coach meant to Campbell.

Of course, the Saints did not end up drafting Campbell. Instead, he was selected by the New York Giants in the third round, 79th overall.

posts.title: Abacha Family Joint Venture Dispute: Fundamental breaches supported by evidence – 18 Units partitioned into 44
posts.excerpt: The available contractual documents and recent court proceedings in the dispute over No. 68 Molade Okoya Thomas Street, Victoria Island, Lagos, appear to lend significant weight to the position of the
posts.content:
The available contractual documents and recent court proceedings in the dispute over No. 68 Molade Okoya Thomas Street, Victoria Island, Lagos, appear to lend significant weight to the position of the original property owner, Dr (Mrs) Maryam Sani Abacha, that the property was entrusted to Levitikal Realties & Construction Limited strictly for the development of 18 units of three-bedroom apartments and was never transferred to Levitikal as its unrestricted commercial asset.

Under the agreement, nine completed apartments were to accrue to Levitikal as consideration for undertaking the development, while the remaining nine were to be retained by the landowner. Upon completion of the project, Mrs Abacha would execute and sign Deeds of Assignment in favour of Levitikal or its nominees for the nine units due to the developer under the agreement. Since there is a dispute over the development, any purchaser may have to wait until the dispute is resolved before obtaining a Deed of Assignment.

The worrisome issue, therefore, is the developer’s attempt to convert a contractual development agreement into an arrangement that seeks to extend its rights to ownership or unrestricted control of the underlying land.

The controversy was heightened by the unilateral partitioning of the development into more than 44 units comprising one-bedroom, two-bedroom and three-bedroom apartments, rather than the original 18 agreed units. This raised fundamental questions about the contractual authority for the additional development, the ownership of the additional interests and the authority under which they may have been marketed or otherwise dealt with.

To prevent the Abacha family from discovering the development’s status, Levitikal allegedly used all means possible to prevent them from gaining access to the property despite several requests and demands.

The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) is already involved in the matter, as investigations are ongoing into the sale of the partitioned units to unsuspecting third parties. Previous publications circulated across several platforms reported that the EFCC had marked the property as part of its ongoing investigation.

Another dispute concerning the development relates to Levitikal’s attempt to register a Power of Attorney granted to it for the development and use the registration as a tool to take over the property. The dispute is currently before the High Court of Lagos State. The suit was instituted by Providus Bank Limited and Levitikal. The Abacha family, which was not initially joined as a party, subsequently became aware of the suit and was joined by an order of the High Court of Lagos State.

On September 29, 2026, Justice Ambrose Lewis-Allagoa of the Federal High Court in Lagos ordered the appointment of a receiver/manager to take possession, custody and control of the property. The court also restrained Levitikal, its directors, agents and representatives from selling, transferring, assigning, mortgaging, leasing, charging or otherwise encumbering the property. The order was made pending the resolution of the arbitration proceedings.

Although the order is interim and does not finally determine the substantive claims, it represents an important step towards preserving the disputed property pending the determination of the arbitration.

At the heart of the controversy is a relatively straightforward contractual question: Did the original agreement give Levitikal ownership of the land or merely the right to develop it under agreed terms?

If the original bargain was for an 18-unit development, with nine units constituting the developer’s consideration, any subsequent expansion of the project and creation of additional proprietary interests would require clear contractual justification.

For now, however, the available evidence appears to lend considerable weight to Mrs Abacha’s contention that she remained the owner of the underlying land and that Levitikal’s mandate was a defined development arrangement, not an unrestricted transfer of proprietary control.

The case consequently raises an important broader question for Nigeria’s real estate sector concerning the rights granted to developers under joint venture agreements. If any of the units has been sold, the purchaser should follow the proceedings closely, as the outcome could affect their interests in the property.

Abacha Family Joint Venture Dispute: Fundamental breaches supported by evidence – 18 Units partitioned into 44

posts.title: Apologise to Tinubu now – Reno Omokri tells Atiku
posts.excerpt: Nigerian ambassador-designate to Mexico, Reno Omokri, has asked the African Democratic Congress, ADC, presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, to apologise to President Bola Tinubu for addressing the P
posts.content:
Nigerian ambassador-designate to Mexico, Reno Omokri, has asked the African Democratic Congress, ADC, presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, to apologise to President Bola Tinubu for addressing the President by his first name.

In a post on his verified X handle, Omokri charged Atiku to address the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces with the respect due to his office.

He said such would show good judgment on Atiku’s part and demonstrate the temperament required of a good leader.

The former presidential aide lamented that repeatedly referring to the President as ‘Bola’ sets a poor precedent, stating that it is wrong and reflects poorly on Nigeria and Nigerians in the international community.

According to him, such an act portrays opposition politics in Nigeria as pedestrian.

He equally said Atiku’s action will divide Nigeria because he had never addressed former President Muhammadu Buhari whom he contested with as ‘Muhammadu’.

“You need to apologise to President Tinubu. I watched your press conference today and noticed that you repeatedly referred to the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces as ‘Bola’ rather than President Bola Tinubu.

“Even when you fell out with your boss, President Olusegun Obasanjo, you never referred to him as ‘Olusegun’. You always gave him the respect due to his office by calling him President Obasanjo, even when you criticised him.

“Yet this was a President who called you names I cannot even print here, and in December 2006 declared your office as Vice President vacant, then withdrew your rights and privileges, and even ordered you out of a Federal Executive Council meeting.

“President Tinubu has not done any of that. He was in your corner when you were being bullied and offered you a ticket on the Action Congress platform. Yet, you disrespect him and respect President Obasanjo,” Omokri wrote.

Apologise to Tinubu now – Reno Omokri tells Atiku

posts.title: Democrats see new chances to flip red states — but a $400M GOP spending advantage could derail their plans
posts.excerpt: Republicans outspend Democrats by $400 million ahead of Election Day, forcing Senate Majority PAC to make tough choices across nine battlegrounds.
posts.content:
With just over three weeks to go until Election Day, more and more red states and congressional districts appear in reach for the Democrats, as they work to win back House and Senate majorities from the Republicans in the midterms. But a massive Republican spending advantage threatens to complicate those ambitions.

Republican campaigns, committees and aligned groups have outspent their Democratic counterparts by $400 million so far this election cycle, according to AdImpact, a leading political advertising tracking firm.

The disparity is forcing Democrats to make difficult decisions about where to invest and how much to spend as the party tries to expand the electoral map.

"We are being outspent by the Republicans. That's just a fact," Lauren French, communications director at the Senate Majority PAC, told Fox News Digital. "In many of these states, they have really transactionalized elections, so they have monopoly money to play with, whereas we are working with real resources."

DEMOCRATS THINK A BLUE WAVE IS FORMER - HERE ARE THREE FACTORS THAT COULD STOP IT

The latest Fox News Power Rankings shifted GOP-dominated South Carolina from Solid to Likely Republican. The Senate showdown in reliably Republican Kansas is Lean Republican, while the races in red-leaning Alaska, Iowa, Ohio and Texas are rated toss-ups.

"Senate Majority PAC has resources to compete, and we are very happy that we're able to be in 9 battleground states," French said.

The super PAC is the leading outside group supporting Democratic Senate candidates and incumbents and is aligned with longtime Democratic leader Sen. Chuck Schumer.

French highlighted record-setting fundraising over the past three months, but added, "of course, more recess resources would be helpful."

With the latest polls from Fox News and other organizations showing Democrats increasingly competitive across the Senate map, the party is pleading for more money.

"Last month a pro-Trump PAC reserved $10 million in New Hampshire advertising, and we’re being outspent 3-to-1," reads a fundraising pitch to supporters by Rep. Chris Pappas, the Democratic Senate nominee in swing state New Hampshire.

WHO'S UP AND WHO'S DOWN IN THE LATEST FOX NEWS MIDTERM POWER RANKINGS

Senate Majority PAC is rushing some of its record fundraising into the newly competitive battlegrounds. And American Bridge PAC, a Democrat-aligned group, recently pumped over $20 million into South Carolina and Kansas, as well as competitive races in two other red states, Florida and Mississippi.

But the Democratic groups are being outspent by their Republican-aligned counterparts, thanks to major expenditures by Senate Leadership Fund, the President Donald Trump-allied MAGA Inc. and a super PAC bankrolled by Elon Musk.

"The hard reality is there isn't enough funding to protect the toss-up states and also heavily invest in the red-leaning states where we're playing offense," a veteran Democratic Senate operative who requested anonymity to speak candidly told Fox News Digital."

French told Fox News Digital "This is the time in the campaign season where everyone really has to make some of those belt-tightening decisions, and that's why we're looking at every race really closely to make sure we have enough resources to get to the majority, but we're also not leaving anyone shortchanged."

House Democrats are facing a similar predicament.

A memo from the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee (DCCC) shared with donors warned that Republicans "are now flooding districts across our battlefield with MAGA Inc. and Trump super PAC money that we simply cannot match."

DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB

The memo, which was obtained by Fox News Digital, requested an additional $17 million that was needed by Oct. 22 "to close the sale" in what they described as "winnable races."

The GOP is fighting political history, which has traditionally seen the party in power in Washington lose congressional seats during midterm election years. Add to that a challenging political climate fueled by persistent inflation Americans see at the grocery store, high gas prices tied to what polls show is an unpopular war with Iran and Trump's negative approval ratings.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

But the Republicans' financial advantage has allowed GOP campaigns and allied groups to spend more on political advertising nationally.

"Thanks to the tireless efforts of Leader John Thune, Senate Leadership Fund has amassed a financial advantage that neither party has had before. SLF will continue to invest unprecedented resources across the map to maintain the Republican Senate majority," Senate Leadership Fund communications director Chris Gustafson told Fox News Digital.

Veteran GOP strategist Jesse Hunt told Fox News Digital that "Republican outside groups will have played a decisive role in positive Republican performance if they have a good election night despite what is strong headwinds working against them."

"This is not an advantage Republicans typically have and it's definitely a contributing factor to a lot of candidates on the ballot right now keeping their races close," Hunt emphasized.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/politics/democrats-widening-path-power-400m-gop-advantage-brutal-dilemma

posts.title: SC Dem Senate candidate claims she will stand up to her party as Graham ties her to 'socialist Democrats'
posts.excerpt: Democratic South Carolina U.S. Senate candidate Annie Andrews and Republican Sen. Darline Graham clashed during a U.S. Senate election debate.
posts.content:
Sen. Darline Graham, R-S.C., and Democratic challenger Annie Andrews clashed on Sunday night during the South Carolina U.S. Senate debate, which also included Libertarian candidate Kasie Whitener.

Graham said she is "concerned about the socialist Democrats," asserting that after Hamas terrorists slaughtered Israelis on Oct. 7, 2023, Democrats in New York cheered "over the death of over a thousand people."

"Annie Andrews will not stand up to the socialist Democratic Party. She's only going to join them," Graham declared.

DARLINE GRAHAM'S 'EMBARRASSING AND INEXCUSABLE' NATIONAL SECURITY STUMBLE SPOTLIGHTS BREAK FROM LATE BROTHER

Andrews fired back, claiming that she is willing to stand up to her party.

"I told you my opponent was going to call me a socialist and there she's done it again. She's been told to come out here and call me Bernie, Ocasio, Mamdani. That's what's in her script," Andrews said, referring to Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

"But the truth is my name is Annie Andrews. And there shouldn't be any confusion about that because unlike my opponent, I haven't changed my name recently," she said.

DEMOCRATS ARE CHANGING THEIR TRANSGENDER MESSAGE. REPUBLICANS SAY THEY'RE JUST FLIP-FLOPPING

"The real difference between me and Sen. Graham is that I will stand up to my own party and I will always put South Carolina first. She seems to believe the job she has right now is to be the White House's ambassador to South Carolina. The job is to represent South Carolina. She considers the job to be to read their scripts and do their bidding. And we can do better," Andrews asserted.

Graham fired back, saying that her "legal name is Graham" and "has always been Graham." She explained, "I lost my parents when I was a little girl, and I kept the name Graham so that I felt connected to them. So my name, every document I have ever signed, has Graham on it."

After the death of Sen. Lindsey Graham, South Carolina Gov. Henry McMaster tapped the late lawmaker's sister Darline to serve the remainder of her brother's Senate term.

DEM SCRAMBLES TO CHANGE TUNE ON TRANS ATHLETES AS TRUMP TARGETS PAST RECORD: 'ANNIE TRANNIE'

President Donald Trump is backing Sen. Darline Graham for election to a full six-year Senate term.

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/politics/sc-dem-senate-candidate-claims-stand-party-graham-ties-socialist-democrats

artists.name: Burna Boy
artists.bio: Damini Ebunoluwa Ogulu, known professionally as Burna Boy, is a Nigerian singer, songwriter, and record producer. He gained recognition in 2012 after releasing "Like to Party", the lead single from his debut studio album L.I.F.E (2013). In 2017, Burna Boy signed a record deal with Atlantic Records and its parent company Warner Music Group. His third studio album Outside, which became his major label debut, was released in 2018.

artists.name: Davido
artists.bio: David Adedeji Adeleke, known professionally as Davido, is a Nigerian-American singer, songwriter, and record producer. Davido was born in Atlanta, U.S, and raised in Lagos, Nigeria. He made his music debut as a member of the group KB International. Davido studied business administration at Oakwood University before dropping out to make beats and record vocal references. He rose to fame after releasing "Dami Duro", the second single from his debut studio album Omo Baba Olowo (2012), from which six additional singles—"Back When", "Ekuro", "Overseas", "All of You", "Gbon Gbon" and "Feel Alright"—were taken. In 2012, Davido won the Next Rated award at The Headies. Between 2013 and 2015, he released the singles "Gobe", "One of a Kind", "Skelewu", "Aye", "Tchelete (Goodlife)", "Naughty", "Owo Ni Koko", "The Sound" and "The Money".

artists.name: YoungBoy Never Broke Again
artists.bio: Kentrell DeSean Gaulden, known professionally as YoungBoy Never Broke Again or NBA YoungBoy, is an American rapper, singer, and songwriter. Gaulden released eight mixtapes from 2015 to 2017, and garnered a regional following for his work. He signed with Atlantic Records and Artist Partner Group in the latter year to release the singles "Untouchable" and "No Smoke", both of which marked his first entries on the Billboard Hot 100. Released in January 2018, his single "Outside Today" became his first to peak within the chart's top 40, and received quadruple platinum certification by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA). It served as both his mainstream breakthrough and the lead single for his debut studio album, Until Death Call My Name (2018), which peaked at number seven on the US Billboard 200 despite mixed critical reception.

artists.name: Frank Edwards (gospel musician)
artists.bio: Frank Ugochukwu Edwards is a Nigerian musician, record producer, sound engineer, worship singer and songwriter from Enugu State. He is the founder and owner of the record label Rocktown Records, which is home to recording artists such as Edwards himself, Gil Joe, King BAS, Nkay, Dudu and, among others. He lives in Lagos, Nigeria.

artists.name: Wizkid
artists.bio: Ayodeji Ibrahim Balogun, known professionally as Wizkid, is a Nigerian singer and songwriter. Born in the Ojuelegba suburb of Surulere, Lagos, Wizkid is a voice in the emerging Afrobeats movement. His music is a blend of Afrobeats, afropop, R&B, afrobeat, reggae, dancehall, and pop. He began recording music at the age of 11 and released a collaborative album with the Glorious Five, a group he and a few of his church friends formed. In 2009, Wizkid signed a record deal with Banky W's Empire Mates Entertainment (E.M.E). He gained recognition after releasing "Holla at Your Boy", the lead single from his debut studio album, Superstar (2011), which also spawned the singles "Tease Me/Bad Guys" and "Don't Dull".

artists.name: Michael Jackson
artists.bio: Michael Joseph Jackson was an American singer, songwriter, dancer, and philanthropist. Dubbed the "King of Pop", he is widely regarded as one of the most culturally significant figures of the 20th century. His musical achievements broke American racial barriers and made him a dominant figure worldwide. Through his songs, music videos, concerts, and fashion, he transformed visual performance in popular music, popularizing street dance moves such as the moonwalk, the robot, and the anti-gravity lean. Jackson is often deemed the greatest entertainer of all time.

artists.name: Asake
artists.bio: Ahmed Ololade, known professionally as Asake, is a Nigerian singer, rapper, and songwriter. His debut album, Mr. Money with the Vibe (2022) broke the record for the biggest opening day for an African album on Apple Music at the time and debuted at number 66 on the Billboard 200 chart. His second album Work of Art (2023), matched the chart position of its predecessor. Asake's third album Lungu Boy (2024) became his third consecutive number one album in Nigeria and the longest-running number one in Nigeria chart history.

artists.name: Fela Kuti
artists.bio: Fela Aníkúlápó Kútì was a Nigerian musician and political activist. He is regarded as the principal innovator of Afrobeat, a Nigerian music genre that combines West African music with American funk and jazz. At the height of his popularity, he was referred to as one of Africa's most "challenging and charismatic music performers". AllMusic described him as "a musical and sociopolitical voice" of international significance.

artists.name: Seyi Vibez
artists.bio: Balogun Afolabi Oluwaloseyi known professionally as Seyi Vibez, is a Nigerian singer and songwriter. He is known for his breakthrough single "Chance " from his second studio album Billion Dollar Baby which debuted at No. 19 on the UK Afrobeats singles chart and peaked number 7 on the TurnTable Top 100 chart.

artists.name: Central Cee
artists.bio: Oakley Neil Caesar-Su, known professionally as Central Cee, is a British rapper from Shepherd's Bush, London. Regarded as a leading figure in UK rap, he rose to prominence in 2020 with the release of his drill singles "Day in the Life" and "Loading". His first mixtape, Wild West (2021), debuted at number two on the UK Albums Chart, while his second, 23 (2022), debuted atop the chart.

artists.name: Lil Durk
artists.bio: Durk Devontay Banks, known professionally as Lil Durk, is an American rapper. Regarded as a pioneer of the Chicago-based hip-hop subgenre drill music, he is often considered the subgenre's most commercially successful rapper. He initially garnered local success with the release of his Signed to the Streets mixtape series (2013–2014), which led to him to sign with Def Jam Recordings. The label released his debut studio album, Remember My Name (2015), and its follow-up, Lil Durk 2X (2016), to moderate commercial reception before parting ways with the rapper in 2018.

artists.name: Drake (musician)
artists.bio: Aubrey Drake Graham is a Canadian rapper and singer. He is credited with popularizing R&B sensibilities in hip-hop music through rap-singing. Drake first gained recognition as Jimmy Brooks in the CTV teen drama series Degrassi: The Next Generation (2001–2008) and began his music career by independently releasing the mixtapes Room for Improvement (2006), Comeback Season (2007), and So Far Gone (2009), before signing with Young Money Entertainment.

artists.name: Eminem
artists.bio: Marshall Bruce Mathers III, known professionally as Eminem, is an American rapper, songwriter, record producer, and record executive. Known for his rap flow and conscious rap, which includes political criticism and social commentary, he is widely regarded as one of the greatest and most influential rappers of all time, often credited with popularizing hip-hop in Middle America and the acceptance of white rappers. While much of his transgressive art during the late 1990s and early 2000s made him a controversial figure, Eminem has become a representation of popular angst in lower-income America.

artists.name: Lil Baby
artists.bio: Dominique Armani Jones, known professionally as Lil Baby, is an American rapper, singer, and songwriter. He rose to prominence following the release of his 2017 mixtapes Harder than Hard and Too Hard — the former of which spawned his first Billboard Hot 100 entry with its lead single, "My Dawg." He signed with Quality Control Music, an imprint of Motown and Capitol Records to release his debut studio album Harder Than Ever (2018), which peaked at number three on the Billboard 200 and was supported by the Billboard Hot 100-top ten single "Yes Indeed". Later that year, he released the collaborative mixtape Drip Harder with fellow Georgia-based rapper Gunna, and his solo mixtape Street Gossip; the former spawned his second top-ten single "Drip Too Hard", while the latter peaked at number two on the Billboard 200.

artists.name: Chioma Jesus
artists.bio: Amaka Okwuoha, known professionally as Chioma Jesus, is a Nigerian gospel singer, songwriter, and worship leader. She rose to prominence with the release of her 2003 song "Chioma," from which her stage name is derived. She is recognized for her contributions to the popularization of indigenous gospel music, particularly songs performed in the Igbo language.

artists.name: Sparqlyn
artists.bio: Ahmmed Kanneh Larweh, popularly known as Sparqlyn, is a Ghanaian Afrobeats musician and songwriter. He was a member of the defunct hiplife group, Dunsin. In January 2023, he was enstooled as the Development Chief at Krobo Odumase in the Eastern Region of Ghana.

artists.name: Theophilus Sunday
artists.bio: Theophilus Sunday is a Nigerian gospel minister, singer, and songwriter.

artists.name: Olamide
artists.bio: Olamide is a Nigerian rapper and singer known professionally as Olamide. He is associated with Nigerian hip-hop and Afrobeats.

artists.name: DeeYasso
artists.bio: Dennis Hope Yasso, professionally known as DeeYasso is a Nigerian record producer, mixing & mastering engineer, multi-Instrumentalist, songwriter and a lawyer. He made his mainstream debut when he produced Yemi Alade's song titled "Tomorrow" which received a nomination at the 67th Annual Grammy Awards for Best African Music Performance

artists.name: Chella (singer)
artists.bio: Uzochukwu Michael Ikechukwu, known professionally as Chella, is a Nigerian singer-songwriter. He gained recognition in 2024 with the release of his single, "Nyash Na Nyash". He followed up with "My Darling", which peaked at number 1 on the Shazam Global chart and became the fourth Nigerian song in history to top the chart. It also peaked at number 1 on the official Nigeria TurnTable Top 100 songs, and at number 8 on the Billboard U.S. Afrobeats Songs chart.

artists.name: Speed Darlington
artists.bio: Darlington Okoye popularly known as Speed Darlington, is a Nigerian rapper. He was born in Bronx, New York, USA, to musicians Pericoma Okoye and Queen Achakpo. Darlington was raised in the Bronx, New York, and began his journey in the arts as a dancer in the 1990s. His shift to music came in 2017 with the release of his single "Bangdadadang!" His style blends Afrobeat, pop, and rap. Over the years, he has released several other tracks, including "Akamu," "Cash & Carry," "Ogiriga Owuwa" and "Baby Oil".

artists.name: Portable (musician)
artists.bio: Habeeb Okikiola Badmus, popularly known as Portable, is a Nigerian singer, songwriter and rapper. He is known for controversies and online buzz.

artists.name: Chike
artists.bio: Chike is a Nigerian singer and songwriter known for soulful Afrobeats and R&B-influenced music. He gained wider recognition after appearing on Nigerian Idol.

artists.name: Coolio
artists.bio: Coolio was the stage name of Artis Leon Ivey Jr., an American rapper, songwriter and record producer. He was best known for "Gangsta's Paradise" (1995), which won a Grammy Award, and also released singles including "Fantastic Voyage" (1994) and "C U When U Get There" (1997).

artists.name: 50 Cent
artists.bio: Curtis James Jackson III, known professionally as 50 Cent, is an American rapper, actor, television producer, record executive, and businessman. Born in Queens, a borough of New York City, Jackson began pursuing a musical career in 1996. In 1999–2000, he recorded his debut album, Power of the Dollar, for Columbia Records. During a shooting in May 2000, he was struck by nine bullets, causing its release to be canceled and Jackson to be dropped from the label. His 2002 mixtape Guess Who's Back? was discovered by Detroit rapper Eminem, who signed Jackson to his label Shady Records that year.
